metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
units.rightText: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

units.leftText: Now the earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters. The First Day
units.rightText: And the earth was waste and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep: and the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.

units.leftText: And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
units.rightText: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
leftNotes: 1:3 Cited in 2 Corinthians 4:6|2CO 4:6*

units.leftText: And God saw that the light was good, and He separated the light from the darkness.
units.rightText: And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.

units.leftText: God called the light “day,” and the darkness He called “night.” And there was evening, and there was morning — the first day. The Second Day
units.rightText: And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And there was evening and there was morning, one day.
leftNotes: 1:5 Literally day one

units.leftText: And God said, “Let there be an expanse between the waters, to separate the waters from the waters.”
units.rightText: And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.
leftNotes: 1:6 Or a canopy or a firmament or a vault; also in verses 7, 8, 14, 15, 17, and 20

units.leftText: So God made the expanse and separated the waters beneath it from the waters above. And it was so.
units.rightText: And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.

units.leftText: God called the expanse “sky.” And there was evening, and there was morning — the second day. The Third Day
units.rightText: And God called the firmament Heaven. And there was evening and there was morning, a second day.

units.leftText: And God said, “Let the waters under the sky be gathered into one place, so that the dry land may appear.” And it was so.
units.rightText: And God said, Let the waters under the heavens be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.

units.leftText: God called the dry land “earth,” and the gathering of waters He called “seas.” And God saw that it was good.
units.rightText: And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.

units.leftText: Then God said, “Let the earth bring forth vegetation: seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each bearing fruit with seed according to its kind.” And it was so.
units.rightText: And God said, Let the earth put forth grass, herbs yielding seed, and fruit-trees bearing fruit after their kind, wherein is the seed thereof, upon the earth: and it was so.

units.leftText: The earth produced vegetation: seed-bearing plants according to their kinds and trees bearing fruit with seed according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.
units.rightText: And the earth brought forth grass, herbs yielding seed after their kind, and trees bearing fruit, wherein is the seed thereof, after their kind: and God saw that it was good.

units.leftText: And there was evening, and there was morning — the third day. The Fourth Day
units.rightText: And there was evening and there was morning, a third day.

units.leftText: And God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to distinguish between the day and the night, and let them be signs to mark the seasons and days and years.
units.rightText: And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years:

units.leftText: And let them serve as lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth.” And it was so.
units.rightText: and let them be for lights in the firmament of heaven to give light upon the earth: and it was so.

units.leftText: God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night. And He made the stars as well.
units.rightText: And God made the two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.

units.leftText: God set these lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth,
units.rightText: And God set them in the firmament of heaven to give light upon the earth,

units.leftText: to preside over the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
units.rightText: and to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and God saw that it was good.

units.leftText: And there was evening, and there was morning — the fourth day. The Fifth Day
units.rightText: And there was evening and there was morning, a fourth day.

units.leftText: And God said, “Let the waters teem with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky.”
units.rightText: And God said, Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.

units.leftText: So God created the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves, with which the waters teemed according to their kinds, and every winged bird after its kind. And God saw that it was good.
units.rightText: And God created the great sea-monsters, and every living creature that moveth, wherewith the waters swarmed, after their kind, and every winged bird after its kind: and God saw that it was good.

units.leftText: Then God blessed them and said, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters of the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.”
units.rightText: And God blessed them, saying, Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.

units.leftText: And there was evening, and there was morning — the fifth day. The Sixth Day
units.rightText: And there was evening and there was morning, a fifth day.

units.leftText: And God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, land crawlers, and beasts of the earth according to their kinds.” And it was so.
units.rightText: And God said, Let the earth bring forth living creatures after their kind, cattle, and creeping things, and beasts of the earth after their kind: and it was so.

units.leftText: God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and everything that crawls upon the earth according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
units.rightText: And God made the beasts of the earth after their kind, and the cattle after their kind, and everything that creepeth upon the ground after its kind: and God saw that it was good.

units.leftText: Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness, to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air, over the livestock, and over all the earth itself and every creature that crawls upon it.”
units.rightText: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the heavens, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
leftNotes: 1:26 MT; Syriac and over all the beasts of the earth

units.leftText: So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.
units.rightText: And God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
leftNotes: 1:27 Cited in Matthew 19:4|MAT 19:4* and Mark 10:6

units.leftText: God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth.”
units.rightText: And God blessed them: and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it; and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the heavens, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.

units.leftText: Then God said, “Behold, I have given you every seed-bearing plant on the face of all the earth, and every tree whose fruit contains seed. They will be yours for food.
units.rightText: And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for food:

units.leftText: And to every beast of the earth and every bird of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth — everything that has the breath of life in it — I have given every green plant for food.” And it was so.
units.rightText: and to every beast of the earth, and to every bird of the heavens, and to everything that creepeth upon the earth, wherein there is life, I have given every green herb for food: and it was so.

units.leftText: And God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning — the sixth day.
units.rightText: And God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.

units.leftText: Thus the heavens and the earth were completed in all their vast array.
units.rightText: And the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.

units.leftText: And by the seventh day God had finished the work He had been doing; so on that day He rested from all His work.
units.rightText: And on the seventh day God finished his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.
leftNotes: 2:2 Cited in Hebrews 4:4|HEB 4:4*

units.leftText: Then God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on that day He rested from all the work of creation that He had accomplished. Man and Woman in the Garden
units.rightText: And God blessed the seventh day, and hallowed it; because that in it he rested from all his work which God had created and made.

units.leftText: This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made them.
units.rightText: These are the generations of the heavens and of the earth when they were created, in the day that Jehovah God made earth and heaven.
leftNotes: 2:4 LORD or GOD, with capital letters, represents the proper name of the God of Israel and the one true God, transliterated from the Hebrew as YHWH; here and throughout the Scriptures.

units.leftText: Now no shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, nor had any plant of the field sprouted, for the LORD God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground.
units.rightText: And no plant of the field was yet in the earth, and no herb of the field had yet sprung up; for Jehovah God had not caused it to rain upon the earth: and there was not a man to till the ground;

units.leftText: But springs welled up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.
units.rightText: but there went up a mist from the earth, and watered the whole face of the ground.
leftNotes: 2:6 Or mist

units.leftText: Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.
units.rightText: And Jehovah God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
leftNotes: 2:7 Or a living soul; cited in 1 Corinthians 15:45|1CO 15:45*

units.leftText: And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, where He placed the man He had formed.
units.rightText: And Jehovah God planted a garden eastward, in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.

units.leftText: Out of the ground the LORD God gave growth to every tree that is pleasing to the eye and good for food. And in the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
units.rightText: And out of the ground made Jehovah God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

units.leftText: Now a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it branched into four headwaters:
units.rightText: And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became four heads.

units.leftText: The name of the first river is the Pishon; it winds through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
units.rightText: The name of the first is Pishon: that is it which compasseth the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;

units.leftText: And the gold of that land is pure, and bdellium and onyx are found there.
units.rightText: and the gold of that land is good: there is bdellium and the onyx stone.

units.leftText: The name of the second river is the Gihon; it winds through the whole land of Cush.
units.rightText: And the name of the second river is Gihon: the same is it that compasseth the whole land of Cush.

units.leftText: The name of the third river is the Tigris; it runs along the east side of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
units.rightText: And the name of the third river is Hiddekel: that is it which goeth in front of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.

units.leftText: Then the LORD God took the man and placed him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
units.rightText: And Jehovah God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.

units.leftText: And the LORD God commanded him, “You may eat freely from every tree of the garden,
units.rightText: And Jehovah God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:

units.leftText: but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”
units.rightText: but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.

units.leftText: The LORD God also said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make for him a suitable helper.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a help meet for him.

units.leftText: And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and He brought them to the man to see what he would name each one. And whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.
units.rightText: And out of the ground Jehovah God formed every beast of the field, and every bird of the heavens; and brought them unto the man to see what he would call them: and whatsoever the man called every living creature, that was the name thereof.

units.leftText: The man gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam no suitable helper was found.
units.rightText: And the man gave names to all cattle, and to the birds of the heavens, and to every beast of the field; but for man there was not found a help meet for him.
leftNotes: 2:20 Or the man, as in verses 19 and 21

units.leftText: So the LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep, and while he slept, He took one of the man’s ribs and closed up the area with flesh.
units.rightText: And Jehovah God caused a deep sleep to fall upon the man, and he slept; and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof:
leftNotes: 2:21 Or took part of the man’s side; similarly in verse 22

units.leftText: And from the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man, He made a woman and brought her to him.
units.rightText: and the rib, which Jehovah God had taken from the man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.

units.leftText: And the man said: “This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called ‘woman,’ for out of man she was taken.”
units.rightText: And the man said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.

units.leftText: For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and they will become one flesh.
units.rightText: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
leftNotes: 2:24 LXX and the two will become one flesh; cited in Matthew 19:5|MAT 19:5*, Mark 10:7–8, 1 Corinthians 6:16, and Ephesians 5:31

units.leftText: And the man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.
units.rightText: And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.

units.leftText: Now the serpent was more crafty than any beast of the field that the LORD God had made. And he said to the woman, “Did God really say, ‘You must not eat from any tree in the garden?’”
units.rightText: Now the serpent was more subtle than any beast of the field which Jehovah God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of any tree of the garden?
leftNotes: 3:1 Hebrew nachash, translated in this chapter as serpent, is translated in most cases as snake.

units.leftText: The woman answered the serpent, “We may eat the fruit of the trees of the garden,
units.rightText: And the woman said unto the serpent, Of the fruit of the trees of the garden we may eat:

units.leftText: but about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God has said, ‘You must not eat of it or touch it, or you will die.’”
units.rightText: but of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.

units.leftText: “You will not surely die,” the serpent told the woman.
units.rightText: And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:

units.leftText: “For God knows that in the day you eat of it, your eyes will be opened and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”
units.rightText: for God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as God, knowing good and evil.

units.leftText: When the woman saw that the tree was good for food and pleasing to the eyes, and that it was desirable for obtaining wisdom, she took the fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate it.
units.rightText: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat; and she gave also unto her husband with her, and he did eat.

units.leftText: And the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked; so they sewed together fig leaves and made coverings for themselves. God Arraigns Adam and Eve
units.rightText: And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig-leaves together, and made themselves aprons.

units.leftText: Then the man and his wife heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the breeze of the day, and they hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
units.rightText: And they heard the voice of Jehovah God walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of Jehovah God amongst the trees of the garden.
leftNotes: 3:8 Or at the breezy (time); Hebrew unto the Ruach

units.leftText: But the LORD God called out to the man, “Where are you?”
units.rightText: And Jehovah God called unto the man, and said unto him, Where art thou?

units.leftText: “I heard Your voice in the garden,” he replied, “and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid myself.”
units.rightText: And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.

units.leftText: “Who told you that you were naked?” asked the LORD God. “Have you eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat?”
units.rightText: And he said, Who told thee that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?

units.leftText: And the man answered, “The woman whom You gave me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.”
units.rightText: And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.

units.leftText: Then the LORD God said to the woman, “What is this you have done?” “The serpent deceived me,” she replied, “and I ate.” The Fate of the Serpent
units.rightText: And Jehovah God said unto the woman, What is this thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.

units.leftText: So the LORD God said to the serpent: “Because you have done this, cursed are you above all livestock and every beast of the field! On your belly will you go, and dust you will eat, all the days of your life.
units.rightText: And Jehovah God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, cursed art thou above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life:

units.leftText: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel. ” The Punishment of Mankind
units.rightText: and I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed: he shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
leftNotes: 3:15 Or He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel. The same Hebrew root for crush, bruise, or strike appears twice in this verse.

units.leftText: To the woman He said: “I will sharply increase your pain in childbirth; in pain you will bring forth children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you.”
units.rightText: Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy pain and thy conception; in pain thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.
leftNotes: 3:16 Or You will desire to control your husband

units.leftText: And to Adam He said: “Because you have listened to the voice of your wife and have eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat, cursed is the ground because of you; through toil you will eat of it all the days of your life.
units.rightText: And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in toil shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life;

units.leftText: Both thorns and thistles it will yield for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.
units.rightText: thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field;

units.leftText: By the sweat of your brow you will eat your bread, until you return to the ground — because out of it were you taken. For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.”
units.rightText: in the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.

units.leftText: And Adam named his wife Eve, because she would be the mother of all the living. The Expulsion from Paradise
units.rightText: And the man called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.
leftNotes: 3:20 Eve sounds like the Hebrew for giving life or living.

units.leftText: And the LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and He clothed them.
units.rightText: And Jehovah God made for Adam and for his wife coats of skins, and clothed them.

units.leftText: Then the LORD God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of Us, knowing good and evil. And now, lest he reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever...”
units.rightText: And Jehovah God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil; and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever—

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD God banished him from the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.
units.rightText: therefore Jehovah God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.

units.leftText: So He drove out the man and stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along with a whirling sword of flame to guard the way to the tree of life.
units.rightText: So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden the Cherubim, and the flame of a sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.

units.leftText: And Adam had relations with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain. “With the help of the LORD I have brought forth a man,” she said.
units.rightText: And the man knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man with the help of Jehovah.
leftNotes: 4:1 Cain sounds like the Hebrew for acquired or brought forth.

units.leftText: Later she gave birth to Cain’s brother Abel.
units.rightText: And again she bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.

units.leftText: So in the course of time, Cain brought some of the fruit of the soil as an offering to the LORD,
units.rightText: And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: while Abel brought the best portions of the firstborn of his flock.
units.rightText: And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And Jehovah had respect unto Abel and to his offering:

units.leftText: but He had no regard for Cain and his offering. So Cain became very angry, and his countenance fell.
units.rightText: but unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.

units.leftText: “Why are you angry,” said the LORD to Cain, “and why has your countenance fallen?
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?

units.leftText: If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you refuse to do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it.”
units.rightText: If thou doest well, shall it not be lifted up? and if thou doest not well, sin coucheth at the door; and unto thee shall be its desire; but do thou rule over it.
leftNotes: 4:7 Or it desires to control you

units.leftText: Then Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let us go out to the field.” And while they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.
units.rightText: And Cain told Abel his brother. And it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.
leftNotes: 4:8 SP, LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate; Hebrew Then Cain spoke to his brother Abel.

units.leftText: And the LORD said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” “I do not know!” he answered. “Am I my brother’s keeper?”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: am I my brother’s keeper?

units.leftText: “What have you done?” replied the LORD. “The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground.
units.rightText: And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.

units.leftText: Now you are cursed and banished from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.
units.rightText: And now cursed art thou from the ground, which hath opened its mouth to receive thy brother’s blood from thy hand;

units.leftText: When you till the ground, it will no longer yield its produce to you. You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.”
units.rightText: when thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee its strength; a fugitive and a wanderer shalt thou be in the earth.

units.leftText: But Cain said to the LORD, “My punishment is greater than I can bear.
units.rightText: And Cain said unto Jehovah, My punishment is greater than I can bear.
leftNotes: 4:13 Or guilt or sin

units.leftText: Behold, this day You have driven me from the face of the earth, and from Your face I will be hidden; I will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.”
units.rightText: Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the ground; and from thy face shall I be hid; and I shall be a fugitive and a wanderer in the earth; and it will come to pass, that whosoever findeth me will slay me.

units.leftText: “Not so!” replied the LORD. “If anyone slays Cain, then Cain will be avenged sevenfold.” And the LORD placed a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would kill him.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And Jehovah appointed a sign for Cain, lest any finding him should smite him.
leftNotes: 4:15 LXX, Vulgate, and Syriac; Hebrew “Very well!” or “Therefore:”

units.leftText: So Cain went out from the presence of the LORD and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden. The Descendants of Cain
units.rightText: And Cain went out from the presence of Jehovah, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.
leftNotes: 4:16 Nod means wandering.

units.leftText: And Cain had relations with his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. Then Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch.
units.rightText: And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.

units.leftText: Now to Enoch was born Irad, and Irad was the father of Mehujael, and Mehujael was the father of Methusael, and Methusael was the father of Lamech.
units.rightText: And unto Enoch was born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael; and Mehujael begat Methushael; and Methushael begat Lamech.

units.leftText: And Lamech married two women, one named Adah and the other Zillah.
units.rightText: And Lamech took unto him two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.

units.leftText: Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and raise livestock.
units.rightText: And Adah bare Jabal: he was the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle.

units.leftText: And his brother’s name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play the harp and flute.
units.rightText: And his brother’s name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and pipe.

units.leftText: And Zillah gave birth to Tubal-cain, a forger of every implement of bronze and iron. And the sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.
units.rightText: And Zillah, she also bare Tubal-cain, the forger of every cutting instrument of brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.

units.leftText: Then Lamech said to his wives: “Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, listen to my speech. For I have slain a man for wounding me, a young man for striking me.
units.rightText: And Lamech said unto his wives: Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; Ye wives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: For I have slain a man for wounding me, And a young man for bruising me:

units.leftText: If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold.” Seth and Enosh
units.rightText: If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, Truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.
leftNotes: 4:24 Hebrew; LXX can be translated as either seventy times seven or seventy-sevenfold; see also Matthew 18:22|MAT 18:22*.

units.leftText: And Adam again had relations with his wife, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, “God has granted me another seed in place of Abel, since Cain killed him.”
units.rightText: And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For, said she, God hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel; for Cain slew him.
leftNotes: 4:25 Seth probably means granted or appointed.

units.leftText: And to Seth also a son was born, and he called him Enosh. At that time men began to call upon the name of the LORD.
units.rightText: And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enosh. Then began men to call upon the name of Jehovah.
leftNotes: 4:26 Or to proclaim; some translators to invoke or to call themselves by or to profane

units.leftText: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, He made him in His own likeness.
units.rightText: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him;

units.leftText: Male and female He created them, and He blessed them. And in the day they were created, He called them “man.”
units.rightText: male and female created he them, and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created.
leftNotes: 5:2 Cited in Matthew 19:4|MAT 19:4* and Mark 10:6
5:2 Hebrew Adam

units.leftText: When Adam was 130 years old, he had a son in his own likeness, after his own image; and he named him Seth.
units.rightText: And Adam lived a hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Seth, Adam lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and the days of Adam after he begat Seth were eight hundred years: and he begat sons and daughters.

units.leftText: So Adam lived a total of 930 years, and then he died.
units.rightText: And all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years: and he died.

units.leftText: When Seth was 105 years old, he became the father of Enosh.
units.rightText: And Seth lived a hundred and five years, and begat Enosh:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Enosh, Seth lived 807 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Seth lived after he begat Enosh eight hundred and seven years, and begat sons and daughters:

units.leftText: So Seth lived a total of 912 years, and then he died.
units.rightText: and all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years: and he died.

units.leftText: When Enosh was 90 years old, he became the father of Kenan.
units.rightText: And Enosh lived ninety years, and begat Kenan:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Kenan, Enosh lived 815 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Enosh lived after he begat Kenan eight hundred and fifteen years, and begat sons and daughters:

units.leftText: So Enosh lived a total of 905 years, and then he died.
units.rightText: and all the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years: and he died.

units.leftText: When Kenan was 70 years old, he became the father of Mahalalel.
units.rightText: And Kenan lived seventy years, and begat Mahalalel:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Mahalalel, Kenan lived 840 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Kenan lived after he begat Mahalalel eight hundred and forty years, and begat sons and daughters:

units.leftText: So Kenan lived a total of 910 years, and then he died.
units.rightText: and all the days of Kenan were nine hundred and ten years: and he died.

units.leftText: When Mahalalel was 65 years old, he became the father of Jared.
units.rightText: And Mahalalel lived sixty and five years, and begat Jared:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Jared, Mahalalel lived 830 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Mahalalel lived after he begat Jared eight hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters:

units.leftText: So Mahalalel lived a total of 895 years, and then he died. God Takes Up Enoch (Hebrews 11:5|HEB 11:5*)
units.rightText: and all the days of Mahalalel were eight hundred ninety and five years: and he died.

units.leftText: When Jared was 162 years old, he became the father of Enoch.
units.rightText: And Jared lived a hundred sixty and two years, and begat Enoch:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Enoch, Jared lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Jared lived after he begat Enoch eight hundred years, and begat sons and daughters:

units.leftText: So Jared lived a total of 962 years, and then he died.
units.rightText: and all the days of Jared were nine hundred sixty and two years: and he died.

units.leftText: When Enoch was 65 years old, he became the father of Methuselah.
units.rightText: And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Methuselah, Enoch walked with God 300 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters:
leftNotes: 5:22 LXX pleased God; also in verse 24

units.leftText: So Enoch lived a total of 365 years.
units.rightText: and all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years:

units.leftText: Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away. From Methuselah to Noah
units.rightText: and Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.
leftNotes: 5:24 LXX and he was not found, because God had taken him away; cited in Hebrews 11:5|HEB 11:5*

units.leftText: When Methuselah was 187 years old, he became the father of Lamech.
units.rightText: And Methuselah lived a hundred eighty and seven years, and begat Lamech:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Lamech, Methuselah lived 782 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Methuselah lived after he begat Lamech seven hundred eighty and two years, and begat sons and daughters:

units.leftText: So Methuselah lived a total of 969 years, and then he died.
units.rightText: and all the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty and nine years: and he died.

units.leftText: When Lamech was 182 years old, he had a son.
units.rightText: And Lamech lived a hundred eighty and two years, and begat a son:

units.leftText: And he named him Noah, saying, “May this one comfort us in the labor and toil of our hands caused by the ground that the LORD has cursed.”
units.rightText: and he called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us in our work and in the toil of our hands, which cometh because of the ground which Jehovah hath cursed.
leftNotes: 5:29 Noah sounds like the Hebrew for rest or comfort.

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Noah, Lamech lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: And Lamech lived after he begat Noah five hundred ninety and five years, and begat sons and daughters:

units.leftText: So Lamech lived a total of 777 years, and then he died.
units.rightText: And all the days of Lamech were seven hundred seventy and seven years: and he died.

units.leftText: After Noah was 500 years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
units.rightText: And Noah was five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

units.leftText: Now when men began to multiply on the face of the earth and daughters were born to them,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the ground, and daughters were born unto them,

units.leftText: the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and they took as wives whomever they chose.
units.rightText: that the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all that they chose.

units.leftText: So the LORD said, “My Spirit will not contend with man forever, for he is mortal; his days shall be 120 years.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, My Spirit shall not strive with man for ever, for that he also is flesh: yet shall his days be a hundred and twenty years.
leftNotes: 6:3 LXX and Syriac My Spirit will not remain in man forever

units.leftText: The Nephilim were on the earth in those days— and afterward as well— when the sons of God had relations with the daughters of men. And they bore them children who became the mighty men of old, men of renown.
units.rightText: The Nephilim were in the earth in those days, and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them: the same were the mighty men that were of old, the men of renown.

units.leftText: Then the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great upon the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time.
units.rightText: And Jehovah saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.

units.leftText: And the LORD regretted that He had made man on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart.
units.rightText: And it repented Jehovah that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.

units.leftText: So the LORD said, “I will blot out man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth — every man and beast and crawling creature and bird of the air — for I am grieved that I have made them.” Noah’s Favor with God
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the ground; both man, and beast, and creeping things, and birds of the heavens; for it repenteth me that I have made them.

units.leftText: Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD.
units.rightText: But Noah found favor in the eyes of Jehovah.

units.leftText: This is the account of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation; Noah walked with God.
units.rightText: These are the generations of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, and perfect in his generations: Noah walked with God.

units.leftText: And Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
units.rightText: And Noah begat three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

units.leftText: Now the earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and full of violence.
units.rightText: And the earth was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.

units.leftText: And God looked upon the earth and saw that it was corrupt; for all living creatures on the earth had corrupted their ways. Preparing the Ark (Hebrews 11:7|HEB 11:7*)
units.rightText: And God saw the earth, and, behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted their way upon the earth.
leftNotes: 6:12 Literally all flesh; similarly in verses 13, 17, and 19

units.leftText: Then God said to Noah, “The end of all living creatures has come before Me, because through them the earth is full of violence. Now behold, I will destroy both them and the earth.
units.rightText: And God said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth.

units.leftText: Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; make rooms in the ark and coat it with pitch inside and out.
units.rightText: Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
leftNotes: 6:14 Gopher is an unknown kind of tree; possibly cypress or cedar.

units.leftText: And this is how you are to build it: The ark is to be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
units.rightText: And this is how thou shalt make it: the length of the ark three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.
leftNotes: 6:15 The ark was approximately 450 feet long, 75 feet wide, and 45 feet high (137.2 meters long, 22.9 meters wide, and 13.7 meters high).

units.leftText: You are to make a roof for the ark, finish its walls a cubit from the top, place a door in the side of the ark, and build lower, middle, and upper decks.
units.rightText: A light shalt thou make to the ark, and to a cubit shalt thou finish it upward; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof; with lower, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.
leftNotes: 6:16 Or skylight or window
6:16 A cubit is approximately 18 inches or 45.7 centimeters.

units.leftText: And behold, I will bring floodwaters upon the earth to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life. Everything on the earth will perish.
units.rightText: And I, behold, I do bring the flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, from under heaven; everything that is in the earth shall die.

units.leftText: But I will establish My covenant with you, and you will enter the ark — you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.
units.rightText: But I will establish my covenant with thee; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons’ wives with thee.

units.leftText: And you are to bring two of every living creature into the ark — male and female — to keep them alive with you.
units.rightText: And of every living thing of all flesh, two of every sort shalt thou bring into the ark, to keep them alive with thee; they shall be male and female.

units.leftText: Two of every kind of bird and animal and crawling creature will come to you to be kept alive.
units.rightText: Of the birds after their kind, and of the cattle after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, two of every sort shall come unto thee, to keep them alive.

units.leftText: You are also to take for yourself every kind of food that is eaten and gather it as food for yourselves and for the animals.”
units.rightText: And take thou unto thee of all food that is eaten, and gather it to thee; and it shall be for food for thee, and for them.

units.leftText: So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.
units.rightText: Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Noah, “Go into the ark, you and all your family, because I have found you righteous in this generation.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.

units.leftText: You are to take with you seven pairs of every kind of clean animal, a male and its mate; a pair of every kind of unclean animal, a male and its mate;
units.rightText: Of every clean beast thou shalt take to thee seven and seven, the male and his female; and of the beasts that are not clean two, the male and his female:
leftNotes: 7:2 Or by sevens; also in verse 3

units.leftText: and seven pairs of every kind of bird of the air, male and female, to preserve their offspring on the face of all the earth.
units.rightText: of the birds also of the heavens, seven and seven, male and female, to keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth.

units.leftText: For seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe from the face of the earth every living thing I have made.”
units.rightText: For yet seven days, and I will cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights; and every living thing that I have made will I destroy from off the face of the ground.

units.leftText: And Noah did all that the LORD had commanded him.
units.rightText: And Noah did according unto all that Jehovah commanded him.

units.leftText: Now Noah was 600 years old when the floodwaters came upon the earth.
units.rightText: And Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters was upon the earth.

units.leftText: And Noah and his wife, with his sons and their wives, entered the ark to escape the waters of the flood.
units.rightText: And Noah went in, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons’ wives with him, into the ark, because of the waters of the flood.

units.leftText: The clean and unclean animals, the birds, and everything that crawls along the ground
units.rightText: Of clean beasts, and of beasts that are not clean, and of birds, and of everything that creepeth upon the ground,

units.leftText: came to Noah to enter the ark, two by two, male and female, as God had commanded Noah.
units.rightText: there went in two and two unto Noah into the ark, male and female, as God commanded Noah.

units.leftText: And after seven days the floodwaters came upon the earth.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after the seven days, that the waters of the flood were upon the earth.

units.leftText: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, on the seventeenth day of the second month, all the fountains of the great deep burst forth, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.
units.rightText: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.

units.leftText: And the rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
units.rightText: And the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.

units.leftText: On that very day Noah entered the ark, along with his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and his wife, and the three wives of his sons —
units.rightText: In the selfsame day entered Noah, and Shem, and Ham, and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah’s wife, and the three wives of his sons with them, into the ark;

units.leftText: they and every kind of wild animal, livestock, crawling creature, bird, and winged creature.
units.rightText: they, and every beast after its kind, and all the cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth after its kind, and every bird after its kind, every bird of every sort.

units.leftText: They came to Noah to enter the ark, two by two of every creature with the breath of life.
units.rightText: And they went in unto Noah into the ark, two and two of all flesh wherein is the breath of life.
leftNotes: 7:15 Literally of all flesh; similarly in verses 16 and 21

units.leftText: And they entered, the male and female of every living thing, as God had commanded Noah. Then the LORD shut him in.
units.rightText: And they that went in, went in male and female of all flesh, as God commanded him: and Jehovah shut him in.

units.leftText: For forty days the flood kept coming on the earth, and the waters rose and lifted the ark high above the earth.
units.rightText: And the flood was forty days upon the earth; and the waters increased, and bare up the ark, and it was lifted up above the earth.

units.leftText: So the waters continued to surge and rise greatly on the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the waters.
units.rightText: And the waters prevailed, and increased greatly upon the earth; and the ark went upon the face of the waters.

units.leftText: Finally, the waters completely prevailed upon the earth, so that all the high mountains under all the heavens were covered.
units.rightText: And the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth; and all the high mountains that were under the whole heaven were covered.

units.leftText: The waters rose and covered the mountaintops to a depth of fifteen cubits.
units.rightText: Fifteen cubits upward did the waters prevail; and the mountains were covered.
leftNotes: 7:20 15 cubits is approximately 22.5 feet or 6.9 meters.

units.leftText: And every living thing that moved upon the earth perished — birds, livestock, animals, every creature that swarms upon the earth, and all mankind.
units.rightText: And all flesh died that moved upon the earth, both birds, and cattle, and beasts, and every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth, and every man:

units.leftText: Of all that was on dry land, everything that had the breath of life in its nostrils died.
units.rightText: all in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, of all that was on the dry land, died.

units.leftText: And every living thing on the face of the earth was destroyed — man and livestock, crawling creatures and birds of the air; they were blotted out from the earth, and only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.
units.rightText: And every living thing was destroyed that was upon the face of the ground, both man, and cattle, and creeping things, and birds of the heavens; and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noah only was left, and they that were with him in the ark.

units.leftText: And the waters prevailed upon the earth for 150 days.
units.rightText: And the waters prevailed upon the earth a hundred and fifty days.

units.leftText: But God remembered Noah and all the animals and livestock that were with him in the ark. And God sent a wind over the earth, and the waters began to subside.
units.rightText: And God remembered Noah, and all the beasts, and all the cattle that were with him in the ark: and God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters assuaged;

units.leftText: The springs of the deep and the floodgates of the heavens were closed, and the rain from the sky was restrained.
units.rightText: the fountains also of the deep and the windows of heaven were stopped, and the rain from heaven was restrained;

units.leftText: The waters receded steadily from the earth, and after 150 days the waters had gone down.
units.rightText: and the waters returned from off the earth continually: and after the end of a hundred and fifty days the waters decreased.

units.leftText: On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
units.rightText: And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.

units.leftText: And the waters continued to recede until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible. Noah Sends a Raven and a Dove
units.rightText: And the waters decreased continually until the tenth month: in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, were the tops of the mountains seen.

units.leftText: After forty days Noah opened the window he had made in the ark
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the end of forty days, that Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made:

units.leftText: and sent out a raven. It kept flying back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth.
units.rightText: and he sent forth a raven, and it went forth to and fro, until the waters were dried up from off the earth.

units.leftText: Then Noah sent out a dove to see if the waters had receded from the surface of the ground.
units.rightText: And he sent forth a dove from him, to see if the waters were abated from off the face of the ground;
leftNotes: 8:8 Literally sent out from him or sent out from it

units.leftText: But the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned to him in the ark, because the waters were still covering the surface of all the earth. So he reached out his hand and brought her back inside the ark.
units.rightText: but the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot, and she returned unto him to the ark; for the waters were on the face of the whole earth: and he put forth his hand, and took her, and brought her in unto him into the ark.

units.leftText: Noah waited seven more days and again sent out the dove from the ark.
units.rightText: And he stayed yet other seven days; and again he sent forth the dove out of the ark;

units.leftText: And behold, the dove returned to him in the evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf in her beak. So Noah knew that the waters had receded from the earth.
units.rightText: and the dove came in to him at eventide; and, lo, in her mouth an olive-leaf plucked off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.

units.leftText: And Noah waited seven more days and sent out the dove again, but this time she did not return to him. Exiting the Ark
units.rightText: And he stayed yet other seven days, and sent forth the dove; and she returned not again unto him any more.

units.leftText: In Noah’s six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the waters had dried up from the earth. So Noah removed the covering from the ark and saw that the surface of the ground was dry.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the six hundred and first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were dried up from off the earth: and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and, behold, the face of the ground was dried.

units.leftText: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was fully dry.
units.rightText: And in the second month, on the seven and twentieth day of the month, was the earth dry.

units.leftText: Then God said to Noah,
units.rightText: And God spake unto Noah, saying,

units.leftText: “Come out of the ark, you and your wife, along with your sons and their wives.
units.rightText: Go forth from the ark, thou, and thy wife, and thy sons, and thy sons’ wives with thee.

units.leftText: Bring out all the living creatures that are with you— birds, livestock, and everything that crawls upon the ground— so that they can spread out over the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon it.”
units.rightText: Bring forth with thee every living thing that is with thee of all flesh, both birds, and cattle, and every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth; that they may breed abundantly in the earth, and be fruitful, and multiply upon the earth.

units.leftText: So Noah came out, along with his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives.
units.rightText: And Noah went forth, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons’ wives with him:

units.leftText: Every living creature, every creeping thing, and every bird — everything that moves upon the earth — came out of the ark, kind by kind. Noah Builds an Altar
units.rightText: every beast, every creeping thing, and every bird, whatsoever moveth upon the earth, after their families, went forth out of the ark.

units.leftText: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD. And taking from every kind of clean animal and clean bird, he offered burnt offerings on the altar.
units.rightText: And Noah builded an altar unto Jehovah, and took of every clean beast, and of every clean bird, and offered burnt-offerings on the altar.

units.leftText: When the LORD smelled the pleasing aroma, He said in His heart, “Never again will I curse the ground because of man, even though every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth. And never again will I destroy all living creatures as I have done.
units.rightText: And Jehovah smelled the sweet savor; and Jehovah said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake, for that the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth; neither will I again smite any more everything living, as I have done.

units.leftText: As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall never cease.”
units.rightText: While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.

units.leftText: And God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.
units.rightText: And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.

units.leftText: The fear and dread of you will fall on every living creature on the earth, every bird of the air, every creature that crawls on the ground, and all the fish of the sea. They are delivered into your hand.
units.rightText: And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every bird of the heavens; with all wherewith the ground teemeth, and all the fishes of the sea, into your hand are they delivered.

units.leftText: Everything that lives and moves will be food for you; just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you all things.
units.rightText: Every moving thing that liveth shall be food for you; as the green herb have I given you all.

units.leftText: But you must not eat meat with its lifeblood still in it.
units.rightText: But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.

units.leftText: And surely I will require the life of any man or beast by whose hand your lifeblood is shed. I will demand an accounting from anyone who takes the life of his fellow man:
units.rightText: And surely your blood, the blood of your lives, will I require; at the hand of every beast will I require it: and at the hand of man, even at the hand of every man’s brother, will I require the life of man.

units.leftText: Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man his blood will be shed; for in His own image God has made mankind.
units.rightText: Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.

units.leftText: But as for you, be fruitful and multiply; spread out across the earth and multiply upon it.”
units.rightText: And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply; bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein.

units.leftText: Then God said to Noah and his sons with him,
units.rightText: And God spake unto Noah, and to his sons with him, saying,

units.leftText: “Behold, I now establish My covenant with you and your descendants after you,
units.rightText: And I, behold, I establish my covenant with you, and with your seed after you;

units.leftText: and with every living creature that was with you — the birds, the livestock, and every beast of the earth— every living thing that came out of the ark.
units.rightText: and with every living creature that is with you, the birds, the cattle, and every beast of the earth with you; of all that go out of the ark, even every beast of the earth.

units.leftText: And I establish My covenant with you: Never again will all life be cut off by the waters of a flood; never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth.”
units.rightText: And I will establish my covenant with you; neither shall all flesh be cut off any more by the waters of the flood; neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth.

units.leftText: And God said, “This is the sign of the covenant I am making between Me and you and every living creature with you, a covenant for all generations to come:
units.rightText: And God said, This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:

units.leftText: I have set My rainbow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth.
units.rightText: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.

units.leftText: Whenever I form clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears in the clouds,
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, when I bring a cloud over the earth, that the bow shall be seen in the cloud,

units.leftText: I will remember My covenant between Me and you and every living creature of every kind. Never again will the waters become a flood to destroy all life.
units.rightText: and I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.

units.leftText: And whenever the rainbow appears in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of every kind that is on the earth.”
units.rightText: And the bow shall be in the cloud; and I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth.

units.leftText: So God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between Me and every creature on the earth.” Noah’s Shame and Canaan’s Curse
units.rightText: And God said unto Noah, This is the token of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh that is upon the earth.

units.leftText: The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. And Ham was the father of Canaan.
units.rightText: And the sons of Noah, that went forth from the ark, were Shem, and Ham, and Japheth: and Ham is the father of Canaan.

units.leftText: These three were the sons of Noah, and from them the whole earth was populated.
units.rightText: These three were the sons of Noah: and of these was the whole earth overspread.

units.leftText: Now Noah, a man of the soil, proceeded to plant a vineyard.
units.rightText: And Noah began to be a husbandman, and planted a vineyard:
leftNotes: 9:20 Or was the first

units.leftText: But when he drank some of its wine, he became drunk and uncovered himself inside his tent.
units.rightText: and he drank of the wine, and was drunken; and he was uncovered within his tent.

units.leftText: And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father’s nakedness and told his two brothers outside.
units.rightText: And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brethren without.

units.leftText: Then Shem and Japheth took a garment and placed it across their shoulders, and walking backward, they covered their father’s nakedness. Their faces were turned away so that they did not see their father’s nakedness.
units.rightText: And Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it upon both their shoulders, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces were backward, and they saw not their father’s nakedness.

units.leftText: When Noah awoke from his drunkenness and learned what his youngest son had done to him,
units.rightText: And Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his youngest son had done unto him.

units.leftText: he said, “Cursed be Canaan! A servant of servants shall he be to his brothers.” Shem’s Blessing and Noah’s Death
units.rightText: And he said, Cursed be Canaan; A servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.

units.leftText: He also declared: “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem! May Canaan be the servant of Shem.
units.rightText: And he said, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Shem; And let Canaan be his servant.

units.leftText: May God expand the territory of Japheth; may he dwell in the tents of Shem, and may Canaan be his servant.”
units.rightText: God enlarge Japheth, And let him dwell in the tents of Shem; And let Canaan be his servant.
leftNotes: 9:27 Japheth sounds like the Hebrew for expand.

units.leftText: After the flood, Noah lived 350 years.
units.rightText: And Noah lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years.

units.leftText: So Noah lived a total of 950 years, and then he died.
units.rightText: And all the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years: and he died.

units.leftText: This is the account of Noah’s sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, who also had sons after the flood. The Japhethites
units.rightText: Now these are the generations of the sons of Noah, namely, of Shem, Ham, and Japheth: and unto them were sons born after the flood.

units.leftText: The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
units.rightText: The sons of Japheth: Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.

units.leftText: The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
units.rightText: And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.

units.leftText: And the sons of Javan:
units.rightText: And the sons of Javan: Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

units.leftText: From these, the maritime peoples separated into their territories, according to their languages, by clans within their nations. The Hamites
units.rightText: Of these were the isles of the nations divided in their lands, every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.

units.leftText: The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
units.rightText: And the sons of Ham: Cush, and Mizraim, and Put, and Canaan.

units.leftText: The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. And the sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
units.rightText: And the sons of Cush: Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabteca; and the sons of Raamah: Sheba, and Dedan.
leftNotes: 10:7 Sabtah is a variant of Sabta; see 1 Chronicles 1:9|1CH 1:9*.

units.leftText: Cush was the father of Nimrod, who began to be a mighty one on the earth.
units.rightText: And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth.
leftNotes: 10:8 Or who established himself as a mighty warrior or who became the first fearless leader

units.leftText: He was a mighty hunter before the LORD; so it is said, “Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD.”
units.rightText: He was a mighty hunter before Jehovah: wherefore it is said, Like Nimrod a mighty hunter before Jehovah.
leftNotes: 10:9 Or in defiance of; twice in this verse

units.leftText: His kingdom began in Babylon, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
units.rightText: And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
leftNotes: 10:10 That is, Babylonia

units.leftText: From that land he went forth into Assyria, where he built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah,
units.rightText: Out of that land he went forth into Assyria, and builded Nineveh, and Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah,

units.leftText: and Resen, which is between Nineveh and the great city of Calah.
units.rightText: and Resen between Nineveh and Calah (the same is the great city).

units.leftText: Mizraim was the father of the Ludites, the Anamites, the Lehabites, the Naphtuhites,
units.rightText: And Mizraim begat Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim,

units.leftText: the Pathrusites, the Casluhites (from whom the Philistines came), and the Caphtorites.
units.rightText: and Pathrusim, and Casluhim (whence went forth the Philistines), and Caphtorim.
leftNotes: 10:14 Some translators adjust the Hebrew word order to the Casluhites, and the Caphtorites (from whom the Philistines came); see also Jeremiah 47:4|JER 47:4* and Amos 9:7.

units.leftText: And Canaan was the father of Sidon his firstborn, and of the Hittites,
units.rightText: And Canaan begat Sidon his first-born, and Heth,
leftNotes: 10:15 Or of the Sidonians, the foremost

units.leftText: the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
units.rightText: and the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite,

units.leftText: the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
units.rightText: and the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite,

units.leftText: the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites.
units.rightText: and the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite: and afterward were the families of the Canaanite spread abroad.

units.leftText: and the borders of Canaan extended from Sidon toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and then toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
units.rightText: And the border of the Canaanite was from Sidon, as thou goest toward Gerar, unto Gaza; as thou goest toward Sodom and Gomorrah and Admah and Zeboiim, unto Lasha.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Ham according to their clans, languages, lands, and nations. The Semites
units.rightText: These are the sons of Ham, after their families, after their tongues, in their lands, in their nations.

units.leftText: And sons were also born to Shem, the older brother of Japheth; Shem was the forefather of all the sons of Eber.
units.rightText: And unto Shem, the father of all the children of Eber, the elder brother of Japheth, to him also were children born.
leftNotes: 10:21 Or Shem, whose older brother was Japheth

units.leftText: The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.
units.rightText: The sons of Shem: Elam, and Asshur, and Arpachshad, and Lud, and Aram.

units.leftText: The sons of Aram: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
units.rightText: And the sons of Aram: Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Mash.
leftNotes: 10:23 Hebrew; LXX and 1 Chronicles 1:17|1CH 1:17* Meshech

units.leftText: Arphaxad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah was the father of Eber.
units.rightText: And Arpachshad begat Shelah; and Shelah begat Eber.
leftNotes: 10:24 Hebrew; LXX (see also Luke 3:35–36|LUK 3:35-36*) And Arphaxad was the father of Cainan, and Cainan was the father of Shelah,

units.leftText: Two sons were born to Eber: One was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and his brother was named Joktan.
units.rightText: And unto Eber were born two sons: the name of the one was Peleg; for in his days was the earth divided; and his brother’s name was Joktan.
leftNotes: 10:25 Peleg means division.

units.leftText: And Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
units.rightText: And Joktan begat Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,

units.leftText: Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
units.rightText: and Hadoram, and Uzal, and Diklah,

units.leftText: Obal, Abimael, Sheba,
units.rightText: and Obal, and Abimael, and Sheba,

units.leftText: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.
units.rightText: and Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab: all these were the sons of Joktan.

units.leftText: Their territory extended from Mesha to Sephar, in the eastern hill country.
units.rightText: And their dwelling was from Mesha, as thou goest toward Sephar, the mountain of the east.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Shem, according to their clans, languages, lands, and nations.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Shem, after their families, after their tongues, in their lands, after their nations.

units.leftText: All these are the clans of Noah’s sons, according to their generations and nations. From these the nations of the earth spread out after the flood.
units.rightText: These are the families of the sons of Noah, after their generations, in their nations: and of these were the nations divided in the earth after the flood.

units.leftText: Now the whole world had one language and a common form of speech.
units.rightText: And the whole earth was of one language and of one speech.

units.leftText: And as people journeyed eastward, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as they journeyed east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar; and they dwelt there.
leftNotes: 11:2 Or from the east or in the east
11:2 That is, Babylonia

units.leftText: And they said to one another, “Come, let us make bricks and bake them thoroughly.” So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.
units.rightText: And they said one to another, Come, let us make brick, and burn them thoroughly. And they had brick for stone, and slime had they for mortar.

units.leftText: “Come,” they said, “let us build for ourselves a city with a tower that reaches to the heavens, that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.”
units.rightText: And they said, Come, let us build us a city, and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven, and let us make us a name; lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.

units.leftText: Then the LORD came down to see the city and the tower that the sons of men were building.
units.rightText: And Jehovah came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men builded.

units.leftText: And the LORD said, “If they have begun to do this as one people speaking the same language, then nothing they devise will be beyond them.
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, Behold, they are one people, and they have all one language; and this is what they begin to do: and now nothing will be withholden from them, which they purpose to do.

units.leftText: Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.”
units.rightText: Come, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.

units.leftText: So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city.
units.rightText: So Jehovah scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off building the city.

units.leftText: That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world, and from that place the LORD scattered them over the face of all the earth. Genealogy from Shem to Abram (1 Chronicles 1:17–27|1CH 1:17-27*)
units.rightText: Therefore was the name of it called Babel; because Jehovah did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did Jehovah scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.
leftNotes: 11:9 Or Babylon; the Hebrew word for Babel sounds like the Hebrew for confused.

units.leftText: This is the account of Shem. Two years after the flood, when Shem was 100 years old, he became the father of Arphaxad.
units.rightText: These are the generations of Shem. Shem was a hundred years old, and begat Arpachshad two years after the flood:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Arphaxad, Shem lived 500 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Shem lived after he begat Arpachshad five hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.

units.leftText: When Arphaxad was 35 years old, he became the father of Shelah.
units.rightText: And Arpachshad lived five and thirty years, and begat Shelah:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Shelah, Arphaxad lived 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Arpachshad lived after he begat Shelah four hundred and three years, and begat sons and daughters.
leftNotes: 11:13 Hebrew; LXX (see also Luke 3:35–36|LUK 3:35-36*) 12*When Arphaxad was 135 years old, he became the father of Cainan. 13*And after he had become the father of Cainan, Arphaxad lived 430 years and had other sons and daughters, and then he died. When Cainan had lived 130 years, he became the father of Shelah. And after he had become the father of Shelah, Cainan lived 330 years and had other sons and daughters.Note that LXX also adds 100 years to the ages of Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, and Nahor in this genealogy.

units.leftText: When Shelah was 30 years old, he became the father of Eber.
units.rightText: And Shelah lived thirty years, and begat Eber:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Eber, Shelah lived 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Shelah lived after he begat Eber four hundred and three years, and begat sons and daughters.

units.leftText: When Eber was 34 years old, he became the father of Peleg.
units.rightText: And Eber lived four and thirty years, and begat Peleg:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Peleg, Eber lived 430 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Eber lived after he begat Peleg four hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters.

units.leftText: When Peleg was 30 years old, he became the father of Reu.
units.rightText: And Peleg lived thirty years, and begat Reu:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Reu, Peleg lived 209 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Peleg lived after he begat Reu two hundred and nine years, and begat sons and daughters.

units.leftText: When Reu was 32 years old, he became the father of Serug.
