units.rightText: And Reu lived two and thirty years, and begat Serug:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Serug, Reu lived 207 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Reu lived after he begat Serug two hundred and seven years, and begat sons and daughters.

units.leftText: When Serug was 30 years old, he became the father of Nahor.
units.rightText: And Serug lived thirty years, and begat Nahor:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Nahor, Serug lived 200 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Serug lived after he begat Nahor two hundred years, and begat sons and daughters.

units.leftText: When Nahor was 29 years old, he became the father of Terah.
units.rightText: And Nahor lived nine and twenty years, and begat Terah:

units.leftText: And after he had become the father of Terah, Nahor lived 119 years and had other sons and daughters.
units.rightText: and Nahor lived after he begat Terah a hundred and nineteen years, and begat sons and daughters.

units.leftText: When Terah was 70 years old, he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Terah’s Descendants
units.rightText: And Terah lived seventy years, and begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

units.leftText: This is the account of Terah. Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. And Haran became the father of Lot.
units.rightText: Now these are the generations of Terah. Terah begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran; and Haran begat Lot.

units.leftText: During his father Terah’s lifetime, Haran died in his native land, in Ur of the Chaldeans.
units.rightText: And Haran died before his father Terah in the land of his nativity, in Ur of the Chaldees.

units.leftText: And Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. Abram’s wife was named Sarai, and Nahor’s wife was named Milcah; she was the daughter of Haran, who was the father of both Milcah and Iscah.
units.rightText: And Abram and Nahor took them wives: the name of Abram’s wife was Sarai; and the name of Nahor’s wife, Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah, and the father of Iscah.

units.leftText: But Sarai was barren; she had no children.
units.rightText: And Sarai was barren; she had no child.

units.leftText: And Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot son of Haran, and his daughter-in-law Sarai the wife of Abram, and they set out from Ur of the Chaldeans for the land of Canaan. But when they arrived in Haran, they settled there.
units.rightText: And Terah took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran, his son’s son, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, his son Abram’s wife; and they went forth with them from Ur of the Chaldees, to go into the land of Canaan; and they came unto Haran, and dwelt there.

units.leftText: Terah lived 205 years, and he died in Haran.
units.rightText: And the days of Terah were two hundred and five years: and Terah died in Haran.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Abram, “Leave your country, your kindred, and your father’s household, and go to the land I will show you.
units.rightText: Now Jehovah said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto the land that I will show thee:
leftNotes: 12:1 Cited in Acts 7:3|ACT 7:3*

units.leftText: I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you; I will make your name great, so that you will be a blessing.
units.rightText: and I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and be thou a blessing:

units.leftText: I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you; and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you. ”
units.rightText: and I will bless them that bless thee, and him that curseth thee will I curse: and in thee shall all the families of the earth be blessed.
leftNotes: 12:3 See Galatians 3:8|GAL 3:8*

units.leftText: So Abram departed, as the LORD had directed him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
units.rightText: So Abram went, as Jehovah had spoken unto him; and Lot went with him: and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.

units.leftText: And Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, and all the possessions and people they had acquired in Haran, and set out for the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: And Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother’s son, and all their substance that they had gathered, and the souls that they had gotten in Haran; and they went forth to go into the land of Canaan; and into the land of Canaan they came.

units.leftText: Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of the Oak of Moreh at Shechem. And at that time the Canaanites were in the land.
units.rightText: And Abram passed through the land unto the place of Shechem, unto the oak of Moreh. And the Canaanite was then in the land.
leftNotes: 12:6 Or Terebinth or Great Tree

units.leftText: Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your offspring. ” So Abram built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
units.rightText: And Jehovah appeared unto Abram, and said, Unto thy seed will I give this land: and there builded he an altar unto Jehovah, who appeared unto him.
leftNotes: 12:7 Cited in Galatians 3:16|GAL 3:16*

units.leftText: From there Abram moved on to the hill country east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built an altar to the LORD, and he called on the name of the LORD.
units.rightText: And he removed from thence unto the mountain on the east of Beth-el, and pitched his tent, having Beth-el on the west, and Ai on the east: and there he builded an altar unto Jehovah, and called upon the name of Jehovah.

units.leftText: And Abram journeyed on toward the Negev. Abram and Sarai in Egypt
units.rightText: And Abram journeyed, going on still toward the South.

units.leftText: Now there was a famine in the land. So Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while because the famine was severe.
units.rightText: And there was a famine in the land: and Abram went down into Egypt to sojourn there; for the famine was sore in the land.

units.leftText: As he was about to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, “Look, I know that you are a beautiful woman,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he was come near to enter into Egypt, that he said unto Sarai his wife, Behold now, I know that thou art a fair woman to look upon:

units.leftText: and when the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife.’ Then they will kill me but will let you live.
units.rightText: and it will come to pass, when the Egyptians shall see thee, that they will say, This is his wife: and they will kill me, but they will save thee alive.

units.leftText: Please say you are my sister, so that I will be treated well for your sake, and on account of you my life will be spared.”
units.rightText: Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister; that it may be well with me for thy sake, and that my soul may live because of thee.

units.leftText: So when Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that, when Abram was come into Egypt, the Egyptians beheld the woman that she was very fair.

units.leftText: When Pharaoh’s officials saw Sarai, they commended her to him, and she was taken into the palace of Pharaoh.
units.rightText: And the princes of Pharaoh saw her, and praised her to Pharaoh: and the woman was taken into Pharaoh’s house.

units.leftText: He treated Abram well on her account, and Abram acquired sheep and cattle, male and female donkeys, menservants and maidservants, and camels.
units.rightText: And he dealt well with Abram for her sake: and he had sheep, and oxen, and he-asses, and men-servants, and maid-servants, and she-asses, and camels.

units.leftText: The LORD, however, afflicted Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues because of Abram’s wife Sarai.
units.rightText: And Jehovah plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.

units.leftText: So Pharaoh summoned Abram and asked, “What have you done to me? Why didn’t you tell me she was your wife?
units.rightText: And Pharaoh called Abram, and said, What is this that thou hast done unto me? why didst thou not tell me that she was thy wife?

units.leftText: Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her as my wife? Now then, here is your wife. Take her and go!”
units.rightText: why saidst thou, She is my sister, so that I took her to be my wife? now therefore behold thy wife, take her, and go thy way.

units.leftText: Then Pharaoh gave his men orders concerning Abram, and they sent him away with his wife and all his possessions.
units.rightText: And Pharaoh gave men charge concerning him: and they brought him on the way, and his wife, and all that he had.

units.leftText: So Abram went up out of Egypt into the Negev— he and his wife and all his possessions— and Lot was with him.
units.rightText: And Abram went up out of Egypt, he, and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him, into the South.

units.leftText: And Abram had become extremely wealthy in livestock and silver and gold.
units.rightText: And Abram was very rich in cattle, in silver, and in gold.

units.leftText: From the Negev he journeyed from place to place toward Bethel, until he came to the place between Bethel and Ai where his tent had formerly been pitched,
units.rightText: And he went on his journeys from the South even to Beth-el, unto the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Beth-el and Ai,

units.leftText: to the site where he had built the altar. And there Abram called on the name of the LORD.
units.rightText: unto the place of the altar, which he had made there at the first: and there Abram called on the name of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Now Lot, who was traveling with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents.
units.rightText: And Lot also, who went with Abram, had flocks, and herds, and tents.

units.leftText: But the land was unable to support both of them while they stayed together, for they had so many possessions that they were unable to coexist.
units.rightText: And the land was not able to bear them, that they might dwell together: for their substance was great, so that they could not dwell together.

units.leftText: And there was discord between the herdsmen of Abram and the herdsmen of Lot. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were also living in the land.
units.rightText: And there was a strife between the herdsmen of Abram’s cattle and the herdsmen of Lot’s cattle: and the Canaanite and the Perizzite dwelt then in the land.

units.leftText: So Abram said to Lot, “Please let there be no contention between you and me, or between your herdsmen and my herdsmen. After all, we are kinsmen.
units.rightText: And Abram said unto Lot, Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdsmen and thy herdsmen; for we are brethren.

units.leftText: Is not the whole land before you? Now separate yourself from me. If you go to the left, I will go to the right; if you go to the right, I will go to the left.” Lot Proceeds toward Sodom
units.rightText: Is not the whole land before thee? separate thyself, I pray thee, from me: if thou wilt take the left hand, then I will go to the right; or if thou take the right hand, then I will go to the left.

units.leftText: And Lot looked out and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan, all the way to Zoar, was well watered like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt. (This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.)
units.rightText: And Lot lifted up his eyes, and beheld all the Plain of the Jordan, that it was well watered every where, before Jehovah destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like the garden of Jehovah, like the land of Egypt, as thou goest unto Zoar.

units.leftText: So Lot chose the whole plain of the Jordan for himself and set out toward the east. And Abram and Lot parted company.
units.rightText: So Lot chose him all the Plain of the Jordan; and Lot journeyed east: and they separated themselves the one from the other.

units.leftText: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, but Lot settled in the cities of the plain and pitched his tent toward Sodom.
units.rightText: Abram dwelt in the land of Canaan, and Lot dwelt in the cities of the Plain, and moved his tent as far as Sodom.

units.leftText: But the men of Sodom were wicked, sinning greatly against the LORD. God Renews the Promise to Abram
units.rightText: Now the men of Sodom were wicked and sinners against Jehovah exceedingly.

units.leftText: After Lot had departed, the LORD said to Abram, “Now lift up your eyes from the place where you are, and look to the north and south and east and west,
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Abram, after that Lot was separated from him, Lift up now thine eyes, and look from the place where thou art, northward and southward and eastward and westward:

units.leftText: for all the land that you see, I will give to you and your offspring forever.
units.rightText: for all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.
leftNotes: 13:15 Cited in Galatians 3:16|GAL 3:16*

units.leftText: I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth, so that if one could count the dust of the earth, then your offspring could be counted.
units.rightText: And I will make thy seed as the dust of the earth: so that if a man can number the dust of the earth, then may thy seed also be numbered.

units.leftText: Get up and walk around the land, through its length and breadth, for I will give it to you.”
units.rightText: Arise, walk through the land in the length of it and in the breadth of it; for unto thee will I give it.

units.leftText: So Abram moved his tent and went to live near the Oaks of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar to the LORD.
units.rightText: And Abram moved his tent, and came and dwelt by the oaks of Mamre, which are in Hebron, and built there an altar unto Jehovah.
leftNotes: 13:18 Or Terebinths or Great Trees

units.leftText: In those days Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim,
leftNotes: 14:1 That is, Babylonia; also in verse 9

units.leftText: went to war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar).
units.rightText: that they made war with Bera king of Sodom, and with Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, and Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (the same is Zoar).

units.leftText: The latter five came as allies to the Valley of Siddim (that is, the Salt Sea ).
units.rightText: All these joined together in the vale of Siddim (the same is the Salt Sea).
leftNotes: 14:3 That is, the Dead Sea

units.leftText: For twelve years they had been subject to Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
units.rightText: Twelve years they served Chedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.

units.leftText: In the fourteenth year, Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him went out and defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, the Emites in Shaveh-kiriathaim,
units.rightText: And in the fourteenth year came Chedorlaomer, and the kings that were with him, and smote the Rephaim in Ashteroth-karnaim, and the Zuzim in Ham, and the Emim in Shaveh-kiriathaim,

units.leftText: and the Horites in the area of Mount Seir, as far as El-paran, which is near the desert.
units.rightText: and the Horites in their mount Seir, unto El-paran, which is by the wilderness.

units.leftText: Then they turned back to invade En-mishpat (that is, Kadesh), and they conquered the whole territory of the Amalekites, as well as the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar.
units.rightText: And they returned, and came to En-mishpat (the same is Kadesh), and smote all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites, that dwelt in Hazazon-tamar.

units.leftText: Then the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar) marched out and arrayed themselves for battle in the Valley of Siddim
units.rightText: And there went out the king of Sodom, and the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Admah, and the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela (the same is Zoar); and they set the battle in array against them in the vale of Siddim;
leftNotes: 14:8 That is, the Valley of the Dead Sea

units.leftText: against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar— four kings against five. Abram Rescues Lot
units.rightText: against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim, and Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar; four kings against the five.

units.leftText: Now the Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits, and as the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some men fell into the pits, but the survivors fled to the hill country.
units.rightText: Now the vale of Siddim was full of slime pits; and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, and they fell there, and they that remained fled to the mountain.

units.leftText: The four kings seized all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food, and they went on their way.
units.rightText: And they took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah, and all their victuals, and went their way.

units.leftText: They also carried off Abram’s nephew Lot and his possessions, since Lot was living in Sodom.
units.rightText: And they took Lot, Abram’s brother’s son, who dwelt in Sodom, and his goods, and departed.

units.leftText: Then an escapee came and reported this to Abram the Hebrew. Now Abram was living near the Oaks of Mamre the Amorite, a brother of Eshcol and Aner, all of whom were bound by treaty to Abram.
units.rightText: And there came one that had escaped, and told Abram the Hebrew: now he dwelt by the oaks of Mamre, the Amorite, brother of Eshcol, and brother of Aner; and these were confederate with Abram.
leftNotes: 14:13 Or Terebinths or Great Trees
14:13 Forms of the Hebrew berit are translated in most passages as covenant.

units.leftText: And when Abram heard that his relative had been captured, he mobilized the 318 trained men born in his household, and they set out in pursuit as far as Dan.
units.rightText: And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he led forth his trained men, born in his house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued as far as Dan.

units.leftText: During the night, Abram divided his forces and routed Chedorlaomer’s army, pursuing them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus.
units.rightText: And he divided himself against them by night, he and his servants, and smote them, and pursued them unto Hobah, which is on the left hand of Damascus.

units.leftText: He retrieved all the goods, as well as his relative Lot and his possessions, together with the women and the rest of the people. Melchizedek Blesses Abram (Psalm 110:1–7|PSA 110:1-7*; Hebrews 7:1–10|HEB 7:1-10*)
units.rightText: And he brought back all the goods, and also brought back his brother Lot, and his goods, and the women also, and the people.

units.leftText: After Abram returned from defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him, the king of Sodom went out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh (that is, the King’s Valley).
units.rightText: And the king of Sodom went out to meet him, after his return from the slaughter of Chedorlaomer and the kings that were with him, at the vale of Shaveh (the same is the King’s Vale).

units.leftText: Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine — since he was priest of God Most High —
units.rightText: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was priest of God Most High.
leftNotes: 14:18 Hebrew El-Elyon; also in verses 19, 20, and 22; cited in Hebrews 7:1|HEB 7:1*

units.leftText: and he blessed Abram and said: “Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth,
units.rightText: And he blessed him, and said, Blessed be Abram of God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth:

units.leftText: and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.” Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.
units.rightText: and blessed be God Most High, who hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. And he gave him a tenth of all.

units.leftText: The king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the people, but take the goods for yourself.”
units.rightText: And the king of Sodom said unto Abram, Give me the persons, and take the goods to thyself.

units.leftText: But Abram replied to the king of Sodom, “I have raised my hand to the LORD God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth,
units.rightText: And Abram said to the king of Sodom, I have lifted up my hand unto Jehovah, God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth,

units.leftText: that I will not accept even a thread, or a strap of a sandal, or anything that belongs to you, lest you should say, ‘I have made Abram rich.’
units.rightText: that I will not take a thread nor a shoe-latchet nor aught that is thine, lest thou shouldest say, I have made Abram rich:

units.leftText: I will accept nothing but what my men have eaten and the share for the men who went with me— Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. They may take their portion.”
units.rightText: save only that which the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men that went with me, Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre; let them take their portion.

units.leftText: After these events, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward.”
units.rightText: After these things the word of Jehovah came unto Abram in a vision, saying, Fear not, Abram: I am thy shield, and thy exceeding great reward.

units.leftText: But Abram replied, “O Lord GOD, what can You give me, since I remain childless, and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?”
units.rightText: And Abram said, O Lord Jehovah, what wilt thou give me, seeing I go childless, and he that shall be possessor of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?

units.leftText: Abram continued, “Behold, You have given me no offspring, so a servant in my household will be my heir.”
units.rightText: And Abram said, Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and, lo, one born in my house is mine heir.

units.leftText: Then the word of the LORD came to Abram, saying, “This one will not be your heir, but one who comes from your own body will be your heir.”
units.rightText: And, behold, the word of Jehovah came unto him, saying, This man shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir.

units.leftText: And the LORD took him outside and said, “Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able.” Then He told him, “So shall your offspring be.”
units.rightText: And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and number the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.
leftNotes: 15:5 Cited in Romans 4:18|ROM 4:18*

units.leftText: Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
units.rightText: And he believed in Jehovah; and he reckoned it to him for righteousness.
leftNotes: 15:6 Cited in Romans 4:3|ROM 4:3*, Romans 4:22, Galatians 3:6, and James 2:23

units.leftText: The LORD also told him, “I am the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess.” God Confirms His Promise (Numbers 34:1–15|NUM 34:1-15*; Romans 4:13–25|ROM 4:13-25*)
units.rightText: And he said unto him, I am Jehovah that brought thee out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give thee this land to inherit it.

units.leftText: But Abram replied, “Lord GOD, how can I know that I will possess it?”
units.rightText: And he said, O Lord Jehovah, whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?

units.leftText: And the LORD said to him, “Bring Me a heifer, a goat, and a ram, each three years old, along with a turtledove and a young pigeon.”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Take me a heifer three years old, and a she-goat three years old, and a ram three years old, and a turtle-dove, and a young pigeon.

units.leftText: So Abram brought all these to Him, split each of them down the middle, and laid the halves opposite each other. The birds, however, he did not cut in half.
units.rightText: And he took him all these, and divided them in the midst, and laid each half over against the other: but the birds divided he not.

units.leftText: And the birds of prey descended on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.
units.rightText: And the birds of prey came down upon the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.

units.leftText: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and suddenly great terror and darkness overwhelmed him.
units.rightText: And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, a horror of great darkness fell upon him.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Abram, “Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not their own, and they will be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.
units.rightText: And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that thy seed shall be sojourners in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;

units.leftText: But I will judge the nation they serve as slaves, and afterward they will depart with many possessions.
units.rightText: and also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out with great substance.
leftNotes: 15:14 Cited in Acts 7:6–7|ACT 7:6-7*

units.leftText: You, however, will go to your fathers in peace and be buried at a ripe old age.
units.rightText: But thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace; thou shalt be buried in a good old age.

units.leftText: In the fourth generation your descendants will return here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete.”
units.rightText: And in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorite is not yet full.

units.leftText: When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, behold, a smoking firepot and a flaming torch appeared and passed between the halves of the carcasses.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold, a smoking furnace, and a flaming torch that passed between these pieces.

units.leftText: On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, “To your descendants I have given this land — from the river of Egypt to the great River Euphrates —
units.rightText: In that day Jehovah made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates:

units.leftText: the land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites,
units.rightText: the Kenite, and the Kenizzite, and the Kadmonite,

units.leftText: Hittites, Perizzites, Rephaites,
units.rightText: and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Rephaim,

units.leftText: Amorites, Canaanites, Girgashites, and Jebusites.”
units.rightText: and the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Girgashite, and the Jebusite.

units.leftText: Now Abram’s wife Sarai had borne him no children, but she had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar.
units.rightText: Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, bare him no children: and she had a handmaid, an Egyptian, whose name was Hagar.

units.leftText: So Sarai said to Abram, “Look now, the LORD has prevented me from bearing children. Please go to my maidservant; perhaps I can build a family by her.”
units.rightText: And Sarai said unto Abram, Behold now, Jehovah hath restrained me from bearing; go in, I pray thee, unto my handmaid; it may be that I shall obtain children by her. And Abram hearkened to the voice of Sarai.

units.leftText: So after he had lived in Canaan for ten years, his wife Sarai took her Egyptian maidservant Hagar and gave her to Abram to be his wife.
units.rightText: And Sarai, Abram’s wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her handmaid, after Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Canaan, and gave her to Abram her husband to be his wife.

units.leftText: And he slept with Hagar, and she conceived. But when Hagar realized that she was pregnant, she began to despise her mistress.
units.rightText: And he went in unto Hagar, and she conceived: and when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes.
leftNotes: 16:4 Or her mistress became despised in her sight

units.leftText: Then Sarai said to Abram, “May the wrong done to me be upon you! I delivered my servant into your arms, and ever since she saw that she was pregnant, she has treated me with contempt. May the LORD judge between you and me.”
units.rightText: And Sarai said unto Abram, My wrong be upon thee: I gave my handmaid into thy bosom; and when she saw that she had conceived, I was despised in her eyes: Jehovah judge between me and thee.

units.leftText: “Here,” said Abram, “your servant is in your hands. Do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that she fled from her.
units.rightText: But Abram said unto Sarai, Behold, thy maid is in thy hand; do to her that which is good in thine eyes. And Sarai dealt hardly with her, and she fled from her face.

units.leftText: Now the angel of the LORD found Hagar by a spring of water in the desert — the spring along the road to Shur.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur.
leftNotes: 16:7 Or Angel; also in verses 9, 10, and 11; corresponding pronouns may also be capitalized.

units.leftText: “Hagar, servant of Sarai,” he said, “where have you come from, and where are you going?” “I am running away from my mistress Sarai,” she replied.
units.rightText: And he said, Hagar, Sarai’s handmaid, whence camest thou? and whither goest thou? And she said, I am fleeing from the face of my mistress Sarai.

units.leftText: So the angel of the LORD told her, “Return to your mistress and submit to her authority.”
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah said unto her, Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands.

units.leftText: Then the angel added, “I will greatly multiply your offspring so that they will be too numerous to count.”
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah said unto her, I will greatly multiply thy seed, that it shall not be numbered for multitude.

units.leftText: The angel of the LORD proceeded: “Behold, you have conceived and will bear a son. And you shall name him Ishmael, for the LORD has heard your cry of affliction.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah said unto her, Behold, thou art with child, and shalt bear a son; and thou shalt call his name Ishmael, because Jehovah hath heard thy affliction.
leftNotes: 16:11 Ishmael means God hears.

units.leftText: He will be a wild donkey of a man, and his hand will be against everyone, and everyone’s hand against him; he will live in hostility toward all his brothers.”
units.rightText: And he shall be as a wild ass among men; his hand shall be against every man, and every man’s hand against him; and he shall dwell over against all his brethren.

units.leftText: So Hagar gave this name to the LORD who had spoken to her: “You are the God who sees me, ” for she said, “Here I have seen the One who sees me!”
units.rightText: And she called the name of Jehovah that spake unto her, Thou art a God that seeth: for she said, Have I even here looked after him that seeth me?
leftNotes: 16:13 Hebrew El-Roi

units.leftText: Therefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi. It is located between Kadesh and Bered.
units.rightText: Wherefore the well was called Beer-lahai-roi; behold, it is between Kadesh and Bered.
leftNotes: 16:14 Beer-lahai-roi means well of the Living One who sees me.

units.leftText: And Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son she had borne.
units.rightText: And Hagar bare Abram a son: and Abram called the name of his son, whom Hagar bare, Ishmael.

units.leftText: Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.
units.rightText: And Abram was fourscore and six years old, when Hagar bare Ishmael to Abram.

units.leftText: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to him and said, “I am God Almighty. Walk before Me and be blameless.
units.rightText: And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, Jehovah appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am God Almighty; walk before me, and be thou perfect.
leftNotes: 17:1 Hebrew El-Shaddai

units.leftText: I will establish My covenant between Me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly.”
units.rightText: And I will make my covenant between me and thee, and will multiply thee exceedingly.

units.leftText: Then Abram fell facedown, and God said to him,
units.rightText: And Abram fell on his face: and God talked with him, saying,

units.leftText: “As for Me, this is My covenant with you: You will be the father of many nations.
units.rightText: As for me, behold, my covenant is with thee, and thou shalt be the father of a multitude of nations.

units.leftText: No longer will you be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations.
units.rightText: Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for the father of a multitude of nations have I made thee.
leftNotes: 17:5 Abram means exalted father.
17:5 Abraham means father of many.
17:5 Cited in Romans 4:17|ROM 4:17*

units.leftText: I will make you exceedingly fruitful; I will make nations of you, and kings will descend from you.
units.rightText: And I will make thee exceeding fruitful, and I will make nations of thee, and kings shall come out of thee.

units.leftText: I will establish My covenant as an everlasting covenant between Me and you and your descendants after you, to be your God and the God of your descendants after you.
units.rightText: And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee throughout their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee and to thy seed after thee.

units.leftText: And to you and your descendants I will give the land where you are residing— all the land of Canaan— as an eternal possession; and I will be their God.” The Covenant of Circumcision
units.rightText: And I will give unto thee, and to thy seed after thee, the land of thy sojournings, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession; and I will be their God.

units.leftText: God also said to Abraham, “You must keep My covenant— you and your descendants in the generations after you.
units.rightText: And God said unto Abraham, And as for thee, thou shalt keep my covenant, thou, and thy seed after thee throughout their generations.

units.leftText: This is My covenant with you and your descendants after you, which you are to keep: Every male among you must be circumcised.
units.rightText: This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee: every male among you shall be circumcised.

units.leftText: You are to circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and this will be a sign of the covenant between Me and you.
units.rightText: And ye shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of a covenant betwixt me and you.

units.leftText: Generation after generation, every male must be circumcised when he is eight days old, including those born in your household and those purchased from a foreigner — even those who are not your offspring.
units.rightText: And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every male throughout your generations, he that is born in the house, or bought with money of any foreigner that is not of thy seed.

units.leftText: Whether they are born in your household or purchased, they must be circumcised. My covenant in your flesh will be an everlasting covenant.
units.rightText: He that is born in thy house, and he that is bought with thy money, must needs be circumcised: and my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.

units.leftText: But if any male is not circumcised, he will be cut off from his people; he has broken My covenant.”
units.rightText: And the uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.

units.leftText: Then God said to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife, do not call her Sarai, for her name is to be Sarah.
units.rightText: And God said unto Abraham, As for Sarai thy wife, thou shalt not call her name Sarai, but Sarah shall her name be.
leftNotes: 17:15 Both Sarai and Sarah mean princess; the change in spelling may reflect the difference in dialect between Ur and Canaan.

units.leftText: And I will bless her and will surely give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she will be the mother of nations; kings of peoples will descend from her.”
units.rightText: And I will bless her, and moreover I will give thee a son of her: yea, I will bless her, and she shall be a mother of nations; kings of peoples shall be of her.

units.leftText: Abraham fell facedown. Then he laughed and said to himself, “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Can Sarah give birth at the age of ninety?”
units.rightText: Then Abraham fell upon his face, and laughed, and said in his heart, Shall a child be born unto him that is a hundred years old? and shall Sarah, that is ninety years old, bear?

units.leftText: And Abraham said to God, “O that Ishmael might live under Your blessing!”
units.rightText: And Abraham said unto God, Oh that Ishmael might live before thee!

units.leftText: But God replied, “Your wife Sarah will indeed bear you a son, and you are to name him Isaac. I will establish My covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him.
units.rightText: And God said, Nay, but Sarah thy wife shall bear thee a son; and thou shalt call his name Isaac: and I will establish my covenant with him for an everlasting covenant for his seed after him.
leftNotes: 17:19 Isaac means he laughs.

units.leftText: As for Ishmael, I have heard you, and I will surely bless him; I will make him fruitful and multiply him greatly. He will become the father of twelve rulers, and I will make him into a great nation.
units.rightText: And as for Ishmael, I have heard thee: behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly; twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation.

units.leftText: But I will establish My covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time next year.”
units.rightText: But my covenant will I establish with Isaac, whom Sarah shall bear unto thee at this set time in the next year.

units.leftText: When He had finished speaking with Abraham, God went up from him.
units.rightText: And he left off talking with him, and God went up from Abraham.

units.leftText: On that very day Abraham took his son Ishmael and all those born in his household or purchased with his money— every male among the members of Abraham’s household— and he circumcised them, just as God had told him.
units.rightText: And Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all that were born in his house, and all that were bought with his money, every male among the men of Abraham’s house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the selfsame day, as God had said unto him.

units.leftText: So Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised,
units.rightText: And Abraham was ninety years old and nine, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.

units.leftText: and his son Ishmael was thirteen;
units.rightText: And Ishmael his son was thirteen years old, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.

units.leftText: Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised on the same day.
units.rightText: In the selfsame day was Abraham circumcised, and Ishmael his son.

units.leftText: And all the men of Abraham’s household— both servants born in his household and those purchased from foreigners— were circumcised with him.
units.rightText: And all the men of his house, those born in the house, and those bought with money of a foreigner, were circumcised with him.

units.leftText: Then the LORD appeared to Abraham by the Oaks of Mamre in the heat of the day, while he was sitting at the entrance of his tent.
units.rightText: And Jehovah appeared unto him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day;
leftNotes: 18:1 Or Terebinths or Great Trees

units.leftText: And Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he ran from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground.
units.rightText: and he lifted up his eyes and looked, and, lo, three men stood over against him: and when he saw them, he ran to meet them from the tent door, and bowed himself to the earth,

units.leftText: “My lord,” said Abraham, “if I have found favor in your sight, please do not pass your servant by.
units.rightText: and said, My lord, if now I have found favor in thy sight, pass not away, I pray thee, from thy servant:

units.leftText: Let a little water be brought, that you may wash your feet and rest yourselves under the tree.
units.rightText: let now a little water be fetched, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree:

units.leftText: And I will bring a bit of bread so that you may refresh yourselves. This is why you have passed your servant’s way. After that, you may continue on your way.” “Yes,” they replied, “you may do as you have said.”
units.rightText: and I will fetch a morsel of bread, and strengthen ye your heart; after that ye shall pass on: forasmuch as ye are come to your servant. And they said, So do, as thou hast said.

units.leftText: So Abraham hurried into the tent and said to Sarah, “Quick! Prepare three seahs of fine flour, knead it, and bake some bread.”
units.rightText: And Abraham hastened into the tent unto Sarah, and said, Make ready quickly three measures of fine meal, knead it, and make cakes.
leftNotes: 18:6 3 seahs is approximately 19.8 dry quarts or 21.9 liters (probably about 24.5 pounds or 11.1 kilograms of flour).

units.leftText: Meanwhile, Abraham ran to the herd, selected a tender and choice calf, and gave it to a servant, who hurried to prepare it.
units.rightText: And Abraham ran unto the herd, and fetched a calf tender and good, and gave it unto the servant; and he hasted to dress it.

units.leftText: Then Abraham brought curds and milk and the calf that had been prepared, and he set them before the men and stood by them under the tree as they ate. Sarah Laughs at the Promise
units.rightText: And he took butter, and milk, and the calf which he had dressed, and set it before them; and he stood by them under the tree, and they did eat.

units.leftText: “Where is your wife Sarah?” they asked. “There, in the tent,” he replied.
units.rightText: And they said unto him, Where is Sarah thy wife? And he said, Behold, in the tent.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said, “I will surely return to you at this time next year, and your wife Sarah will have a son!”
units.rightText: And he said, I will certainly return unto thee when the season cometh round; and, lo, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard in the tent door, which was behind him.

units.leftText: And Abraham and Sarah were already old and well along in years; Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.
units.rightText: Now Abraham and Sarah were old, and well stricken in age; it had ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women.

units.leftText: So she laughed to herself, saying, “After I am worn out and my master is old, will I now have this pleasure?”
units.rightText: And Sarah laughed within herself, saying, After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?

units.leftText: And the LORD asked Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh and say, ‘Can I really bear a child when I am old?’
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Abraham, Wherefore did Sarah laugh, saying, Shall I of a surety bear a child, who am old?

units.leftText: Is anything too difficult for the LORD? At the appointed time I will return to you — in about a year — and Sarah will have a son.”
units.rightText: Is anything too hard for Jehovah? At the set time I will return unto thee, when the season cometh round, and Sarah shall have a son.
leftNotes: 18:14 Cited in Romans 9:9|ROM 9:9*

units.leftText: But Sarah was afraid, so she denied it and said, “I did not laugh.” “No,” replied the LORD, “but you did laugh.” Abraham Intercedes for Sodom
units.rightText: Then Sarah denied, saying, I laughed not; for she was afraid. And he said, Nay; but thou didst laugh.

units.leftText: When the men got up to leave, they looked out over Sodom, and Abraham walked along with them to see them off.
units.rightText: And the men rose up from thence, and looked toward Sodom: and Abraham went with them to bring them on the way.

units.leftText: And the LORD said, “Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, Shall I hide from Abraham that which I do;

units.leftText: Abraham will surely become a great and powerful nation, and through him all the nations of the earth will be blessed.
units.rightText: seeing that Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him?

units.leftText: For I have chosen him, so that he will command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing what is right and just, in order that the LORD may bring upon Abraham what He has promised.”
units.rightText: For I have known him, to the end that he may command his children and his household after him, that they may keep the way of Jehovah, to do righteousness and justice; to the end that Jehovah may bring upon Abraham that which he hath spoken of him.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said, “The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great. Because their sin is so grievous,
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, Because the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and because their sin is very grievous;

units.leftText: I will go down to see if their actions fully justify the outcry that has reached Me. If not, I will find out.”
units.rightText: I will go down now, and see whether they have done altogether according to the cry of it, which is come unto me; and if not, I will know.

units.leftText: And the two men turned away and went toward Sodom, but Abraham remained standing before the LORD.
units.rightText: And the men turned from thence, and went toward Sodom: but Abraham stood yet before Jehovah.

units.leftText: Abraham stepped forward and said, “Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
units.rightText: And Abraham drew near, and said, Wilt thou consume the righteous with the wicked?

units.leftText: What if there are fifty righteous ones in the city? Will You really sweep it away and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous ones who are there?
units.rightText: Peradventure there are fifty righteous within the city: wilt thou consume and not spare the place for the fifty righteous that are therein?

units.leftText: Far be it from You to do such a thing — to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous and the wicked are treated alike. Far be it from You! Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?”
units.rightText: That be far from thee to do after this manner, to slay the righteous with the wicked, that so the righteous should be as the wicked; that be far from thee: shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?

units.leftText: So the LORD replied, “If I find fifty righteous ones within the city of Sodom, on their account I will spare the whole place.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare all the place for their sake.

units.leftText: Then Abraham answered, “Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord— though I am but dust and ashes—
units.rightText: And Abraham answered and said, Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord, who am but dust and ashes:

units.leftText: suppose the fifty righteous ones lack five. Will You destroy the whole city for the lack of five?” He replied, “If I find forty-five there, I will not destroy it.”
units.rightText: peradventure there shall lack five of the fifty righteous: wilt thou destroy all the city for lack of five? And he said, I will not destroy it, if I find there forty and five.

units.leftText: Once again Abraham spoke to the LORD, “Suppose forty are found there?” He answered, “On account of the forty, I will not do it.”
units.rightText: And he spake unto him yet again, and said, Peradventure there shall be forty found there. And he said, I will not do it for the forty’s sake.

units.leftText: Then Abraham said, “May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak further. Suppose thirty are found there?” He replied, “If I find thirty there, I will not do it.”
units.rightText: And he said, Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak: peradventure there shall thirty be found there. And he said, I will not do it, if I find thirty there.

units.leftText: And Abraham said, “Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord, suppose twenty are found there?” He answered, “On account of the twenty, I will not destroy it.”
units.rightText: And he said, Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak unto the Lord: peradventure there shall be twenty found there. And he said, I will not destroy it for the twenty’s sake.

units.leftText: Finally, Abraham said, “May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak once more. Suppose ten are found there?” And He answered, “On account of the ten, I will not destroy it.”
units.rightText: And he said, Oh let not the Lord be angry, and I will speak yet but this once: peradventure ten shall be found there. And he said, I will not destroy it for the ten’s sake.

units.leftText: When the LORD had finished speaking with Abraham, He departed, and Abraham returned home.
units.rightText: And Jehovah went his way, as soon as he had left off communing with Abraham: and Abraham returned unto his place.

units.leftText: Now the two angels arrived at Sodom in the evening, and Lot was sitting in the gateway of the city. When Lot saw them, he got up to meet them, bowed facedown,
units.rightText: And the two angels came to Sodom at even; and Lot sat in the gate of Sodom: and Lot saw them, and rose up to meet them; and he bowed himself with his face to the earth;

units.leftText: and said, “My lords, please turn aside into the house of your servant; wash your feet and spend the night. Then you can rise early and go on your way.” “No,” they answered, “we will spend the night in the square.”
units.rightText: and he said, Behold now, my lords, turn aside, I pray you, into your servant’s house, and tarry all night, and wash your feet, and ye shall rise up early, and go on your way. And they said, Nay; but we will abide in the street all night.

units.leftText: But Lot insisted so strongly that they followed him into his house. He prepared a feast for them and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
units.rightText: And he urged them greatly; and they turned in unto him, and entered into his house; and he made them a feast, and did bake unleavened bread, and they did eat.

units.leftText: Before they had gone to bed, all the men of the city of Sodom, both young and old, surrounded the house.
units.rightText: But before they lay down, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, compassed the house round, both young and old, all the people from every quarter;

units.leftText: They called out to Lot, saying, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Send them out to us so we can have relations with them!”
units.rightText: and they called unto Lot, and said unto him, Where are the men that came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them.

units.leftText: Lot went outside to meet them, shutting the door behind him.
units.rightText: And Lot went out unto them to the door, and shut the door after him.

units.leftText: “Please, my brothers,” he pleaded, “don’t do such a wicked thing!
units.rightText: And he said, I pray you, my brethren, do not so wickedly.

units.leftText: Look, I have two daughters who have never slept with a man. Let me bring them to you, and you can do to them as you please. But do not do anything to these men, for they have come under the protection of my roof.”
units.rightText: Behold now, I have two daughters that have not known man; let me, I pray you, bring them out unto you, and do ye to them as is good in your eyes: only unto these men do nothing, forasmuch as they are come under the shadow of my roof.

units.leftText: “Get out of the way!” they replied. And they declared, “This one came here as a foreigner, and he is already acting like a judge! Now we will treat you worse than them.” And they pressed in on Lot and moved in to break down the door.
units.rightText: And they said, Stand back. And they said, This one fellow came in to sojourn, and he will needs be a judge: now will we deal worse with thee, than with them. And they pressed sore upon the man, even Lot, and drew near to break the door.

units.leftText: But the men inside reached out, pulled Lot into the house with them, and shut the door.
units.rightText: But the men put forth their hand, and brought Lot into the house to them, and shut to the door.

units.leftText: And they struck the men at the entrance, young and old, with blindness, so that they wearied themselves trying to find the door. Lot Flees to Zoar
units.rightText: And they smote the men that were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great, so that they wearied themselves to find the door.

units.leftText: Then the two men said to Lot, “Do you have anyone else here — a son-in-law, your sons or daughters, or anyone else in the city who belongs to you? Get them out of here,
units.rightText: And the men said unto Lot, Hast thou here any besides? son-in-law, and thy sons, and thy daughters, and whomsoever thou hast in the city, bring them out of the place:

units.leftText: because we are about to destroy this place. For the outcry to the LORD against its people is so great that He has sent us to destroy it.”
units.rightText: for we will destroy this place, because the cry of them is waxed great before Jehovah; and Jehovah hath sent us to destroy it.

units.leftText: So Lot went out and spoke to the sons-in-law who were pledged in marriage to his daughters. “Get up,” he said. “Get out of this place, for the LORD is about to destroy the city!” But his sons-in-law thought he was joking.
units.rightText: And Lot went out, and spake unto his sons-in-law, who married his daughters, and said, Up, get you out of this place; for Jehovah will destroy the city. But he seemed unto his sons-in-law as one that mocked.

units.leftText: At daybreak the angels hurried Lot along, saying, “Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you will be swept away in the punishment of the city.”
units.rightText: And when the morning arose, then the angels hastened Lot, saying, Arise, take thy wife, and thy two daughters that are here, lest thou be consumed in the iniquity of the city.

units.leftText: But when Lot hesitated, the men grabbed his hand and the hands of his wife and his two daughters. And they led them safely out of the city, because of the LORD’s compassion for them.
units.rightText: But he lingered; and the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters, Jehovah being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city.

units.leftText: As soon as the men had brought them out, one of them said, “Run for your lives! Do not look back, and do not stop anywhere on the plain! Flee to the mountains, or you will be swept away!”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he said, Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the Plain; escape to the mountain, lest thou be consumed.

units.leftText: But Lot replied, “No, my lords, please!
units.rightText: And Lot said unto them, Oh, not so, my lord:

units.leftText: Your servant has indeed found favor in your sight, and you have shown me great kindness by sparing my life. But I cannot run to the mountains; the disaster will overtake me, and I will die.
units.rightText: behold now, thy servant hath found favor in thy sight, and thou hast magnified thy lovingkindness, which thou hast showed unto me in saving my life; and I cannot escape to the mountain, lest evil overtake me, and I die:

units.leftText: Look, there is a town nearby where I can flee, and it is a small place. Please let me flee there — is it not a small place? Then my life will be saved.”
units.rightText: behold now, this city is near to flee unto, and it is a little one. Oh let me escape thither (is it not a little one?), and my soul shall live.

units.leftText: “Very well,” he answered, “I will grant this request as well, and will not demolish the town you indicate.
units.rightText: And he said unto him, See, I have accepted thee concerning this thing also, that I will not overthrow the city of which thou hast spoken.

units.leftText: Hurry! Run there quickly, for I cannot do anything until you reach it.” That is why the town was called Zoar.
units.rightText: Haste thee, escape thither; for I cannot do anything till thou be come thither. Therefore the name of the city was called Zoar.
leftNotes: 19:22 Zoar means small.

units.leftText: And by the time the sun had risen over the land, Lot had reached Zoar. The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah (Luke 17:20–37|LUK 17:20-37*)
units.rightText: The sun was risen upon the earth when Lot came unto Zoar.

units.leftText: Then the LORD rained down sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah — from the LORD out of the heavens.
units.rightText: Then Jehovah rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Jehovah out of heaven;

units.leftText: Thus He destroyed these cities and the entire plain, including all the inhabitants of the cities and everything that grew on the ground.
units.rightText: and he overthrew those cities, and all the Plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.

units.leftText: But Lot’s wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.
units.rightText: But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.

units.leftText: Early the next morning, Abraham got up and returned to the place where he had stood before the LORD.
units.rightText: And Abraham gat up early in the morning to the place where he had stood before Jehovah:

units.leftText: He looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and all the land of the plain, and he saw the smoke rising from the land like smoke from a furnace.
units.rightText: and he looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and toward all the land of the Plain, and beheld, and, lo, the smoke of the land went up as the smoke of a furnace.

units.leftText: So when God destroyed the cities of the plain, He remembered Abraham, and He brought Lot out of the catastrophe that destroyed the cities where he had lived. Lot and His Daughters
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when God destroyed the cities of the Plain, that God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow, when he overthrew the cities in which Lot dwelt.

units.leftText: Lot and his two daughters left Zoar and settled in the mountains — for he was afraid to stay in Zoar — where they lived in a cave.
units.rightText: And Lot went up out of Zoar, and dwelt in the mountain, and his two daughters with him; for he feared to dwell in Zoar: and he dwelt in a cave, he and his two daughters.

units.leftText: One day the older daughter said to the younger, “Our father is old, and there is no man in the land to sleep with us, as is the custom over all the earth.
units.rightText: And the first-born said unto the younger, Our father is old, and there is not a man in the earth to come in unto us after the manner of all the earth:

units.leftText: Come, let us get our father drunk with wine so we can sleep with him and preserve his line.”
units.rightText: come, let us make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, that we may preserve seed of our father.

units.leftText: So that night they got their father drunk with wine, and the firstborn went in and slept with her father; he was not aware when she lay down or when she got up.
units.rightText: And they made their father drink wine that night: and the first-born went in, and lay with her father; and he knew not when she lay down, nor when she arose.

units.leftText: The next day the older daughter said to the younger, “Look, I slept with my father last night. Let us get him drunk with wine again tonight so you can go in and sleep with him and we can preserve our father’s line.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the morrow, that the first-born said unto the younger, Behold, I lay yesternight with my father: let us make him drink wine this night also; and go thou in, and lie with him, that we may preserve seed of our father.

units.leftText: So again that night they got their father drunk with wine, and the younger daughter went in and slept with him; he was not aware when she lay down or when she got up.
units.rightText: And they made their father drink wine that night also: and the younger arose, and lay with him; and he knew not when she lay down, nor when she arose.

units.leftText: Thus both of Lot’s daughters became pregnant by their father.
units.rightText: Thus were both the daughters of Lot with child by their father.

units.leftText: The older daughter gave birth to a son and named him Moab. He is the father of the Moabites of today.
units.rightText: And the first-born bare a son, and called his name Moab: the same is the father of the Moabites unto this day.
leftNotes: 19:37 Moab sounds like the Hebrew for from my father.

units.leftText: The younger daughter also gave birth to a son, and she named him Ben-ammi. He is the father of the Ammonites of today.
units.rightText: And the younger, she also bare a son, and called his name Ben-ammi: the same is the father of the children of Ammon unto this day.
leftNotes: 19:38 Ben-ammi means son of my people.

units.leftText: Now Abraham journeyed from there to the region of the Negev and settled between Kadesh and Shur. While he was staying in Gerar,
units.rightText: And Abraham journeyed from thence toward the land of the South, and dwelt between Kadesh and Shur; and he sojourned in Gerar.

units.leftText: Abraham said of his wife Sarah, “She is my sister.” So Abimelech king of Gerar had Sarah brought to him.
units.rightText: And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, She is my sister: and Abimelech king of Gerar sent, and took Sarah.

units.leftText: One night, however, God came to Abimelech in a dream and told him, “You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken, for she is a married woman.”
units.rightText: But God came to Abimelech in a dream of the night, and said to him, Behold, thou art but a dead man, because of the woman whom thou hast taken; for she is a man’s wife.

units.leftText: Now Abimelech had not gone near her, so he replied, “Lord, would You destroy a nation even though it is innocent?
units.rightText: Now Abimelech had not come near her: and he said, Lord, wilt thou slay even a righteous nation?

units.leftText: Didn’t Abraham tell me, ‘She is my sister’? And she herself said, ‘He is my brother.’ I have done this in the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands.”
units.rightText: Said he not himself unto me, She is my sister? and she, even she herself said, He is my brother: in the integrity of my heart and the innocency of my hands have I done this.

units.leftText: Then God said to Abimelech in the dream, “Yes, I know that you did this with a clear conscience, and so I have kept you from sinning against Me. That is why I did not let you touch her.
units.rightText: And God said unto him in the dream, Yea, I know that in the integrity of thy heart thou hast done this, and I also withheld thee from sinning against me: therefore suffered I thee not to touch her.

units.leftText: Now return the man’s wife, for he is a prophet; he will pray for you and you will live. But if you do not restore her, be aware that you will surely die — you and all who belong to you.”
units.rightText: Now therefore restore the man’s wife; for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live: and if thou restore her not, know thou that thou shalt surely die, thou, and all that are thine.

units.leftText: Early the next morning Abimelech got up and summoned all his servants; and when he described to them all that had happened, the men were terrified.
units.rightText: And Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and told all these things in their ears: and the men were sore afraid.

units.leftText: Then Abimelech called Abraham and asked, “What have you done to us? How have I sinned against you, that you have brought such tremendous guilt upon me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should not be done.”
units.rightText: Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said unto him, What hast thou done unto us? and wherein have I sinned against thee, that thou hast brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? thou hast done deeds unto me that ought not to be done.

units.leftText: Abimelech also asked Abraham, “What prompted you to do such a thing?”
units.rightText: And Abimelech said unto Abraham, What sawest thou, that thou hast done this thing?

units.leftText: Abraham replied, “I thought to myself, ‘Surely there is no fear of God in this place. They will kill me on account of my wife.’
units.rightText: And Abraham said, Because I thought, Surely the fear of God is not in this place; and they will slay me for my wife’s sake.

units.leftText: Besides, she really is my sister, the daughter of my father — though not the daughter of my mother — and she became my wife.
units.rightText: And moreover she is indeed my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife:

units.leftText: So when God had me journey from my father’s house, I said to Sarah, ‘This is how you can show your loyalty to me: Wherever we go, say of me, “He is my brother.”’”
units.rightText: and it came to pass, when God caused me to wander from my father’s house, that I said unto her, This is thy kindness which thou shalt show unto me: at every place whither we shall come, say of me, He is my brother.

units.leftText: So Abimelech brought sheep and cattle, menservants and maidservants, and he gave them to Abraham and restored his wife Sarah to him.
units.rightText: And Abimelech took sheep and oxen, and men-servants and women-servants, and gave them unto Abraham, and restored him Sarah his wife.

units.leftText: And Abimelech said, “Look, my land is before you. Settle wherever you please.”
units.rightText: And Abimelech said, Behold, my land is before thee: dwell where it pleaseth thee.

units.leftText: And he said to Sarah, “See, I am giving your brother a thousand pieces of silver. It is your vindication before all who are with you; you are completely cleared.”
units.rightText: And unto Sarah he said, Behold, I have given thy brother a thousand pieces of silver: behold, it is for thee a covering of the eyes to all that are with thee; and in respect of all thou art righted.
leftNotes: 20:16 Or a thousand shekels of silver; that is, approximately 25.1 pounds or 11.4 kilograms of silver

units.leftText: Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech and his wife and his maidservants, so that they could again bear children —
units.rightText: And Abraham prayed unto God: and God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his maid-servants; and they bare children.

units.leftText: for on account of Abraham’s wife Sarah, the LORD had completely closed all the wombs in Abimelech’s household.
units.rightText: For Jehovah had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.

units.leftText: Now the LORD attended to Sarah as He had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what He had promised.
units.rightText: And Jehovah visited Sarah as he had said, and Jehovah did unto Sarah as he had spoken.

units.leftText: So Sarah conceived and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the very time God had promised.
units.rightText: And Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.

units.leftText: And Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore to him.
units.rightText: And Abraham called the name of his son that was born unto him, whom Sarah bare to him, Isaac.
leftNotes: 21:3 Isaac means he laughs.

units.leftText: When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him, as God had commanded him.
units.rightText: And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.

units.leftText: Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
units.rightText: And Abraham was a hundred years old, when his son Isaac was born unto him.

units.leftText: Then Sarah said, “God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears of this will laugh with me.”
units.rightText: And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh; every one that heareth will laugh with me.

units.leftText: She added, “Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.”
units.rightText: And she said, Who would have said unto Abraham, that Sarah should give children suck? for I have borne him a son in his old age.

units.leftText: So the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned. Sarah Turns against Hagar (Galatians 4:21–30|GAL 4:21-30*)
units.rightText: And the child grew, and was weaned: and Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac was weaned.

units.leftText: But Sarah saw that the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham was mocking her son,
units.rightText: And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne unto Abraham, mocking.
leftNotes: 21:9 LXX and Vulgate; Hebrew lacks her son

units.leftText: and she said to Abraham, “Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with my son Isaac!”
units.rightText: Wherefore she said unto Abraham, Cast out this handmaid and her son: for the son of this handmaid shall not be heir with my son, even with Isaac.
leftNotes: 21:10 Cited in Galatians 4:30|GAL 4:30*

units.leftText: Now this matter distressed Abraham greatly because it concerned his son Ishmael.
units.rightText: And the thing was very grievous in Abraham’s sight on account of his son.

units.leftText: But God said to Abraham, “Do not be distressed about the boy and your maidservant. Listen to everything that Sarah tells you, for through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.
units.rightText: And God said unto Abraham, Let it not be grievous in thy sight because of the lad, and because of thy handmaid; in all that Sarah saith unto thee, hearken unto her voice; for in Isaac shall thy seed be called.
leftNotes: 21:12 Cited in Romans 9:7|ROM 9:7* and Hebrews 11:18

units.leftText: But I will also make a nation of the slave woman’s son, because he is your offspring.”
units.rightText: And also of the son of the handmaid will I make a nation, because he is thy seed.

units.leftText: Early in the morning, Abraham got up, took bread and a skin of water, put them on Hagar’s shoulders, and sent her away with the boy. She left and wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba.
units.rightText: And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread and a bottle of water, and gave it unto Hagar, putting it on her shoulder, and gave her the child, and sent her away: and she departed, and wandered in the wilderness of Beer-sheba.

units.leftText: When the water in the skin was gone, she left the boy under one of the bushes.
units.rightText: And the water in the bottle was spent, and she cast the child under one of the shrubs.

units.leftText: Then she went off and sat down nearby, about a bowshot away, for she said, “I cannot bear to watch the boy die!” And as she sat nearby, she lifted up her voice and wept.
units.rightText: And she went, and sat her down over against him a good way off, as it were a bowshot: for she said, Let me not look upon the death of the child. And she sat over against him, and lifted up her voice, and wept.
leftNotes: 21:16 Hebrew; LXX the child lifted up his voice and wept

units.leftText: Then God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, “What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he lies.
units.rightText: And God heard the voice of the lad; and the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said unto her, What aileth thee, Hagar? fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad where he is.

units.leftText: Get up, lift up the boy, and take him by the hand, for I will make him into a great nation.”
units.rightText: Arise, lift up the lad, and hold him in thy hand; for I will make him a great nation.

units.leftText: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. So she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.
units.rightText: And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water; and she went, and filled the bottle with water, and gave the lad drink.

units.leftText: And God was with the boy, and he grew up and settled in the wilderness and became a great archer.
units.rightText: And God was with the lad, and he grew; and he dwelt in the wilderness, and became, as he grew up, an archer.

units.leftText: And while he was dwelling in the Wilderness of Paran, his mother got a wife for him from the land of Egypt. The Covenant at Beersheba
units.rightText: And he dwelt in the wilderness of Paran: and his mother took him a wife out of the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: At that time Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army said to Abraham, “God is with you in all that you do.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at that time, that Abimelech and Phicol the captain of his host spake unto Abraham, saying, God is with thee in all that thou doest:

units.leftText: Now, therefore, swear to me here before God that you will not deal falsely with me or my children or descendants. Show to me and to the country in which you reside the same kindness that I have shown to you.”
units.rightText: now therefore swear unto me here by God that thou wilt not deal falsely with me, nor with my son, nor with my son’s son: but according to the kindness that I have done unto thee, thou shalt do unto me, and to the land wherein thou hast sojourned.

units.leftText: And Abraham replied, “I swear it.”
units.rightText: And Abraham said, I will swear.

units.leftText: But when Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well that Abimelech’s servants had seized,
units.rightText: And Abraham reproved Abimelech because of the well of water, which Abimelech’s servants had violently taken away.

units.leftText: Abimelech replied, “I do not know who has done this. You did not tell me, so I have not heard about it until today.”
units.rightText: And Abimelech said, I know not who hath done this thing: neither didst thou tell me, neither yet heard I of it, but to-day.

units.leftText: So Abraham brought sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two men made a covenant.
units.rightText: And Abraham took sheep and oxen, and gave them unto Abimelech; and they two made a covenant.

units.leftText: Abraham separated seven ewe lambs from the flock,
units.rightText: And Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves.

units.leftText: and Abimelech asked him, “Why have you set apart these seven ewe lambs?”
units.rightText: And Abimelech said unto Abraham, What mean these seven ewe lambs which thou hast set by themselves?

units.leftText: He replied, “You are to accept the seven ewe lambs from my hand as my witness that I dug this well.”
units.rightText: And he said, These seven ewe lambs shalt thou take of my hand, that it may be a witness unto me, that I have digged this well.

units.leftText: So that place was called Beersheba, because it was there that the two of them swore an oath.
units.rightText: Wherefore he called that place Beer-sheba; because there they sware both of them.
leftNotes: 21:31 Beersheba means well of seven or well of the oath.

units.leftText: After they had made the covenant at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army got up and returned to the land of the Philistines.
units.rightText: So they made a covenant at Beer-sheba: and Abimelech rose up, and Phicol the captain of his host, and they returned into the land of the Philistines.

units.leftText: And Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called upon the name of the LORD, the Eternal God.
units.rightText: And Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beer-sheba, and called there on the name of Jehovah, the Everlasting God.
leftNotes: 21:33 Hebrew El-Olam

units.leftText: And Abraham resided in the land of the Philistines for a long time.
units.rightText: And Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days.

units.leftText: Some time later God tested Abraham and said to him, “Abraham!” “Here I am,” he answered.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after these things, that God did prove Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham; and he said, Here am I.

units.leftText: “Take your son,” God said, “your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains, which I will show you.”
units.rightText: And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son, whom thou lovest, even Isaac, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt-offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.

units.leftText: So Abraham got up early the next morning, saddled his donkey, and took along two of his servants and his son Isaac. He split the wood for a burnt offering and set out for the place God had designated.
units.rightText: And Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son; and he clave the wood for the burnt-offering, and rose up, and went unto the place of which God had told him.

units.leftText: On the third day Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.
units.rightText: On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place afar off.

units.leftText: “Stay here with the donkey,” Abraham told his servants. “The boy and I will go over there to worship, and then we will return to you.”
units.rightText: And Abraham said unto his young men, Abide ye here with the ass, and I and the lad will go yonder; and we will worship, and come again to you.

units.leftText: Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac. He himself carried the fire and the sacrificial knife, and the two of them walked on together.
