units.rightText: And Abraham took the wood of the burnt-offering, and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he took in his hand the fire and the knife; and they went both of them together.

units.leftText: Then Isaac said to his father Abraham, “My father!” “Here I am, my son,” he replied. “The fire and the wood are here,” said Isaac, “but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?”
units.rightText: And Isaac spake unto Abraham his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I, my son. And he said, Behold, the fire and the wood: but where is the lamb for a burnt-offering?

units.leftText: Abraham answered, “God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.” And the two walked on together.
units.rightText: And Abraham said, God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt-offering, my son: so they went both of them together.

units.leftText: When they arrived at the place God had designated, Abraham built the altar there and arranged the wood. He bound his son Isaac and placed him on the altar, atop the wood.
units.rightText: And they came to the place which God had told him of; and Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, upon the wood.

units.leftText: Then Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son. The LORD Provides the Sacrifice
units.rightText: And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.

units.leftText: Just then the angel of the LORD called out to him from heaven, “Abraham, Abraham!” “Here I am,” he replied.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah called unto him out of heaven, and said, Abraham, Abraham: and he said, Here am I.
leftNotes: 22:11 Or Angel; also in verses 12 and 15

units.leftText: “Do not lay a hand on the boy or do anything to him,” said the angel, “for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your only son from me. ”
units.rightText: And he said, Lay not thy hand upon the lad, neither do thou anything unto him; for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son, from me.
leftNotes: 22:12 Or from Me

units.leftText: Then Abraham looked up and saw behind him a ram in a thicket, caught by its horns. So he went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
units.rightText: And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, behind him a ram caught in the thicket by his horns: and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt-offering in the stead of his son.
leftNotes: 22:13 Most MT manuscripts; other Hebrew manuscripts, SP, LXX, and Syriac saw one ram

units.leftText: And Abraham called that place The LORD Will Provide. So to this day it is said, “On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided.”
units.rightText: And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah-jireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of Jehovah it shall be provided.
leftNotes: 22:14 Hebrew YHWH Yireh

units.leftText: And the angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time,
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah called unto Abraham a second time out of heaven,

units.leftText: saying, “By Myself I have sworn, declares the LORD, that because you have done this and have not withheld your only son,
units.rightText: and said, By myself have I sworn, saith Jehovah, because thou hast done this thing, and hast not withheld thy son, thine only son,

units.leftText: I will surely bless you, and I will multiply your descendants like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will possess the gates of their enemies.
units.rightText: that in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heavens, and as the sand which is upon the sea-shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies;
leftNotes: 22:17 Cited in Hebrews 6:14|HEB 6:14*

units.leftText: And through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed My voice.”
units.rightText: and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice.
leftNotes: 22:18 Cited in Acts 3:25|ACT 3:25*

units.leftText: Abraham went back to his servants, and they got up and set out together for Beersheba. And Abraham settled in Beersheba. The Sons of Nahor
units.rightText: So Abraham returned unto his young men, and they rose up and went together to Beer-sheba; and Abraham dwelt at Beer-sheba.

units.leftText: Some time later, Abraham was told, “Milcah has also borne sons to your brother Nahor:
units.rightText: And it came to pass after these things, that it was told Abraham, saying, Behold, Milcah, she also hath borne children unto thy brother Nahor:

units.leftText: Uz the firstborn, his brother Buz, Kemuel (the father of Aram),
units.rightText: Uz his first-born, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,

units.leftText: Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
units.rightText: and Chesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel.

units.leftText: And Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. Milcah bore these eight sons to Abraham’s brother Nahor.
units.rightText: And Bethuel begat Rebekah: these eight did Milcah bear to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.

units.leftText: Moreover, Nahor’s concubine, whose name was Reumah, bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
units.rightText: And his concubine, whose name was Reumah, she also bare Tebah, and Gaham, and Tahash, and Maacah.

units.leftText: Now Sarah lived to be 127 years old.
units.rightText: And the life of Sarah was a hundred and seven and twenty years: these were the years of the life of Sarah.

units.leftText: She died in Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham went out to mourn and to weep for her.
units.rightText: And Sarah died in Kiriath-arba (the same is Hebron), in the land of Canaan: and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her.

units.leftText: Then Abraham got up from beside his dead wife and said to the Hittites,
units.rightText: And Abraham rose up from before his dead, and spake unto the children of Heth, saying,
leftNotes: 23:3 Or sons of Heth; also in verses 5, 7, 10, 16, 18, and 20

units.leftText: “I am a foreigner and an outsider among you. Give me a burial site among you so that I can bury my dead.”
units.rightText: I am a stranger and a sojourner with you: give me a possession of a burying-place with you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.

units.leftText: The Hittites replied to Abraham,
units.rightText: And the children of Heth answered Abraham, saying unto him,

units.leftText: “Listen to us, sir. You are God’s chosen one among us. Bury your dead in the finest of our tombs. None of us will withhold his tomb for burying your dead.”
units.rightText: Hear us, my lord; thou art a prince of God among us: in the choice of our sepulchres bury thy dead; none of us shall withhold from thee his sepulchre, but that thou mayest bury thy dead.

units.leftText: Then Abraham rose and bowed down before the people of the land, the Hittites.
units.rightText: And Abraham rose up, and bowed himself to the people of the land, even to the children of Heth.

units.leftText: “If you are willing for me to bury my dead,” he said to them, “listen to me, and approach Ephron son of Zohar on my behalf
units.rightText: And he communed with them, saying, If it be your mind that I should bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and entreat for me to Ephron the son of Zohar,

units.leftText: to sell me the cave of Machpelah that belongs to him; it is at the end of his field. Let him sell it to me in your presence for full price, so that I may have a burial site.”
units.rightText: that he may give me the cave of Machpelah, which he hath, which is in the end of his field; for the full price let him give it to me in the midst of you for a possession of a burying-place.

units.leftText: Now Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth. So in the presence of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city, Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham,
units.rightText: Now Ephron was sitting in the midst of the children of Heth: and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the audience of the children of Heth, even of all that went in at the gate of his city, saying,

units.leftText: “No, my lord. Listen to me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. I give it to you in the presence of my people. Bury your dead.”
units.rightText: Nay, my lord, hear me: the field give I thee, and the cave that is therein, I give it thee; in the presence of the children of my people give I it thee: bury thy dead.

units.leftText: Again Abraham bowed down before the people of the land
units.rightText: And Abraham bowed himself down before the people of the land.

units.leftText: and said to Ephron in their presence, “If you will please listen to me, I will pay you the price of the field. Accept it from me, so that I may bury my dead there.”
units.rightText: And he spake unto Ephron in the audience of the people of the land, saying, But if thou wilt, I pray thee, hear me: I will give the price of the field; take it of me, and I will bury my dead there.

units.leftText: Ephron answered Abraham,
units.rightText: And Ephron answered Abraham, saying unto him,

units.leftText: “Listen to me, my lord. The land is worth four hundred shekels of silver, but what is that between you and me? Bury your dead.”
units.rightText: My lord, hearken unto me: a piece of land worth four hundred shekels of silver, what is that betwixt me and thee? bury therefore thy dead.
leftNotes: 23:15 400 shekels is approximately 10.1 pounds or 4.6 kilograms of silver; also in verse 16.

units.leftText: Abraham agreed to Ephron’s terms and weighed out for him the price he had named in the hearing of the Hittites: four hundred shekels of silver, according to the standard of the merchants.
units.rightText: And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron; and Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver which he had named in the audience of the children of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant.

units.leftText: So Ephron’s field at Machpelah near Mamre, the cave that was in it, and all the trees within the boundaries of the field were deeded over
units.rightText: So the field of Ephron, which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field, and the cave which was therein, and all the trees that were in the field, that were in all the border thereof round about, were made sure

units.leftText: to Abraham’s possession in the presence of all the Hittites who had come to the gate of his city.
units.rightText: unto Abraham for a possession in the presence of the children of Heth, before all that went in at the gate of his city.

units.leftText: After this, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah near Mamre (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre (the same is Hebron), in the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: So the field and its cave were deeded by the Hittites to Abraham as a burial site.
units.rightText: And the field, and the cave that is therein, were made sure unto Abraham for a possession of a burying-place by the children of Heth.

units.leftText: By now Abraham was old and well along in years, and the LORD had blessed him in every way.
units.rightText: And Abraham was old, and well stricken in age: and Jehovah had blessed Abraham in all things.

units.leftText: So Abraham instructed the chief servant of his household, who managed all he owned, “Place your hand under my thigh,
units.rightText: And Abraham said unto his servant, the elder of his house, that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh:

units.leftText: and I will have you swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites among whom I am dwelling,
units.rightText: and I will make thee swear by Jehovah, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that thou wilt not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell:

units.leftText: but will go to my country and my kindred to take a wife for my son Isaac.”
units.rightText: but thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son Isaac.

units.leftText: The servant asked him, “What if the woman is unwilling to follow me to this land? Shall I then take your son back to the land from which you came?”
units.rightText: And the servant said unto him, Peradventure the woman will not be willing to follow me unto this land: must I needs bring thy son again unto the land from whence thou camest?

units.leftText: Abraham replied, “Make sure that you do not take my son back there.
units.rightText: And Abraham said unto him, Beware thou that thou bring not my son thither again.

units.leftText: The LORD, the God of heaven, who brought me from my father’s house and my native land, who spoke to me and promised me on oath, saying, ‘To your offspring I will give this land’— He will send His angel before you so that you can take a wife for my son from there.
units.rightText: Jehovah, the God of heaven, who took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my nativity, and who spake unto me, and who sware unto me, saying, Unto thy seed will I give this land; he will send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take a wife for my son from thence.

units.leftText: And if the woman is unwilling to follow you, then you are released from this oath of mine. Only do not take my son back there.”
units.rightText: And if the woman be not willing to follow thee, then thou shalt be clear from this my oath; only thou shalt not bring my son thither again.

units.leftText: So the servant placed his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and swore an oath to him concerning this matter.
units.rightText: And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and sware to him concerning this matter.

units.leftText: Then the servant took ten of his master’s camels and departed with all manner of good things from his master in hand. And he set out for Nahor’s hometown in Aram-naharaim.
units.rightText: And the servant took ten camels, of the camels of his master, and departed, having all goodly things of his master’s in his hand: and he arose, and went to Mesopotamia, unto the city of Nahor.
leftNotes: 24:10 That is, Mesopotamia; Aram-naharaim means Aram of the two rivers, likely the region between the Euphrates and Balih Rivers in northwestern Mesopotamia.

units.leftText: As evening approached, he made the camels kneel down near the well outside the town at the time when the women went out to draw water.
units.rightText: And he made the camels to kneel down without the city by the well of water at the time of evening, the time that women go out to draw water.

units.leftText: “O LORD, God of my master Abraham,” he prayed, “please grant me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham.
units.rightText: And he said, O Jehovah, the God of my master Abraham, send me, I pray thee, good speed this day, and show kindness unto my master Abraham.

units.leftText: Here I am, standing beside the spring, and the daughters of the townspeople are coming out to draw water.
units.rightText: Behold, I am standing by the fountain of water; and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water:

units.leftText: Now may it happen that the girl to whom I say, ‘Please let down your jar that I may drink,’ and who responds, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels as well’— let her be the one You have appointed for Your servant Isaac. By this I will know that You have shown kindness to my master.” Rebekah Is Chosen
units.rightText: and let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: let the same be she that thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and thereby shall I know that thou hast showed kindness unto my master.

units.leftText: Before the servant had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham’s brother Nahor.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.

units.leftText: Now the girl was very beautiful, a virgin who had not had relations with any man. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up again.
units.rightText: And the damsel was very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her: and she went down to the fountain, and filled her pitcher, and came up.

units.leftText: So the servant ran to meet her and said, “Please let me have a little water from your jar.”
units.rightText: And the servant ran to meet her, and said, Give me to drink, I pray thee, a little water from thy pitcher.

units.leftText: “Drink, my lord,” she replied, and she quickly lowered her jar to her hands and gave him a drink.
units.rightText: And she said, Drink, my lord: and she hasted, and let down her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him drink.

units.leftText: After she had given him a drink, she said, “I will also draw water for your camels, until they have had enough to drink.”
units.rightText: And when she had done giving him drink, she said, I will draw for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.

units.leftText: And she quickly emptied her jar into the trough and ran back to the well to draw water, until she had drawn water for all his camels.
units.rightText: And she hasted, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again unto the well to draw, and drew for all his camels.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, the man watched her silently to see whether or not the LORD had made his journey a success.
units.rightText: And the man looked stedfastly on her, holding his peace, to know whether Jehovah had made his journey prosperous or not.

units.leftText: And after the camels had finished drinking, he took out a gold ring weighing a beka, and two gold bracelets for her wrists weighing ten shekels.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as the camels had done drinking, that the man took a golden ring of half a shekel weight, and two bracelets for her hands of ten shekels weight of gold,
leftNotes: 24:22 A beka is half a shekel, or approximately 0.2 ounces or 5.7 grams.
24:22 10 shekels is approximately 4 ounces or 114 grams.

units.leftText: “Whose daughter are you?” he asked. “Please tell me, is there room in your father’s house for us to spend the night?”
units.rightText: and said, Whose daughter art thou? tell me, I pray thee. Is there room in thy father’s house for us to lodge in?

units.leftText: She replied, “I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son that Milcah bore to Nahor.”
units.rightText: And she said unto him, I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, whom she bare unto Nahor.

units.leftText: Then she added, “We have plenty of straw and feed, as well as a place for you to spend the night.”
units.rightText: She said moreover unto him, We have both straw and provender enough, and room to lodge in.

units.leftText: Then the man bowed down and worshiped the LORD,
units.rightText: And the man bowed his head, and worshipped Jehovah.

units.leftText: saying, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not withheld His kindness and faithfulness from my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the journey to the house of my master’s relatives.”
units.rightText: And he said, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of my master Abraham, who hath not forsaken his lovingkindness and his truth toward my master: as for me, Jehovah hath led me in the way to the house of my master’s brethren.

units.leftText: The girl ran and told her mother’s household about these things.
units.rightText: And the damsel ran, and told her mother’s house according to these words.

units.leftText: Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and he rushed out to the man at the spring.
units.rightText: And Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban: and Laban ran out unto the man, unto the fountain.

units.leftText: As soon as he saw the ring, and the bracelets on his sister’s wrists, and heard Rebekah’s words, “The man said this to me,” he went and found the man standing by the camels near the spring.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he saw the ring, and the bracelets upon his sister’s hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, Thus spake the man unto me; that he came unto the man; and, behold, he was standing by the camels at the fountain.

units.leftText: “Come, you who are blessed by the LORD,” said Laban. “Why are you standing out here? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.”
units.rightText: And he said, Come in, thou blessed of Jehovah; wherefore standest thou without? for I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.

units.leftText: So the man came to the house, and the camels were unloaded. Straw and feed were brought to the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of his companions.
units.rightText: And the man came into the house, and he ungirded the camels; and he gave straw and provender for the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men that were with him.

units.leftText: Then a meal was set before the man, but he said, “I will not eat until I have told you what I came to say.” So Laban said, “Please speak.”
units.rightText: And there was set food before him to eat: but he said, I will not eat, until I have told mine errand. And he said, Speak on.

units.leftText: “I am Abraham’s servant,” he replied.
units.rightText: And he said, I am Abraham’s servant.

units.leftText: “The LORD has greatly blessed my master, and he has become rich. He has given him sheep and cattle, silver and gold, menservants and maidservants, camels and donkeys.
units.rightText: And Jehovah hath blessed my master greatly; and he is become great: and he hath given him flocks and herds, and silver and gold, and men-servants and maid-servants, and camels and asses.

units.leftText: My master’s wife Sarah has borne him a son in her old age, and my master has given him everything he owns.
units.rightText: And Sarah my master’s wife bare a son to my master when she was old: and unto him hath he given all that he hath.

units.leftText: My master made me swear an oath and said, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites in whose land I dwell,
units.rightText: And my master made me swear, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell:

units.leftText: but you shall go to my father’s house and to my kindred to take a wife for my son.’
units.rightText: but thou shalt go unto my father’s house, and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son.

units.leftText: Then I asked my master, ‘What if the woman will not come back with me?’
units.rightText: And I said unto my master, Peradventure the woman will not follow me.

units.leftText: And he told me, ‘The LORD, before whom I have walked, will send His angel with you and make your journey a success, so that you may take a wife for my son from my kindred and from my father’s house.
units.rightText: And he said unto me, Jehovah, before whom I walk, will send his angel with thee, and prosper thy way; and thou shalt take a wife for my son of my kindred, and of my father’s house:

units.leftText: And when you go to my kindred, if they refuse to give her to you, then you will be released from my oath.’
units.rightText: then shalt thou be clear from my oath, when thou comest to my kindred; and if they give her not to thee, thou shalt be clear from my oath.

units.leftText: So when I came to the spring today, I prayed: O LORD, God of my master Abraham, if only You would make my journey a success!
units.rightText: And I came this day unto the fountain, and said, O Jehovah, the God of my master Abraham, if now thou do prosper my way which I go:

units.leftText: Here I am, standing beside this spring. Now if a maiden comes out to draw water and I say to her, ‘Please let me drink a little water from your jar,’
units.rightText: behold, I am standing by the fountain of water; and let it come to pass, that the maiden that cometh forth to draw, to whom I shall say, Give me, I pray thee, a little water from thy pitcher to drink;

units.leftText: and she replies, ‘Drink, and I will draw water for your camels as well,’ may she be the woman the LORD has appointed for my master’s son.
units.rightText: and she shall say to me, Both drink thou, and I will also draw for thy camels: let the same be the woman whom Jehovah hath appointed for my master’s son.

units.leftText: And before I had finished praying in my heart, there was Rebekah coming out with her jar on her shoulder, and she went down to the spring and drew water. So I said to her, ‘Please give me a drink.’
units.rightText: And before I had done speaking in my heart, behold, Rebekah came forth with her pitcher on her shoulder; and she went down unto the fountain, and drew: and I said unto her, Let me drink, I pray thee.

units.leftText: She quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels as well.’ So I drank, and she also watered the camels.
units.rightText: And she made haste, and let down her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: so I drank, and she made the camels drink also.

units.leftText: Then I asked her, ‘Whose daughter are you?’
units.rightText: And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter art thou? And she said, The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, whom Milcah bare unto him: and I put the ring upon her nose, and the bracelets upon her hands.

units.leftText: Then I bowed down and worshiped the LORD; and I blessed the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who led me on the right road to take the granddaughter of my master’s brother for his son.
units.rightText: And I bowed my head, and worshipped Jehovah, and blessed Jehovah, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me in the right way to take my master’s brother’s daughter for his son.

units.leftText: Now if you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me; but if not, let me know, so that I may go elsewhere.”
units.rightText: And now if ye will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me: and if not, tell me; that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.

units.leftText: Laban and Bethuel answered, “This is from the LORD; we have no choice in the matter.
units.rightText: Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said, The thing proceedeth from Jehovah: we cannot speak unto thee bad or good.

units.leftText: Rebekah is here before you. Take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master’s son, just as the LORD has decreed.”
units.rightText: Behold, Rebekah is before thee, take her, and go, and let her be thy master’s son’s wife, as Jehovah hath spoken.

units.leftText: When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed down to the ground before the LORD.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that, when Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed himself down to the earth unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then he brought out jewels of silver and gold, and articles of clothing, and he gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious gifts to her brother and her mother.
units.rightText: And the servant brought forth jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment, and gave them to Rebekah: he gave also to her brother and to her mother precious things.

units.leftText: Then he and the men with him ate and drank and spent the night there. When they got up the next morning, he said, “Send me on my way to my master.”
units.rightText: And they did eat and drink, he and the men that were with him, and tarried all night; and they rose up in the morning, and he said, Send me away unto my master.

units.leftText: But her brother and mother said, “Let the girl remain with us ten days or so. After that, she may go.”
units.rightText: And her brother and her mother said, Let the damsel abide with us a few days, at the least ten; after that she shall go.

units.leftText: But he replied, “Do not delay me, since the LORD has made my journey a success. Send me on my way so that I may go to my master.”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Hinder me not, seeing Jehovah hath prospered my way; send me away that I may go to my master.

units.leftText: So they said, “We will call the girl and ask her opinion.”
units.rightText: And they said, We will call the damsel, and inquire at her mouth.

units.leftText: They called Rebekah and asked her, “Will you go with this man?” “I will go,” she replied.
units.rightText: And they called Rebekah, and said unto her, Wilt thou go with this man? And she said, I will go.

units.leftText: So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way, along with her nurse and Abraham’s servant and his men.
units.rightText: And they sent away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham’s servant, and his men.

units.leftText: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, “Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands. May your offspring possess the gates of their enemies.”
units.rightText: And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, Our sister, be thou the mother of thousands of ten thousands, and let thy seed possess the gate of those that hate them.

units.leftText: Then Rebekah and her servant girls got ready, mounted the camels, and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and left. Isaac Marries Rebekah
units.rightText: And Rebekah arose, and her damsels, and they rode upon the camels, and followed the man: and the servant took Rebekah, and went his way.

units.leftText: Now Isaac had just returned from Beer-lahai-roi, for he was living in the Negev.
units.rightText: And Isaac came from the way of Beer-lahai-roi; for he dwelt in the land of the South.

units.leftText: Early in the evening, Isaac went out to the field to meditate, and looking up, he saw the camels approaching.
units.rightText: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide: and he lifted up his eyes, and saw, and, behold, there were camels coming.

units.leftText: And when Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac, she got down from her camel
units.rightText: And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she alighted from the camel.

units.leftText: and asked the servant, “Who is that man in the field coming to meet us?”
units.rightText: And she said unto the servant, What man is this that walketh in the field to meet us? And the servant said, It is my master: and she took her veil, and covered herself.

units.leftText: Then the servant told Isaac all that he had done.
units.rightText: And the servant told Isaac all the things that he had done.

units.leftText: And Isaac brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah and took Rebekah as his wife. And Isaac loved her and was comforted after his mother’s death.
units.rightText: And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her. And Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.

units.leftText: Now Abraham had taken another wife, named Keturah,
units.rightText: And Abraham took another wife, and her name was Keturah.

units.leftText: and she bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
units.rightText: And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.

units.leftText: Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were the Asshurites, the Letushites, and the Leummites.
units.rightText: And Jokshan begat Sheba, and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, and Letushim, and Leummim.

units.leftText: The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were descendants of Keturah.
units.rightText: And the sons of Midian: Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.

units.leftText: Abraham left everything he owned to Isaac.
units.rightText: And Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac.

units.leftText: But while he was still alive, Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his concubines and sent them away from his son Isaac to the land of the east. The Death of Abraham
units.rightText: But unto the sons of the concubines, that Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts; and he sent them away from Isaac his son, while he yet lived, eastward, unto the east country.

units.leftText: Abraham lived a total of 175 years.
units.rightText: And these are the days of the years of Abraham’s life which he lived, a hundred threescore and fifteen years.

units.leftText: And at a ripe old age he breathed his last and died, old and contented, and was gathered to his people.
units.rightText: And Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years, and was gathered to his people.

units.leftText: His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah near Mamre, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite.
units.rightText: And Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is before Mamre;

units.leftText: This was the field that Abraham had bought from the Hittites. Abraham was buried there with his wife Sarah.
units.rightText: the field which Abraham purchased of the children of Heth: there was Abraham buried, and Sarah his wife.

units.leftText: After Abraham’s death, God blessed his son Isaac, who lived near Beer-lahai-roi. The Descendants of Ishmael (1 Chronicles 1:28–31|1CH 1:28-31*)
units.rightText: And it came to pass after the death of Abraham, that God blessed Isaac his son: and Isaac dwelt by Beer-lahai-roi.

units.leftText: This is the account of Abraham’s son Ishmael, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s maidservant, bore to Abraham.
units.rightText: Now these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid, bare unto Abraham:

units.leftText: These are the names of the sons of Ishmael in the order of their birth: Nebaioth the firstborn of Ishmael, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
units.rightText: and these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: the first-born of Ishmael, Nebaioth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,

units.leftText: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
units.rightText: and Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,

units.leftText: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
units.rightText: Hadad, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah:

units.leftText: These were the sons of Ishmael, and these were their names by their villages and encampments — twelve princes of their tribes.
units.rightText: these are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their villages, and by their encampments; twelve princes according to their nations.

units.leftText: Ishmael lived a total of 137 years. Then he breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people.
units.rightText: And these are the years of the life of Ishmael, a hundred and thirty and seven years: and he gave up the ghost and died, and was gathered unto his people.

units.leftText: Ishmael’s descendants settled from Havilah to Shur, which is near the border of Egypt as you go toward Asshur. And they lived in hostility toward all their brothers. Jacob and Esau (Malachi 1:1–5|MAL 1:1-5*; Romans 9:6–29|ROM 9:6-29*)
units.rightText: And they dwelt from Havilah unto Shur that is before Egypt, as thou goest toward Assyria: he abode over against all his brethren.
leftNotes: 25:18 Or Assyria

units.leftText: This is the account of Abraham’s son Isaac. Abraham became the father of Isaac,
units.rightText: And these are the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son: Abraham begat Isaac:

units.leftText: and Isaac was forty years old when he married Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan-aram and the sister of Laban the Aramean.
units.rightText: and Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Paddan-aram, the sister of Laban the Syrian, to be his wife.
leftNotes: 25:20 That is, northwest Mesopotamia

units.leftText: Later, Isaac prayed to the LORD on behalf of his wife, because she was barren. And the LORD heard his prayer, and his wife Rebekah conceived.
units.rightText: And Isaac entreated Jehovah for his wife, because she was barren: and Jehovah was entreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.

units.leftText: But the children inside her struggled with each other, and she said, “Why is this happening to me?” So Rebekah went to inquire of the LORD,
units.rightText: And the children struggled together within her; and she said, If it be so, wherefore do I live? And she went to inquire of Jehovah.

units.leftText: and He declared to her: “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you will be separated; one people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb, And two peoples shall be separated from thy bowels: And the one people shall be stronger than the other people; And the elder shall serve the younger.
leftNotes: 25:23 Cited in Romans 9:12|ROM 9:12*

units.leftText: When her time came to give birth, there were indeed twins in her womb.
units.rightText: And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.

units.leftText: The first one came out red, covered with hair like a fur coat; so they named him Esau.
units.rightText: And the first came forth red, all over like a hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.
leftNotes: 25:25 Esau sounds like a Hebrew term that means hairy.

units.leftText: After this, his brother came out grasping Esau’s heel; so he was named Jacob. And Isaac was sixty years old when the twins were born.
units.rightText: And after that came forth his brother, and his hand had hold on Esau’s heel; and his name was called Jacob: and Isaac was threescore years old when she bare them.
leftNotes: 25:26 Jacob means he grasps the heel or he deceives.

units.leftText: When the boys grew up, Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the field, while Jacob was a quiet man who stayed at home.
units.rightText: And the boys grew: and Esau was a skilful hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a quiet man, dwelling in tents.

units.leftText: Because Isaac had a taste for wild game, he loved Esau; but Rebekah loved Jacob. Esau Sells His Birthright
units.rightText: Now Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: and Rebekah loved Jacob.

units.leftText: One day, while Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau came in from the field and was famished.
units.rightText: And Jacob boiled pottage: and Esau came in from the field, and he was faint:

units.leftText: He said to Jacob, “Let me eat some of that red stew, for I am famished.” (That is why he was also called Edom. )
units.rightText: and Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint: therefore was his name called Edom.
leftNotes: 25:30 Edom means red.

units.leftText: “First sell me your birthright,” Jacob replied.
units.rightText: And Jacob said, Sell me first thy birthright.

units.leftText: “Look,” said Esau, “I am about to die, so what good is a birthright to me?”
units.rightText: And Esau said, Behold, I am about to die: and what profit shall the birthright do to me?

units.leftText: “Swear to me first,” Jacob said.
units.rightText: And Jacob said, Swear to me first; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob.

units.leftText: Then Jacob gave some bread and lentil stew to Esau, who ate and drank and then got up and went away. Thus Esau despised his birthright.
units.rightText: And Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentils; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: so Esau despised his birthright.

units.leftText: Now there was another famine in the land, subsequent to the one that had occurred in Abraham’s time. And Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines at Gerar.
units.rightText: And there was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went unto Abimelech king of the Philistines, unto Gerar.

units.leftText: The LORD appeared to Isaac and said, “Do not go down to Egypt. Settle in the land where I tell you.
units.rightText: And Jehovah appeared unto him, and said, Go not down into Egypt; dwell in the land which I shall tell thee of:

units.leftText: Stay in this land as a foreigner, and I will be with you and bless you. For I will give all these lands to you and your offspring, and I will confirm the oath that I swore to your father Abraham.
units.rightText: sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath which I sware unto Abraham thy father;

units.leftText: I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, and I will give them all these lands, and through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed,
units.rightText: and I will multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven, and will give unto thy seed all these lands; and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed;

units.leftText: because Abraham listened to My voice and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My laws.” Isaac Deceives Abimelech
units.rightText: because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.

units.leftText: So Isaac settled in Gerar.
units.rightText: And Isaac dwelt in Gerar:

units.leftText: But when the men of that place asked about his wife, he said, “She is my sister.” For he was afraid to say, “She is my wife,” since he thought to himself, “The men of this place will kill me on account of Rebekah, because she is so beautiful.”
units.rightText: and the men of the place asked him of his wife; and he said, She is my sister: for he feared to say, My wife; lest, said he, the men of the place should kill me for Rebekah; because she was fair to look upon.

units.leftText: When Isaac had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked down from the window and was surprised to see Isaac caressing his wife Rebekah.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac was sporting with Rebekah his wife.

units.leftText: Abimelech sent for Isaac and said, “So she is really your wife! How could you say, ‘She is my sister’?” Isaac replied, “Because I thought I might die on account of her.”
units.rightText: And Abimelech called Isaac, and said, Behold, of a surety she is thy wife: and how saidst thou, She is my sister? And Isaac said unto him, Because I said, Lest I die because of her.

units.leftText: “What is this you have done to us?” asked Abimelech. “One of the people could easily have slept with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.”
units.rightText: And Abimelech said, What is this thou hast done unto us? one of the people might easily have lain with thy wife, and thou wouldest have brought guiltiness upon us.

units.leftText: So Abimelech warned all the people, saying, “Whoever harms this man or his wife will surely be put to death.” Isaac’s Prosperity
units.rightText: And Abimelech charged all the people, saying, He that toucheth this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.

units.leftText: Now Isaac sowed seed in the land, and that very year he reaped a hundredfold. And the LORD blessed him,
units.rightText: And Isaac sowed in that land, and found in the same year a hundredfold: and Jehovah blessed him.

units.leftText: and he became richer and richer, until he was exceedingly wealthy.
units.rightText: And the man waxed great, and grew more and more until he became very great:

units.leftText: He owned so many flocks and herds and servants that the Philistines envied him.
units.rightText: and he had possessions of flocks, and possessions of herds, and a great household: and the Philistines envied him.

units.leftText: So the Philistines took dirt and stopped up all the wells that his father’s servants had dug in the days of his father Abraham.
units.rightText: Now all the wells which his father’s servants had digged in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped, and filled with earth.

units.leftText: Then Abimelech said to Isaac, “Depart from us, for you are much too powerful for us.”
units.rightText: And Abimelech said unto Isaac, Go from us; for thou art much mightier than we.

units.leftText: So Isaac left that place and encamped in the Valley of Gerar and settled there.
units.rightText: And Isaac departed thence, and encamped in the valley of Gerar, and dwelt there.

units.leftText: Isaac reopened the wells that had been dug in the days of his father Abraham, which the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham died. And he gave these wells the same names his father had given them.
units.rightText: And Isaac digged again the wells of water, which they had digged in the days of Abraham his father; for the Philistines had stopped them after the death of Abraham: and he called their names after the names by which his father had called them.

units.leftText: Then Isaac’s servants dug in the valley and found a well of fresh water there.
units.rightText: And Isaac’s servants digged in the valley, and found there a well of springing water.
leftNotes: 26:19 Or flowing water or living water

units.leftText: But the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s herdsmen and said, “The water is ours!” So he named the well Esek, because they contended with him.
units.rightText: And the herdsmen of Gerar strove with Isaac’s herdsmen, saying, The water is ours: and he called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him.
leftNotes: 26:20 Esek means contention.

units.leftText: Then they dug another well and quarreled over that one also; so he named it Sitnah.
units.rightText: And they digged another well, and they strove for that also: and he called the name of it Sitnah.
leftNotes: 26:21 Sitnah means enmity or hostility.

units.leftText: He moved on from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it. He named it Rehoboth and said, “At last the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.”
units.rightText: And he removed from thence, and digged another well; and for that they strove not: and he called the name of it Rehoboth; and he said, For now Jehovah hath made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.
leftNotes: 26:22 Rehoboth means broad places or open spaces.

units.leftText: From there Isaac went up to Beersheba,
units.rightText: And he went up from thence to Beer-sheba.

units.leftText: and that night the LORD appeared to him and said, “I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your descendants for the sake of My servant Abraham.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah appeared unto him the same night, and said, I am the God of Abraham thy father: fear not, for I am with thee, and will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham’s sake.

units.leftText: So Isaac built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD, and he pitched his tent there. His servants also dug a well there. Isaac’s Covenant with Abimelech
units.rightText: And he builded an altar there, and called upon the name of Jehovah, and pitched his tent there: and there Isaac’s servants digged a well.

units.leftText: Later, Abimelech came to Isaac from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his adviser and Phicol the commander of his army.
units.rightText: Then Abimelech went to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath his friend, and Phicol the captain of his host.

units.leftText: “Why have you come to me?” Isaac asked them. “You hated me and sent me away.”
units.rightText: And Isaac said unto them, Wherefore are ye come unto me, seeing ye hate me, and have sent me away from you?

units.leftText: “We can plainly see that the LORD has been with you,” they replied. “We recommend that there should now be an oath between us and you. Let us make a covenant with you
units.rightText: And they said, We saw plainly that Jehovah was with thee: and we said, Let there now be an oath betwixt us, even betwixt us and thee, and let us make a covenant with thee,

units.leftText: that you will not harm us, just as we have not harmed you but have done only good to you, sending you on your way in peace. And now you are blessed by the LORD.”
units.rightText: that thou wilt do us no hurt, as we have not touched thee, and as we have done unto thee nothing but good, and have sent thee away in peace: thou art now the blessed of Jehovah.

units.leftText: So Isaac prepared a feast for them, and they ate and drank.
units.rightText: And he made them a feast, and they did eat and drink.

units.leftText: And they got up early the next morning and swore an oath to each other. Then Isaac sent them on their way, and they left him in peace.
units.rightText: And they rose up betimes in the morning, and sware one to another: and Isaac sent them away, and they departed from him in peace.

units.leftText: On that same day, Isaac’s servants came and told him about the well they had dug. “We have found water!” they told him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass the same day, that Isaac’s servants came, and told him concerning the well which they had digged, and said unto him, We have found water.

units.leftText: So he called it Shibah, and to this day the name of the city is Beersheba. Esau’s Wives
units.rightText: And he called it Shibah: therefore the name of the city is Beer-sheba unto this day.
leftNotes: 26:33 Shibah can mean oath or seven.
26:33 Beersheba means well of seven or well of the oath.

units.leftText: When Esau was forty years old, he took as his wives Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite.
units.rightText: And when Esau was forty years old he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite:

units.leftText: And they brought grief to Isaac and Rebekah.
units.rightText: and they were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.

units.leftText: When Isaac was old and his eyes were so weak that he could no longer see, he called his older son Esau and said to him, “My son.” “Here I am,” Esau replied.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his elder son, and said unto him, My son: and he said unto him, Here am I.

units.leftText: “Look,” said Isaac, “I am now old, and I do not know the day of my death.
units.rightText: And he said, Behold now, I am old, I know not the day of my death.

units.leftText: Take your weapons — your quiver and bow — and go out into the field to hunt some game for me.
units.rightText: Now therefore take, I pray thee, thy weapons, thy quiver and thy bow, and go out to the field, and take me venison;

units.leftText: Then prepare a tasty dish that I love and bring it to me to eat, so that I may bless you before I die.”
units.rightText: and make me savory food, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat; that my soul may bless thee before I die.

units.leftText: Now Rebekah was listening to what Isaac told his son Esau. So when Esau went into the field to hunt game and bring it back,
units.rightText: And Rebekah heard when Isaac spake to Esau his son. And Esau went to the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it.

units.leftText: Rebekah said to her son Jacob, “Behold, I overheard your father saying to your brother Esau,
units.rightText: And Rebekah spake unto Jacob her son, saying, Behold, I heard thy father speak unto Esau thy brother, saying,

units.leftText: ‘Bring me some game and prepare me a tasty dish to eat, so that I may bless you in the presence of the LORD before I die.’
units.rightText: Bring me venison, and make me savory food, that I may eat, and bless thee before Jehovah before my death.

units.leftText: Now, my son, listen to my voice and do exactly as I tell you.
units.rightText: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command thee.

units.leftText: Go out to the flock and bring me two choice young goats, so that I can make them into a tasty dish for your father— the kind he loves.
units.rightText: Go now to the flock, and fetch me from thence two good kids of the goats; and I will make them savory food for thy father, such as he loveth:

units.leftText: Then take it to your father to eat, so that he may bless you before he dies.”
units.rightText: and thou shalt bring it to thy father, that he may eat, so that he may bless thee before his death.

units.leftText: Jacob answered his mother Rebekah, “Look, my brother Esau is a hairy man, but I am smooth-skinned.
units.rightText: And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.

units.leftText: What if my father touches me? Then I would be revealed to him as a deceiver, and I would bring upon myself a curse rather than a blessing.”
units.rightText: My father peradventure will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver; and I shall bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing.

units.leftText: His mother replied, “Your curse be on me, my son. Just obey my voice and go get them for me.”
units.rightText: And his mother said unto him, Upon me be thy curse, my son; only obey my voice, and go fetch me them.

units.leftText: So Jacob went and got two goats and brought them to his mother, who made the tasty food his father loved.
units.rightText: And he went, and fetched, and brought them to his mother: and his mother made savory food, such as his father loved.

units.leftText: And Rebekah took the finest clothes in the house that belonged to her older son Esau, and she put them on her younger son Jacob.
units.rightText: And Rebekah took the goodly garments of Esau her elder son, which were with her in the house, and put them upon Jacob her younger son;

units.leftText: She also put the skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck.
units.rightText: and she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck:

units.leftText: Then she handed her son Jacob the tasty food and bread she had made.
units.rightText: and she gave the savory food and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.

units.leftText: So Jacob went to his father and said, “My father.” “Here I am!” he answered. “Which one are you, my son?”
units.rightText: And he came unto his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I; who art thou, my son?

units.leftText: Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Please sit up and eat some of my game, so that you may bless me.”
units.rightText: And Jacob said unto his father, I am Esau thy first-born; I have done according as thou badest me: arise, I pray thee, sit and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me.

units.leftText: But Isaac asked his son, “How did you ever find it so quickly, my son?” “Because the LORD your God brought it to me,” he replied.
units.rightText: And Isaac said unto his son, How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son? And he said, Because Jehovah thy God sent me good speed.

units.leftText: Then Isaac said to Jacob, “Please come closer so I can touch you, my son. Are you really my son Esau, or not?”
units.rightText: And Isaac said unto Jacob, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, whether thou be my very son Esau or not.

units.leftText: So Jacob came close to his father Isaac, who touched him and said, “The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”
units.rightText: And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.

units.leftText: Isaac did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like those of his brother Esau; so he blessed him.
units.rightText: And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau’s hands: so he blessed him.

units.leftText: Again he asked, “Are you really my son Esau?” And he replied, “I am.”
units.rightText: And he said, Art thou my very son Esau? And he said, I am.

units.leftText: “Serve me,” said Isaac, “and let me eat some of my son’s game, so that I may bless you.” Jacob brought it to him, and he ate; then he brought him wine, and he drank.
units.rightText: And he said, Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son’s venison, that my soul may bless thee. And he brought it near to him, and he did eat: and he brought him wine, and he drank.

units.leftText: Then his father Isaac said to him, “Please come near and kiss me, my son.”
units.rightText: And his father Isaac said unto him, Come near now, and kiss me, my son.

units.leftText: So he came near and kissed him. When Isaac smelled his clothing, he blessed him and said: “Ah, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field that the LORD has blessed.
units.rightText: And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son Is as the smell of a field which Jehovah hath blessed:

units.leftText: May God give to you the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth — an abundance of grain and new wine.
units.rightText: And God give thee of the dew of heaven, And of the fatness of the earth, And plenty of grain and new wine:

units.leftText: May peoples serve you and nations bow down to you. May you be the master of your brothers, and may the sons of your mother bow down to you. May those who curse you be cursed, and those who bless you be blessed.” Esau’s Lost Hope
units.rightText: Let peoples serve thee, And nations bow down to thee: Be lord over thy brethren, And let thy mother’s sons bow down to thee: Cursed be every one that curseth thee, And blessed be every one that blesseth thee.

units.leftText: As soon as Isaac had finished blessing him and Jacob had left his father’s presence, his brother Esau returned from the hunt.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob, and Jacob was yet scarce gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.

units.leftText: He too made some tasty food, brought it to his father, and said to him, “My father, sit up and eat of your son’s game, so that you may bless me.”
units.rightText: And he also made savory food, and brought it unto his father; and he said unto his father, Let my father arise, and eat of his son’s venison, that thy soul may bless me.

units.leftText: But his father Isaac replied, “Who are you?” “I am Esau, your firstborn son,” he answered.
units.rightText: And Isaac his father said unto him, Who art thou? And he said, I am thy son, thy first-born, Esau.

units.leftText: Isaac began to tremble violently and said, “Who was it, then, who hunted the game and brought it to me? Before you came in, I ate it all and blessed him — and indeed, he will be blessed!”
units.rightText: And Isaac trembled very exceedingly, and said, Who then is he that hath taken venison, and brought it me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him? yea, and he shall be blessed.

units.leftText: When Esau heard his father’s words, he let out a loud and bitter cry and said to his father, “Bless me too, O my father!”
units.rightText: When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with an exceeding great and bitter cry, and said unto his father, Bless me, even me also, O my father.

units.leftText: But Isaac replied, “Your brother came deceitfully and took your blessing.”
units.rightText: And he said, Thy brother came with guile, and hath taken away thy blessing.

units.leftText: So Esau declared, “Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has cheated me twice. He took my birthright, and now he has taken my blessing.” Then he asked, “Haven’t you saved a blessing for me?”
units.rightText: And he said, Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing. And he said, Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?
leftNotes: 27:36 Jacob means he grasps the heel or he deceives.

units.leftText: But Isaac answered Esau: “Look, I have made him your master and given him all his relatives as servants; I have sustained him with grain and new wine. What is left that I can do for you, my son?”
units.rightText: And Isaac answered and said unto Esau, Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants; and with grain and new wine have I sustained him: and what then shall I do for thee, my son?

units.leftText: Esau said to his father, “Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me too, O my father!” Then Esau wept aloud.
units.rightText: And Esau said unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.

units.leftText: His father Isaac answered him: “Behold, your dwelling place shall be away from the richness of the land, away from the dew of heaven above.
units.rightText: And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, of the fatness of the earth shall be thy dwelling, And of the dew of heaven from above;

units.leftText: You shall live by the sword and serve your brother. But when you rebel, you will tear his yoke from your neck.”
units.rightText: And by thy sword shalt thou live, and thou shalt serve thy brother; And it shall come to pass, when thou shalt break loose, That thou shalt shake his yoke from off thy neck.

units.leftText: Esau held a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing his father had given him. And Esau said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then I will kill my brother Jacob.”
units.rightText: And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.

units.leftText: When the words of her older son Esau were relayed to Rebekah, she sent for her younger son Jacob and told him, “Look, your brother Esau is consoling himself by plotting to kill you.
units.rightText: And the words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah; and she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said unto him, Behold, thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee.

units.leftText: So now, my son, obey my voice and flee at once to my brother Laban in Haran.
units.rightText: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice; and arise, flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran;

units.leftText: Stay with him for a while, until your brother’s fury subsides—
units.rightText: and tarry with him a few days, until thy brother’s fury turn away;

units.leftText: until your brother’s rage against you wanes and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send for you and bring you back from there. Why should I lose both of you in one day?”
units.rightText: until thy brother’s anger turn away from thee, and he forget that which thou hast done to him: then I will send, and fetch thee from thence: why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?

units.leftText: Then Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of these Hittite women. If Jacob takes a Hittite wife from among them, what good is my life?”
units.rightText: And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these, of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me?
leftNotes: 27:46 Or daughters of Heth

units.leftText: So Isaac called for Jacob and blessed him. “Do not take a wife from the Canaanite women,” he commanded.
units.rightText: And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.

units.leftText: “Go at once to Paddan-aram, to the house of your mother’s father Bethuel, and take a wife from among the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.
units.rightText: Arise, go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel thy mother’s father; and take thee a wife from thence of the daughters of Laban thy mother’s brother.
leftNotes: 28:2 That is, northwest Mesopotamia; also in verses 5, 6, and 7

units.leftText: May God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, so that you may become a company of peoples.
units.rightText: And God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a company of peoples;
leftNotes: 28:3 Hebrew El-Shaddai

units.leftText: And may He give the blessing of Abraham to you and your descendants, so that you may possess the land where you dwell as a foreigner, the land God gave to Abraham.”
units.rightText: and give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee; that thou mayest inherit the land of thy sojournings, which God gave unto Abraham.

units.leftText: So Isaac sent Jacob to Paddan-aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, who was the mother of Jacob and Esau. Esau Marries Mahalath
units.rightText: And Isaac sent away Jacob: and he went to Paddan-aram unto Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.

units.leftText: Now Esau learned that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-aram to take a wife there, commanding him, “Do not marry a Canaanite woman,”
units.rightText: Now Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Paddan-aram, to take him a wife from thence; and that as he blessed him he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;

units.leftText: and that Jacob had obeyed his father and mother and gone to Paddan-aram.
units.rightText: and that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Paddan-aram:

units.leftText: And seeing that his father Isaac disapproved of the Canaanite women,
units.rightText: and Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father;

units.leftText: Esau went to Ishmael and married Mahalath, the sister of Nebaioth and daughter of Abraham’s son Ishmael, in addition to the wives he already had. Jacob’s Ladder
units.rightText: and Esau went unto Ishmael, and took, besides the wives that he had, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebaioth, to be his wife.

units.leftText: Meanwhile Jacob left Beersheba and set out for Haran.
units.rightText: And Jacob went out from Beer-sheba, and went toward Haran.

units.leftText: On reaching a certain place, he spent the night there because the sun had set. And taking one of the stones from that place, he put it under his head and lay down to sleep.
units.rightText: And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set; and he took one of the stones of the place, and put it under his head, and lay down in that place to sleep.

units.leftText: And Jacob had a dream about a ladder that rested on the earth with its top reaching up to heaven, and God’s angels were going up and down the ladder.
units.rightText: And he dreamed; and behold, a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold, the angels of God ascending and descending on it.

units.leftText: And there at the top the LORD was standing and saying, “I am the LORD, the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac. I will give you and your descendants the land on which you now lie.
units.rightText: And, behold, Jehovah stood above it, and said, I am Jehovah, the God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed;
leftNotes: 28:13 Or there beside him

units.leftText: Your descendants will be like the dust of the earth, and you will spread out to the west and east and north and south. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you and your offspring.
units.rightText: and thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.

units.leftText: Look, I am with you, and I will watch over you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land. For I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.”
units.rightText: And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee whithersoever thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.

units.leftText: When Jacob woke up, he said, “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I was unaware of it.”
units.rightText: And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely Jehovah is in this place; and I knew it not.

units.leftText: And he was afraid and said, “How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God; this is the gate of heaven!” The Stone of Bethel
units.rightText: And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.

units.leftText: Early the next morning, Jacob took the stone that he had placed under his head, and he set it up as a pillar. He poured oil on top of it,
units.rightText: And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put under his head, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.

units.leftText: and he called that place Bethel, though previously the city had been named Luz.
units.rightText: And he called the name of that place Beth-el: but the name of the city was Luz at the first.
leftNotes: 28:19 Bethel means house of God.

units.leftText: Then Jacob made a vow, saying, “If God will be with me and watch over me on this journey, and if He will provide me with food to eat and clothes to wear,
units.rightText: And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on,

units.leftText: so that I may return safely to my father’s house, then the LORD will be my God.
units.rightText: so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, and Jehovah will be my God,

units.leftText: And this stone I have set up as a pillar will be God’s house, and of all that You give me I will surely give You a tenth.”
units.rightText: then this stone, which I have set up for a pillar, shall be God’s house: and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.

units.leftText: Jacob resumed his journey and came to the land of the people of the east.
units.rightText: Then Jacob went on his journey, and came to the land of the children of the east.

units.leftText: He looked and saw a well in the field, and near it lay three flocks of sheep, because the sheep were watered from this well. And a large stone covered the mouth of the well.
units.rightText: And he looked, and, behold, a well in the field, and, lo, three flocks of sheep lying there by it; for out of that well they watered the flocks: and the stone upon the well’s mouth was great.

units.leftText: When all the flocks had been gathered there, the shepherds would roll away the stone from the mouth of the well and water the sheep. Then they would return the stone to its place over the mouth of the well.
units.rightText: And thither were all the flocks gathered: and they rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the sheep, and put the stone again upon the well’s mouth in its place.

units.leftText: “My brothers,” Jacob asked the shepherds, “where are you from?” “We are from Haran,” they answered.
units.rightText: And Jacob said unto them, My brethren, whence are ye? And they said, Of Haran are we.

units.leftText: “Do you know Laban the grandson of Nahor?” Jacob asked. “We know him,” they replied.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Know ye Laban the son of Nahor? And they said, We know him.

units.leftText: “Is he well?” Jacob inquired. “Yes,” they answered, “and here comes his daughter Rachel with his sheep.”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Is it well with him? And they said, It is well: and, behold, Rachel his daughter cometh with the sheep.

units.leftText: “Look,” said Jacob, “it is still broad daylight; it is not yet time to gather the livestock. Water the sheep and take them back to pasture.”
units.rightText: And he said, Lo, it is yet high day, neither is it time that the cattle should be gathered together: water ye the sheep, and go and feed them.

units.leftText: But they replied, “We cannot, until all the flocks have been gathered and the stone has been rolled away from the mouth of the well. Then we will water the sheep.”
units.rightText: And they said, We cannot, until all the flocks be gathered together, and they roll the stone from the well’s mouth; then we water the sheep.

units.leftText: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel arrived with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.
units.rightText: While he was yet speaking with them, Rachel came with her father’s sheep; for she kept them.

units.leftText: As soon as Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his mother’s brother Laban, with Laban’s sheep, he went up and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and watered his uncle’s sheep.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother’s brother, that Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother’s brother.

units.leftText: Then Jacob kissed Rachel and wept aloud.
units.rightText: And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.

units.leftText: He told Rachel that he was Rebekah’s son, a relative of her father, and she ran and told her father.
units.rightText: And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s brother, and that he was Rebekah’s son: and she ran and told her father.

units.leftText: When Laban heard the news about his sister’s son Jacob, he ran out to meet him. He embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him all that had happened. Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Laban heard the tidings of Jacob his sister’s son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.

units.leftText: Then Laban declared, “You are indeed my own flesh and blood.”
units.rightText: And Laban said to him, Surely thou art my bone and my flesh. And he abode with him the space of a month.

units.leftText: Laban said to him, “Just because you are my relative, should you work for nothing? Tell me what your wages should be.”
units.rightText: And Laban said unto Jacob, Because thou art my brother, shouldest thou therefore serve me for nought? tell me, what shall thy wages be?

units.leftText: Now Laban had two daughters; the older was named Leah, and the younger was named Rachel.
units.rightText: And Laban had two daughters: the name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.

units.leftText: Leah had weak eyes, but Rachel was shapely and beautiful.
units.rightText: And Leah’s eyes were tender; but Rachel was beautiful and well favored.
leftNotes: 29:17 Or had delicate eyes

units.leftText: Since Jacob loved Rachel, he answered, “I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.”
units.rightText: And Jacob loved Rachel; and he said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.

units.leftText: Laban replied, “Better that I give her to you than to another. Stay here with me.”
units.rightText: And Laban said, It is better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man: abide with me.

units.leftText: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, yet it seemed but a few days because of his love for her.
units.rightText: And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her.

units.leftText: Finally Jacob said to Laban, “Grant me my wife, for my time is complete, and I want to sleep with her.”
units.rightText: And Jacob said unto Laban, Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.

units.leftText: So Laban invited all the men of that place and prepared a feast.
units.rightText: And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.

units.leftText: But when evening came, Laban took his daughter Leah and gave her to Jacob, and he slept with her.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.

units.leftText: And Laban gave his servant girl Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her maidservant.
units.rightText: And Laban gave Zilpah his handmaid unto his daughter Leah for a handmaid.

units.leftText: When morning came, there was Leah! “What have you done to me?” Jacob said to Laban. “Wasn’t it for Rachel that I served you? Why have you deceived me?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the morning that, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me? did not I serve with thee for Rachel? wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?

units.leftText: Laban replied, “It is not our custom here to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older.
units.rightText: And Laban said, It is not so done in our place, to give the younger before the first-born.

units.leftText: Finish this week’s celebration, and we will give you the younger one in return for another seven years of work.”
units.rightText: Fulfil the week of this one, and we will give thee the other also for the service which thou shalt serve with me yet seven other years.

units.leftText: And Jacob did just that. He finished the week’s celebration, and Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.
units.rightText: And Jacob did so, and fulfilled her week: and he gave him Rachel his daughter to wife.

units.leftText: Laban also gave his servant girl Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her maidservant.
units.rightText: And Laban gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his handmaid to be her handmaid.

units.leftText: Jacob slept with Rachel as well, and indeed, he loved Rachel more than Leah. So he worked for Laban another seven years. Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah
units.rightText: And he went in also unto Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him yet seven other years.

units.leftText: When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, He opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.
units.rightText: And Jehovah saw that Leah was hated, and he opened her womb: but Rachel was barren.

units.leftText: And Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she named him Reuben, for she said, “The LORD has seen my affliction. Surely my husband will love me now.”
units.rightText: And Leah conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Reuben: for she said, Because Jehovah hath looked upon my affliction; for now my husband will love me.
leftNotes: 29:32 Reuben means Look, a son and also sounds like the Hebrew for He has seen my misery.
