units.leftText: Again she conceived and gave birth to a son, and she said, “Because the LORD has heard that I am unloved, He has given me this son as well.” So she named him Simeon.
units.rightText: And she conceived again, and bare a son: and said, Because Jehovah hath heard that I am hated, he hath therefore given me this son also: and she called his name Simeon.
leftNotes: 29:33 Simeon probably means one who hears.

units.leftText: Once again Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she said, “Now at last my husband will become attached to me, because I have borne him three sons.” So he was named Levi.
units.rightText: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, Now this time will my husband be joined unto me, because I have borne him three sons: therefore was his name called Levi.
leftNotes: 29:34 Levi sounds like the Hebrew for being attached to or feeling affection for.

units.leftText: And once more she conceived and gave birth to a son and said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” So she named him Judah. Then Leah stopped having children.
units.rightText: And she conceived again, and bare a son: and she said, This time will I praise Jehovah: therefore she called his name Judah; and she left off bearing.
leftNotes: 29:35 Judah sounds like the Hebrew for praise.

units.leftText: When Rachel saw that she was not bearing any children for Jacob, she envied her sister. “Give me children, or I will die!” she said to Jacob.
units.rightText: And when Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister; and she said unto Jacob, Give me children, or else I die.

units.leftText: Jacob became angry with Rachel and said, “Am I in the place of God, who has withheld children from you?”
units.rightText: And Jacob’s anger was kindled against Rachel: and he said, Am I in God’s stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?

units.leftText: Then she said, “Here is my maidservant Bilhah. Sleep with her, that she may bear children for me, so that through her I too can build a family.”
units.rightText: And she said, Behold, my maid Bilhah, go in unto her; that she may bear upon my knees, and I also may obtain children by her.
leftNotes: 30:3 Literally bear children on my knees

units.leftText: So Rachel gave Jacob her servant Bilhah as a wife, and he slept with her,
units.rightText: And she gave him Bilhah her handmaid to wife: and Jacob went in unto her.

units.leftText: and Bilhah conceived and bore him a son.
units.rightText: And Bilhah conceived, and bare Jacob a son.

units.leftText: Then Rachel said, “God has vindicated me; He has heard my plea and given me a son.” So she named him Dan.
units.rightText: And Rachel said, God hath judged me, and hath also heard my voice, and hath given me a son: therefore called she his name Dan.
leftNotes: 30:6 Dan means He has judged or He has vindicated.

units.leftText: And Rachel’s servant Bilhah conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.
units.rightText: And Bilhah Rachel’s handmaid conceived again, and bare Jacob a second son.

units.leftText: Then Rachel said, “In my great struggles, I have wrestled with my sister and won.” So she named him Naphtali. Gad and Asher
units.rightText: And Rachel said, With mighty wrestlings have I wrestled with my sister, and have prevailed: and she called his name Naphtali.
leftNotes: 30:8 Naphtali sounds like the Hebrew for wrestling.

units.leftText: When Leah saw that she had stopped having children, she gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife.
units.rightText: When Leah saw that she had left off bearing, she took Zilpah her handmaid, and gave her to Jacob to wife.

units.leftText: And Leah’s servant Zilpah bore Jacob a son.
units.rightText: And Zilpah Leah’s handmaid bare Jacob a son.

units.leftText: Then Leah said, “How fortunate!” So she named him Gad.
units.rightText: And Leah said, Fortunate! and she called his name Gad.
leftNotes: 30:11 Alternate MT reading (see also LXX); the other alternate reads “A troop is coming!”
30:11 Gad sounds like the Hebrew for good fortune, or alternately for band of raiders.

units.leftText: When Leah’s servant Zilpah bore Jacob a second son,
units.rightText: And Zilpah Leah’s handmaid bare Jacob a second son.

units.leftText: Leah said, “How happy I am! For the women call me happy.” So she named him Asher.
units.rightText: And Leah said, Happy am I! for the daughters will call me happy: and she called his name Asher.
leftNotes: 30:13 Asher means happy.

units.leftText: Now during the wheat harvest, Reuben went out and found some mandrakes in the field. When he brought them to his mother, Rachel begged Leah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”
units.rightText: And Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them unto his mother Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, Give me, I pray thee, of thy son’s mandrakes.

units.leftText: But Leah replied, “Is it not enough that you have taken away my husband? Now you want to take my son’s mandrakes as well?” “Very well,” said Rachel, “he may sleep with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.”
units.rightText: And she said unto her, Is it a small matter that thou hast taken away my husband? and wouldest thou take away my son’s mandrakes also? And Rachel said, Therefore he shall lie with thee to-night for thy son’s mandrakes.

units.leftText: When Jacob came in from the field that evening, Leah went out to meet him and said, “You must come with me, for I have hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” So he slept with her that night. Issachar, Zebulun, and Dinah
units.rightText: And Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and said, Thou must come in unto me; for I have surely hired thee with my son’s mandrakes. And he lay with her that night.

units.leftText: And God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore a fifth son to Jacob.
units.rightText: And God hearkened unto Leah, and she conceived, and bare Jacob a fifth son.

units.leftText: Then Leah said, “God has rewarded me for giving my maidservant to my husband.” So she named him Issachar.
units.rightText: And Leah said, God hath given me my hire, because I gave my handmaid to my husband: and she called his name Issachar.
leftNotes: 30:18 Issachar sounds like the Hebrew for wages or reward.

units.leftText: Again Leah conceived and bore a sixth son to Jacob.
units.rightText: And Leah conceived again, and bare a sixth son to Jacob.

units.leftText: “God has given me a good gift,” she said. “This time my husband will honor me, because I have borne him six sons.” And she named him Zebulun.
units.rightText: And Leah said, God hath endowed me with a good dowry; now will my husband dwell with me, because I have borne him six sons: and she called his name Zebulun.
leftNotes: 30:20 Zebulun sounds like the Hebrew for honor.

units.leftText: After that, Leah gave birth to a daughter and named her Dinah. Joseph
units.rightText: And afterwards she bare a daughter, and called her name Dinah.

units.leftText: Then God remembered Rachel. He listened to her and opened her womb,
units.rightText: And God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and opened her womb.

units.leftText: and she conceived and gave birth to a son. “God has taken away my shame,” she said.
units.rightText: And she conceived, and bare a son: and said, God hath taken away my reproach:

units.leftText: She named him Joseph, and said, “May the LORD add to me another son.” Jacob Prospers
units.rightText: and she called his name Joseph, saying, Jehovah add to me another son.
leftNotes: 30:24 Joseph means may He add.

units.leftText: Now after Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, “Send me on my way so I can return to my homeland.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Rachel had borne Joseph, that Jacob said unto Laban, Send me away, that I may go unto mine own place, and to my country.

units.leftText: Give me my wives and children for whom I have served you, that I may go on my way. You know how hard I have worked for you.”
units.rightText: Give me my wives and my children for whom I have served thee, and let me go: for thou knowest my service wherewith I have served thee.

units.leftText: But Laban replied, “If I have found favor in your eyes, please stay. I have learned by divination that the LORD has blessed me because of you.”
units.rightText: And Laban said unto him, If now I have found favor in thine eyes, tarry: for I have divined that Jehovah hath blessed me for thy sake.

units.leftText: And he added, “Name your wages, and I will pay them.”
units.rightText: And he said, Appoint me thy wages, and I will give it.

units.leftText: Then Jacob answered, “You know how I have served you and how your livestock have thrived under my care.
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Thou knowest how I have served thee, and how thy cattle have fared with me.

units.leftText: Indeed, you had very little before my arrival, but now your wealth has increased many times over. The LORD has blessed you wherever I set foot. But now, when may I also provide for my own household?”
units.rightText: For it was little which thou hadst before I came, and it hath increased unto a multitude; and Jehovah hath blessed thee whithersoever I turned: and now when shall I provide for mine own house also?

units.leftText: “What can I give you?” Laban asked.
units.rightText: And he said, What shall I give thee? And Jacob said, Thou shalt not give me aught: if thou wilt do this thing for me, I will again feed thy flock and keep it.

units.leftText: Let me go through all your flocks today and remove from them every speckled or spotted sheep, every dark-colored lamb, and every spotted or speckled goat. These will be my wages.
units.rightText: I will pass through all thy flock to-day, removing from thence every speckled and spotted one, and every black one among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats: and of such shall be my hire.

units.leftText: So my honesty will testify for me when you come to check on my wages in the future. If I have any goats that are not speckled or spotted, or any lambs that are not dark-colored, they will be considered stolen.”
units.rightText: So shall my righteousness answer for me hereafter, when thou shalt come concerning my hire that is before thee: every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and black among the sheep, that, if found with me, shall be counted stolen.

units.leftText: “Agreed,” said Laban. “Let it be as you have said.”
units.rightText: And Laban said, Behold, I would it might be according to thy word.

units.leftText: That very day Laban removed all the streaked or spotted male goats and every speckled or spotted female goat— every one that had any white on it— and every dark-colored lamb, and he placed them under the care of his sons.
units.rightText: And he removed that day the he-goats that were ringstreaked and spotted, and all the she-goats that were speckled and spotted, every one that had white in it, and all the black ones among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his sons;

units.leftText: Then he put a three-day journey between himself and Jacob, while Jacob was shepherding the rest of Laban’s flocks.
units.rightText: and he set three days’ journey betwixt himself and Jacob: and Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.

units.leftText: Jacob, however, took fresh branches of poplar, almond, and plane trees, and peeled the bark, exposing the white inner wood of the branches.
units.rightText: And Jacob took him rods of fresh poplar, and of the almond and of the plane-tree; and peeled white streaks in them, and made the white appear which was in the rods.

units.leftText: Then he set the peeled branches in the watering troughs in front of the flocks coming in to drink. So when the flocks were in heat and came to drink,
units.rightText: And he set the rods which he had peeled over against the flocks in the gutters in the watering-troughs where the flocks came to drink; and they conceived when they came to drink.

units.leftText: they mated in front of the branches. And they bore young that were streaked or speckled or spotted.
units.rightText: And the flocks conceived before the rods, and the flocks brought forth ringstreaked, speckled, and spotted.

units.leftText: Jacob set apart the young, but made the rest face the streaked dark-colored sheep in Laban’s flocks. Then he set his own stock apart and did not put them with Laban’s animals.
units.rightText: And Jacob separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toward the ringstreaked and all the black in the flock of Laban: and he put his own droves apart, and put them not unto Laban’s flock.

units.leftText: Whenever the stronger females of the flock were in heat, Jacob would place the branches in the troughs, in full view of the animals, so that they would breed in front of the branches.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, whensoever the stronger of the flock did conceive, that Jacob laid the rods before the eyes of the flock in the gutters, that they might conceive among the rods;

units.leftText: But if the animals were weak, he did not set out the branches. So the weaker animals went to Laban and the stronger ones to Jacob.
units.rightText: but when the flock were feeble, he put them not in: so the feebler were Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s.

units.leftText: Thus Jacob became exceedingly prosperous. He owned large flocks, maidservants and menservants, and camels and donkeys.
units.rightText: And the man increased exceedingly, and had large flocks, and maid-servants and men-servants, and camels and asses.

units.leftText: Now Jacob heard that Laban’s sons were saying, “Jacob has taken away all that belonged to our father and built all this wealth at our father’s expense.”
units.rightText: And he heard the words of Laban’s sons, saying, Jacob hath taken away all that was our father’s; and of that which was our father’s hath he gotten all this glory.

units.leftText: And Jacob saw from the countenance of Laban that his attitude toward him had changed.
units.rightText: And Jacob beheld the countenance of Laban, and, behold, it was not toward him as beforetime.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Jacob, “Go back to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Jacob, Return unto the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred; and I will be with thee.

units.leftText: So Jacob sent word and called Rachel and Leah to the field where his flocks were,
units.rightText: And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field unto his flock,

units.leftText: and he told them, “I can see from your father’s countenance that his attitude toward me has changed; but the God of my father has been with me.
units.rightText: and said unto them, I see your father’s countenance, that it is not toward me as beforetime; but the God of my father hath been with me.

units.leftText: You know that I have served your father with all my strength.
units.rightText: And ye know that with all my power I have served your father.

units.leftText: And although he has cheated me and changed my wages ten times, God has not allowed him to harm me.
units.rightText: And your father hath deceived me, and changed my wages ten times; but God suffered him not to hurt me.

units.leftText: If he said, ‘The speckled will be your wages,’ then the whole flock bore speckled offspring. If he said, ‘The streaked will be your wages,’ then the whole flock bore streaked offspring.
units.rightText: If he said thus, The speckled shall be thy wages; then all the flock bare speckled: and if he said thus, The ringstreaked shall be thy wages; then bare all the flock ringstreaked.

units.leftText: Thus God has taken away your father’s livestock and given them to me.
units.rightText: Thus God hath taken away the cattle of your father, and given them to me.

units.leftText: When the flocks were breeding, I saw in a dream that the streaked, spotted, and speckled males were mating with the females.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the time that the flock conceive, that I lifted up mine eyes, and saw in a dream, and, behold, the he-goats which leaped upon the flock were ringstreaked, speckled, and grizzled.

units.leftText: In that dream the angel of God said to me, ‘Jacob!’ And I replied, ‘Here I am.’
units.rightText: And the angel of God said unto me in the dream, Jacob: and I said, Here am I.
leftNotes: 31:11 Or Angel

units.leftText: ‘Look up,’ he said, ‘and see that all the males that are mating with the flock are streaked, spotted, or speckled; for I have seen all that Laban has done to you.
units.rightText: And he said, Lift up now thine eyes, and see: all the he-goats which leap upon the flock are ringstreaked, speckled, and grizzled: for I have seen all that Laban doeth unto thee.

units.leftText: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed the pillar and made a solemn vow to Me. Now get up, leave this land at once, and return to your native land.’”
units.rightText: I am the God of Beth-el, where thou anointedst a pillar, where thou vowedst a vow unto me: now arise, get thee out from this land, and return unto the land of thy nativity.

units.leftText: And Rachel and Leah replied, “Do we have any portion or inheritance left in our father’s house?
units.rightText: And Rachel and Leah answered and said unto him, Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in our father’s house?

units.leftText: Are we not regarded by him as outsiders? Not only has he sold us, but he has certainly squandered what was paid for us.
units.rightText: Are we not accounted by him as foreigners? for he hath sold us, and hath also quite devoured our money.

units.leftText: Surely all the wealth that God has taken away from our father belongs to us and to our children. So do whatever God has told you.”
units.rightText: For all the riches which God hath taken away from our father, that is ours and our children’s: now then, whatsoever God hath said unto thee, do.

units.leftText: Then Jacob got up and put his children and his wives on camels,
units.rightText: Then Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his wives upon the camels;

units.leftText: and he drove all his livestock before him, along with all the possessions he had acquired in Paddan-aram, to go to his father Isaac in the land in Canaan.
units.rightText: and he carried away all his cattle, and all his substance which he had gathered, the cattle of his getting, which he had gathered in Paddan-aram, to go to Isaac his father unto the land of Canaan.
leftNotes: 31:18 That is, northwest Mesopotamia

units.leftText: Now while Laban was out shearing his sheep, Rachel stole her father’s household idols.
units.rightText: Now Laban was gone to shear his sheep: and Rachel stole the teraphim that were her father’s.

units.leftText: Moreover, Jacob deceived Laban the Aramean by not telling him that he was running away.
units.rightText: And Jacob stole away unawares to Laban the Syrian, in that he told him not that he fled.
leftNotes: 31:20 Or stole the heart of; also in verses 26 and 27

units.leftText: So he fled with all his possessions, crossed the Euphrates, and headed for the hill country of Gilead. Laban Pursues Jacob
units.rightText: So he fled with all that he had; and he rose up, and passed over the River, and set his face toward the mountain of Gilead.
leftNotes: 31:21 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: On the third day Laban was informed that Jacob had fled.
units.rightText: And it was told Laban on the third day that Jacob was fled.

units.leftText: So he took his relatives with him, pursued Jacob for seven days, and overtook him in the hill country of Gilead.
units.rightText: And he took his brethren with him, and pursued after him seven days’ journey; and he overtook him in the mountain of Gilead.

units.leftText: But that night God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream and warned him, “Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.”
units.rightText: And God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream of the night, and said unto him, Take heed to thyself that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad.

units.leftText: Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country of Gilead when Laban overtook him, and Laban and his relatives camped there as well.
units.rightText: And Laban came up with Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain: and Laban with his brethren encamped in the mountain of Gilead.

units.leftText: Then Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done? You have deceived me and carried off my daughters like captives of war!
units.rightText: And Laban said to Jacob, What hast thou done, that thou hast stolen away unawares to me, and carried away my daughters as captives of the sword?

units.leftText: Why did you run away secretly and deceive me, without even telling me? I would have sent you away with joy and singing, with tambourines and harps.
units.rightText: Wherefore didst thou flee secretly, and steal away from me, and didst not tell me, that I might have sent thee away with mirth and with songs, with tabret and with harp;

units.leftText: But you did not even let me kiss my grandchildren and my daughters goodbye. Now you have done a foolish thing.
units.rightText: and didst not suffer me to kiss my sons and my daughters? now hast thou done foolishly.

units.leftText: I have power to do you great harm, but last night the God of your father said to me, ‘Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.’
units.rightText: It is in the power of my hand to do you hurt: but the God of your father spake unto me yesternight, saying, Take heed to thyself that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad.

units.leftText: Now you have gone off because you long for your father’s house. But why have you stolen my gods?”
units.rightText: And now, though thou wouldest needs be gone, because thou sore longedst after thy father’s house, yet wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?

units.leftText: “I was afraid,” Jacob answered, “for I thought you would take your daughters from me by force.
units.rightText: And Jacob answered and said to Laban, Because I was afraid: for I said, Lest thou shouldest take thy daughters from me by force.

units.leftText: If you find your gods with anyone here, he shall not live! In the presence of our relatives, see for yourself if anything is yours, and take it back.” For Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the idols.
units.rightText: With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, he shall not live: before our brethren discern thou what is thine with me, and take it to thee. For Jacob knew not that Rachel had stolen them.

units.leftText: So Laban went into Jacob’s tent, then Leah’s tent, and then the tents of the two maidservants, but he found nothing. Then he left Leah’s tent and entered Rachel’s tent.
units.rightText: And Laban went into Jacob’s tent, and into Leah’s tent, and into the tent of the two maid-servants; but he found them not. And he went out of Leah’s tent, and entered into Rachel’s tent.

units.leftText: Now Rachel had taken Laban’s household idols, put them in the saddlebag of her camel, and was sitting on them. And Laban searched everything in the tent but found nothing.
units.rightText: Now Rachel had taken the teraphim, and put them in the camel’s saddle, and sat upon them. And Laban felt about all the tent, but found them not.

units.leftText: Rachel said to her father, “Sir, do not be angry that I cannot stand up before you; for I am having my period.” So Laban searched but could not find the household idols.
units.rightText: And she said to her father, Let not my lord be angry that I cannot rise up before thee; for the manner of women is upon me. And he searched, but found not the teraphim.

units.leftText: Then Jacob became incensed and challenged Laban. “What is my crime?” he said. “For what sin of mine have you so hotly pursued me?
units.rightText: And Jacob was wroth, and chode with Laban: and Jacob answered and said to Laban, What is my trespass? what is my sin, that thou hast hotly pursued after me?

units.leftText: You have searched all my goods! Have you found anything that belongs to you? Put it here before my brothers and yours, that they may judge between the two of us.
units.rightText: Whereas thou hast felt about all my stuff, what hast thou found of all thy household stuff? Set it here before my brethren and thy brethren, that they may judge betwixt us two.

units.leftText: I have been with you for twenty years now. Your sheep and goats have not miscarried, nor have I eaten the rams of your flock.
units.rightText: These twenty years have I been with thee; thy ewes and thy she-goats have not cast their young, and the rams of thy flocks have I not eaten.

units.leftText: I did not bring you anything torn by wild beasts; I bore the loss myself. And you demanded payment from me for what was stolen by day or night.
units.rightText: That which was torn of beasts I brought not unto thee; I bare the loss of it; of my hand didst thou require it, whether stolen by day or stolen by night.

units.leftText: As it was, the heat consumed me by day and the frost by night, and sleep fled from my eyes.
units.rightText: Thus I was; in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep fled from mine eyes.

units.leftText: Thus for twenty years I have served in your household— fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks— and you have changed my wages ten times!
units.rightText: These twenty years have I been in thy house; I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy flock: and thou hast changed my wages ten times.

units.leftText: If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been with me, surely by now you would have sent me away empty-handed. But God has seen my affliction and the toil of my hands, and last night He rendered judgment.” Jacob’s Covenant with Laban
units.rightText: Except the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the Fear of Isaac, had been with me, surely now hadst thou sent me away empty. God hath seen mine affliction and the labor of my hands, and rebuked thee yesternight.

units.leftText: But Laban answered Jacob, “These daughters are my daughters, these sons are my sons, and these flocks are my flocks! Everything you see is mine! Yet what can I do today about these daughters of mine or the children they have borne?
units.rightText: And Laban answered and said unto Jacob, The daughters are my daughters, and the children are my children, and the flocks are my flocks, and all that thou seest is mine: and what can I do this day unto these my daughters, or unto their children whom they have borne?

units.leftText: Come now, let us make a covenant, you and I, and let it serve as a witness between you and me.”
units.rightText: And now come, let us make a covenant, I and thou; and let it be for a witness between me and thee.

units.leftText: So Jacob picked out a stone and set it up as a pillar,
units.rightText: And Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.

units.leftText: and he said to his relatives, “Gather some stones.” So they took stones and made a mound, and there by the mound they ate.
units.rightText: And Jacob said unto his brethren, Gather stones; and they took stones, and made a heap: and they did eat there by the heap.

units.leftText: Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.
units.rightText: And Laban called it Jegar-saha-dutha: but Jacob called it Galeed.
leftNotes: 31:47 The Aramaic Jegar-sahadutha and the Hebrew Galeed both mean heap of witnesses.

units.leftText: Then Laban declared, “This mound is a witness between you and me this day.”
units.rightText: And Laban said, This heap is witness between me and thee this day. Therefore was the name of it called Galeed:

units.leftText: It was also called Mizpah, because Laban said, “May the LORD keep watch between you and me when we are absent from each other.
units.rightText: and Mizpah, for he said, Jehovah watch between me and thee, when we are absent one from another.
leftNotes: 31:49 Mizpah means watchtower.

units.leftText: If you mistreat my daughters or take other wives, although no one is with us, remember that God is a witness between you and me.”
units.rightText: If thou shalt afflict my daughters, and if thou shalt take wives besides my daughters, no man is with us; see, God is witness betwixt me and thee.

units.leftText: Laban also said to Jacob, “Here is the mound, and here is the pillar I have set up between you and me.
units.rightText: And Laban said to Jacob, Behold this heap, and behold the pillar, which I have set betwixt me and thee.

units.leftText: This mound is a witness, and this pillar is a witness, that I will not go past this mound to harm you, and you will not go past this mound and pillar to harm me.
units.rightText: This heap be witness, and the pillar be witness, that I will not pass over this heap to thee, and that thou shalt not pass over this heap and this pillar unto me, for harm.

units.leftText: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.” So Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.
units.rightText: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge betwixt us. And Jacob sware by the Fear of his father Isaac.

units.leftText: Then Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and invited his relatives to eat a meal. And after they had eaten, they spent the night on the mountain.
units.rightText: And Jacob offered a sacrifice in the mountain, and called his brethren to eat bread: and they did eat bread, and tarried all night in the mountain.

units.leftText: Early the next morning, Laban got up and kissed his grandchildren and daughters and blessed them. Then he left to return home.
units.rightText: And early in the morning Laban rose up, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them: and Laban departed, and returned unto his place.

units.leftText: Jacob also went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
units.rightText: And Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.

units.leftText: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is the camp of God.” So he named that place Mahanaim.
units.rightText: And Jacob said when he saw them, This is God’s host: and he called the name of that place Mahanaim.
leftNotes: 32:2 Mahanaim means two camps.

units.leftText: Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.
units.rightText: And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother unto the land of Seir, the field of Edom.

units.leftText: He instructed them, “You are to say to my master Esau, ‘Your servant Jacob says: I have been staying with Laban and have remained there until now.
units.rightText: And he commanded them, saying, Thus shall ye say unto my lord Esau: Thus saith thy servant Jacob, I have sojourned with Laban, and stayed until now:

units.leftText: I have oxen, donkeys, flocks, menservants, and maidservants. I have sent this message to inform my master, so that I may find favor in your sight.’”
units.rightText: and I have oxen, and asses, and flocks, and men-servants, and maid-servants: and I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find favor in thy sight.

units.leftText: When the messengers returned to Jacob, they said, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is coming to meet you— he and four hundred men with him.”
units.rightText: And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, We came to thy brother Esau, and moreover he cometh to meet thee, and four hundred men with him.

units.leftText: In great fear and distress, Jacob divided his people into two camps, as well as the flocks and herds and camels.
units.rightText: Then Jacob was greatly afraid and was distressed: and he divided the people that were with him, and the flocks, and the herds, and the camels, into two companies;

units.leftText: He thought, “If Esau comes and attacks one camp, then the other camp can escape.”
units.rightText: and he said, If Esau come to the one company, and smite it, then the company which is left shall escape.

units.leftText: Then Jacob declared, “O God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac, the LORD who told me, ‘Go back to your country and to your kindred, and I will make you prosper,’
units.rightText: And Jacob said, O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, O Jehovah, who saidst unto me, Return unto thy country, and to thy kindred, and I will do thee good:

units.leftText: I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness You have shown Your servant. Indeed, with only my staff I came across the Jordan, but now I have become two camps.
units.rightText: I am not worthy of the least of all the lovingkindnesses, and of all the truth, which thou hast showed unto thy servant; for with my staff I passed over this Jordan; and now I am become two companies.

units.leftText: Please deliver me from the hand of my brother Esau, for I am afraid that he may come and attack me and the mothers and children with me.
units.rightText: Deliver me, I pray thee, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, lest he come and smite me, the mother with the children.

units.leftText: But You have said, ‘I will surely make you prosper, and I will make your offspring like the sand of the sea, too numerous to count.’”
units.rightText: And thou saidst, I will surely do thee good, and make thy seed as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.

units.leftText: Jacob spent the night there, and from what he had brought with him, he selected a gift for his brother Esau:
units.rightText: And he lodged there that night, and took of that which he had with him a present for Esau his brother:

units.leftText: 200 female goats, 20 male goats, 200 ewes, 20 rams,
units.rightText: two hundred she-goats and twenty he-goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,

units.leftText: 30 milk camels with their young, 40 cows, 10 bulls, 20 female donkeys, and 10 male donkeys.
units.rightText: thirty milch camels and their colts, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty she-asses and ten foals.

units.leftText: He entrusted them to his servants in separate herds and told them, “Go on ahead of me, and keep some distance between the herds.”
units.rightText: And he delivered them into the hand of his servants, every drove by itself, and said unto his servants, Pass over before me, and put a space betwixt drove and drove.

units.leftText: He instructed the one in the lead, “When my brother Esau meets you and asks, ‘To whom do you belong, where are you going, and whose animals are these before you?’
units.rightText: And he commanded the foremost, saying, When Esau my brother meeteth thee, and asketh thee, saying, Whose art thou? and whither goest thou? and whose are these before thee?

units.leftText: then you are to say, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob. They are a gift, sent to my lord Esau. And behold, Jacob is behind us.’”
units.rightText: then thou shalt say, They are thy servant Jacob’s; it is a present sent unto my lord Esau: and, behold, he also is behind us.

units.leftText: He also instructed the second, the third, and all those following behind the herds: “When you meet Esau, you are to say the same thing to him.
units.rightText: And he commanded also the second, and the third, and all that followed the droves, saying, On this manner shall ye speak unto Esau, when ye find him;

units.leftText: You are also to say, ‘Look, your servant Jacob is right behind us.’” For he thought, “I will appease Esau with the gift that is going before me. After that I can face him, and perhaps he will accept me. ”
units.rightText: and ye shall say, Moreover, behold, thy servant Jacob is behind us. For he said, I will appease him with the present that goeth before me, and afterward I will see his face; peradventure he will accept me.
leftNotes: 32:20 Or I will appease his face
32:20 Literally perhaps he will lift up my face

units.leftText: So Jacob’s gifts went on before him, while he spent the night in the camp. Jacob Wrestles with God
units.rightText: So the present passed over before him: and he himself lodged that night in the company.

units.leftText: During the night Jacob got up and took his two wives, his two maidservants, and his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.
units.rightText: And he rose up that night, and took his two wives, and his two handmaids, and his eleven children, and passed over the ford of the Jabbok.

units.leftText: He took them and sent them across the stream, along with all his possessions.
units.rightText: And he took them, and sent them over the stream, and sent over that which he had.

units.leftText: So Jacob was left all alone, and there a man wrestled with him until daybreak.
units.rightText: And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day.
leftNotes: 32:24 Or Man; here and in verses 25–28; corresponding pronouns may also be capitalized

units.leftText: When the man saw that he could not overpower Jacob, he struck the socket of Jacob’s hip and dislocated it as they wrestled.
units.rightText: And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was strained, as he wrestled with him.

units.leftText: Then the man said, “Let me go, for it is daybreak.” But Jacob replied, “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”
units.rightText: And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.

units.leftText: “What is your name?” the man asked. “Jacob,” he replied.
units.rightText: And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob.

units.leftText: Then the man said, “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with men, and you have prevailed.”
units.rightText: And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for thou hast striven with God and with men, and hast prevailed.
leftNotes: 32:28 Jacob means he grasps the heel or he deceives.
32:28 Israel means he struggles with God.

units.leftText: And Jacob requested, “Please tell me your name.” But he replied, “Why do you ask my name?” Then he blessed Jacob there.
units.rightText: And Jacob asked him, and said, Tell me, I pray thee, thy name. And he said, Wherefore is it that thou dost ask after my name? And he blessed him there.

units.leftText: So Jacob named the place Peniel, saying, “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.”
units.rightText: And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for, said he, I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.
leftNotes: 32:30 Peniel means the face of God.

units.leftText: The sun rose above him as he passed by Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip.
units.rightText: And the sun rose upon him as he passed over Penuel, and he limped upon his thigh.
leftNotes: 32:31 Penuel is a variant of Peniel; see verse 30.

units.leftText: Therefore to this day the Israelites do not eat the tendon attached to the socket of the hip, because the socket of Jacob’s hip was struck near that tendon.
units.rightText: Therefore the children of Israel eat not the sinew of the hip which is upon the hollow of the thigh, unto this day: because he touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh in the sinew of the hip.

units.leftText: Now Jacob looked up and saw Esau coming toward him with four hundred men. So he divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two maidservants.
units.rightText: And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau was coming, and with him four hundred men. And he divided the children unto Leah, and unto Rachel, and unto the two handmaids.

units.leftText: He put the maidservants and their children in front, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph at the rear.
units.rightText: And he put the handmaids and their children foremost, and Leah and her children after, and Rachel and Joseph hindermost.

units.leftText: But Jacob himself went on ahead and bowed to the ground seven times as he approached his brother.
units.rightText: And he himself passed over before them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.

units.leftText: Esau, however, ran to him and embraced him, threw his arms around his neck, and kissed him. And they both wept.
units.rightText: And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.

units.leftText: When Esau looked up and saw the women and children, he asked, “Who are these with you?”
units.rightText: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children; and said, Who are these with thee? And he said, The children whom God hath graciously given thy servant.

units.leftText: Then the maidservants and their children approached and bowed down.
units.rightText: Then the handmaids came near, they and their children, and they bowed themselves.

units.leftText: Leah and her children also approached and bowed down, and then Joseph and Rachel approached and bowed down.
units.rightText: And Leah also and her children came near, and bowed themselves: and after came Joseph near and Rachel, and they bowed themselves.

units.leftText: “What do you mean by sending this whole company to meet me?” asked Esau. “To find favor in your sight, my lord,” Jacob answered.
units.rightText: And he said, What meanest thou by all this company which I met? And he said, To find favor in the sight of my lord.

units.leftText: “I already have plenty, my brother,” Esau replied. “Keep what belongs to you.”
units.rightText: And Esau said, I have enough, my brother; let that which thou hast be thine.

units.leftText: But Jacob insisted, “No, please! If I have found favor in your sight, then receive this gift from my hand. For indeed, I have seen your face, and it is like seeing the face of God, since you have received me favorably.
units.rightText: And Jacob said, Nay, I pray thee, if now I have found favor in thy sight, then receive my present at my hand; forasmuch as I have seen thy face, as one seeth the face of God, and thou wast pleased with me.

units.leftText: Please accept my gift that was brought to you, because God has been gracious to me and I have all I need.” So Jacob pressed him until he accepted.
units.rightText: Take, I pray thee, my gift that is brought to thee; because God hath dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough. And he urged him, and he took it.
leftNotes: 33:11 Or blessing or treaty of peace

units.leftText: Then Esau said, “Let us be on our way, and I will go ahead of you.”
units.rightText: And he said, Let us take our journey, and let us go, and I will go before thee.

units.leftText: But Jacob replied, “My lord knows that the children are frail, and I must care for sheep and cattle that are nursing their young. If they are driven hard for even a day, all the animals will die.
units.rightText: And he said unto him, My lord knoweth that the children are tender, and that the flocks and herds with me have their young: and if they overdrive them one day, all the flocks will die.

units.leftText: Please let my lord go ahead of his servant. I will continue on slowly, at a comfortable pace for the livestock and children, until I come to my lord at Seir.”
units.rightText: Let my lord, I pray thee, pass over before his servant: and I will lead on gently, according to the pace of the cattle that are before me and according to the pace of the children, until I come unto my lord unto Seir.

units.leftText: “Let me leave some of my people with you,” Esau said. But Jacob replied, “Why do that? Let me find favor in the sight of my lord.”
units.rightText: And Esau said, Let me now leave with thee some of the folk that are with me. And he said, What needeth it? let me find favor in the sight of my lord.

units.leftText: So that day Esau started on his way back to Seir,
units.rightText: So Esau returned that day on his way unto Seir.

units.leftText: but Jacob went on to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and shelters for his livestock; that is why the place was called Succoth. Jacob Settles in Shechem
units.rightText: And Jacob journeyed to Succoth, and built him a house, and made booths for his cattle: therefore the name of the place is called Succoth.
leftNotes: 33:17 Succoth means booths or shelters or tabernacles; twice in this verse.

units.leftText: After Jacob had come from Paddan-aram, he arrived safely at the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan, and he camped just outside the city.
units.rightText: And Jacob came in peace to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan-aram; and encamped before the city.
leftNotes: 33:18 That is, northwest Mesopotamia

units.leftText: And the plot of ground where he pitched his tent, he purchased from the sons of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for a hundred pieces of silver.
units.rightText: And he bought the parcel of ground, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for a hundred pieces of money.
leftNotes: 33:19 Hebrew a hundred kesitahs; the value or weight of the kesitah is no longer known

units.leftText: There he set up an altar and called it El-Elohe-Israel.
units.rightText: And he erected there an altar, and called it El-Elohe-Israel.
leftNotes: 33:20 El-Elohe-Israel means God is the God of Israel or mighty is the God of Israel.

units.leftText: Now Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob, went out to visit the daughters of the land.
units.rightText: And Dinah the daughter of Leah, whom she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.

units.leftText: When Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the region, saw her, he took her and lay with her by force.
units.rightText: And Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her; and he took her, and lay with her, and humbled her.

units.leftText: And his soul was drawn to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob. He loved the young girl and spoke to her tenderly.
units.rightText: And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.

units.leftText: So Shechem told his father Hamor, “Get me this girl as a wife.”
units.rightText: And Shechem spake unto his father Hamor, saying, Get me this damsel to wife.

units.leftText: Jacob heard that Shechem had defiled his daughter Dinah, but since his sons were with his livestock in the field, he remained silent about it until they returned.
units.rightText: Now Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter; and his sons were with his cattle in the field: and Jacob held his peace until they came.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, Shechem’s father Hamor came to speak with Jacob.
units.rightText: And Hamor the father of Shechem went out unto Jacob to commune with him.

units.leftText: When Jacob’s sons heard what had happened, they returned from the field. They were filled with grief and fury, because Shechem had committed an outrage in Israel by lying with Jacob’s daughter — a thing that should not be done.
units.rightText: And the sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard it: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Israel in lying with Jacob’s daughter; which thing ought not to be done.
leftNotes: 34:7 Or against Israel

units.leftText: But Hamor said to them, “My son Shechem longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as his wife.
units.rightText: And Hamor communed with them, saying, The soul of my son Shechem longeth for your daughter: I pray you, give her unto him to wife.

units.leftText: Intermarry with us; give us your daughters and take our daughters for yourselves.
units.rightText: And make ye marriages with us; give your daughters unto us, and take our daughters unto you.

units.leftText: You may settle among us, and the land will be open to you. Live here, move about freely, and acquire your own property.”
units.rightText: And ye shall dwell with us: and the land shall be before you; dwell and trade ye therein, and get you possessions therein.

units.leftText: Then Shechem said to Dinah’s father and brothers, “Grant me this favor, and I will give you whatever you ask.
units.rightText: And Shechem said unto her father and unto her brethren, Let me find favor in your eyes, and what ye shall say unto me I will give.

units.leftText: Demand a high dowry and an expensive gift, and I will give you whatever you ask. Only give me the girl as my wife!” The Revenge of Dinah’s Brothers
units.rightText: Ask me never so much dowry and gift, and I will give according as ye shall say unto me: but give me the damsel to wife.

units.leftText: But because Shechem had defiled their sister Dinah, Jacob’s sons answered him and his father Hamor deceitfully.
units.rightText: And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father with guile, and spake, because he had defiled Dinah their sister,

units.leftText: “We cannot do such a thing,” they said. “To give our sister to an uncircumcised man would be a disgrace to us.
units.rightText: and said unto them, We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; for that were a reproach unto us.

units.leftText: We will consent to this on one condition, that you become circumcised like us — every one of your males.
units.rightText: Only on this condition will we consent unto you: if ye will be as we are, that every male of you be circumcised;

units.leftText: Then we will give you our daughters and take your daughters for ourselves. We will dwell among you and become one people.
units.rightText: then will we give our daughters unto you, and we will take your daughters to us, and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.

units.leftText: But if you will not agree to be circumcised, then we will take our sister and go.”
units.rightText: But if ye will not hearken unto us, to be circumcised; then will we take our daughter, and we will be gone.

units.leftText: Their offer seemed good to Hamor and his son Shechem.
units.rightText: And their words pleased Hamor, and Shechem Hamor’s son.

units.leftText: The young man, who was the most respected of all his father’s household, did not hesitate to fulfill this request, because he was delighted with Jacob’s daughter.
units.rightText: And the young man deferred not to do the thing, because he had delight in Jacob’s daughter: and he was honored above all the house of his father.

units.leftText: So Hamor and his son Shechem went to the gate of their city and addressed the men of their city:
units.rightText: And Hamor and Shechem his son came unto the gate of their city, and communed with the men of their city, saying,

units.leftText: “These men are at peace with us. Let them live and trade in our land; indeed, it is large enough for them. Let us take their daughters in marriage and give our daughters to them.
units.rightText: These men are peaceable with us; therefore let them dwell in the land, and trade therein; for, behold, the land is large enough for them; let us take their daughters to us for wives, and let us give them our daughters.

units.leftText: But only on this condition will the men agree to dwell with us and be one people: if all our men are circumcised as they are.
units.rightText: Only on this condition will the men consent unto us to dwell with us, to become one people, if every male among us be circumcised, as they are circumcised.

units.leftText: Will not their livestock, their possessions, and all their animals become ours? Only let us consent to them, and they will dwell among us.”
units.rightText: Shall not their cattle and their substance and all their beasts be ours? only let us consent unto them, and they will dwell with us.

units.leftText: All the men who went out of the city gate listened to Hamor and his son Shechem, and every male of the city was circumcised.
units.rightText: And unto Hamor and unto Shechem his son hearkened all that went out of the gate of his city; and every male was circumcised, all that went out of the gate of his city.

units.leftText: Three days later, while they were still in pain, two of Jacob’s sons (Dinah’s brothers Simeon and Levi) took their swords, went into the unsuspecting city, and slaughtered every male.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city unawares, and slew all the males.

units.leftText: They killed Hamor and his son Shechem with their swords, took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went away.
units.rightText: And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went forth.

units.leftText: Jacob’s other sons came upon the slaughter and looted the city, because their sister had been defiled.
units.rightText: The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.

units.leftText: They took their flocks and herds and donkeys, and everything else in the city or in the field.
units.rightText: They took their flocks and their herds and their asses, and that which was in the city, and that which was in the field;

units.leftText: They carried off all their possessions and women and children, and they plundered everything in their houses.
units.rightText: and all their wealth, and all their little ones and their wives, took they captive and made a prey, even all that was in the house.

units.leftText: Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have brought trouble upon me by making me a stench to the Canaanites and Perizzites, the people of this land. We are few in number; if they unite against me and attack me, I and my household will be destroyed.”
units.rightText: And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me, to make me odious to the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites: and, I being few in number, they will gather themselves together against me and smite me; and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.

units.leftText: But they replied, “Should he have treated our sister like a prostitute?”
units.rightText: And they said, Should he deal with our sister as with a harlot?

units.leftText: Then God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel, and settle there. Build an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you fled from your brother Esau.”
units.rightText: And God said unto Jacob, Arise, go up to Beth-el, and dwell there: and make there an altar unto God, who appeared unto thee when thou fleddest from the face of Esau thy brother.

units.leftText: So Jacob told his household and all who were with him, “Get rid of the foreign gods that are among you. Purify yourselves and change your garments.
units.rightText: Then Jacob said unto his household, and to all that were with him, Put away the foreign gods that are among you, and purify yourselves, and change your garments:

units.leftText: Then let us arise and go to Bethel. I will build an altar there to God, who answered me in my day of distress. He has been with me wherever I have gone.”
units.rightText: and let us arise, and go up to Beth-el; and I will make there an altar unto God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way which I went.

units.leftText: So they gave Jacob all their foreign gods and all their earrings, and Jacob buried them under the oak near Shechem.
units.rightText: And they gave unto Jacob all the foreign gods which were in their hand, and the rings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem.
leftNotes: 35:4 Or terebinth or great tree

units.leftText: As they set out, a terror from God fell over the surrounding cities, so that they did not pursue Jacob’s sons.
units.rightText: And they journeyed: and a terror of God was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.

units.leftText: So Jacob and everyone with him arrived in Luz (that is, Bethel) in the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: So Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan (the same is Beth-el), he and all the people that were with him.

units.leftText: There Jacob built an altar, and he called that place El-bethel, because it was there that God had revealed Himself to Jacob as he fled from his brother.
units.rightText: And he built there an altar, and called the place El-beth-el; because there God was revealed unto him, when he fled from the face of his brother.
leftNotes: 35:7 El-bethel means God of Bethel.

units.leftText: Now Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died and was buried under the oak below Bethel. So Jacob named it Allon-bacuth.
units.rightText: And Deborah Rebekah’s nurse died, and she was buried below Beth-el under the oak: and the name of it was called Allon-bacuth.
leftNotes: 35:8 Or great tree
35:8 Allon-bacuth means oak of weeping.

units.leftText: After Jacob had returned from Paddan-aram, God appeared to him again and blessed him.
units.rightText: And God appeared unto Jacob again, when he came from Paddan-aram, and blessed him.
leftNotes: 35:9 That is, northwest Mesopotamia; also in verse 26

units.leftText: And God said to him, “Though your name is Jacob, you will no longer be called Jacob. Instead, your name will be Israel. ” So God named him Israel.
units.rightText: And God said unto him, Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name: and he called his name Israel.
leftNotes: 35:10 Jacob means he grasps the heel or he deceives.
35:10 Israel means he struggles with God.

units.leftText: And God told him, “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation — even a company of nations — shall come from you, and kings shall descend from you.
units.rightText: And God said unto him, I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins;
leftNotes: 35:11 Hebrew El-Shaddai

units.leftText: The land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac I will give to you, and I will give this land to your descendants after you.”
units.rightText: and the land which I gave unto Abraham and Isaac, to thee I will give it, and to thy seed after thee will I give the land.

units.leftText: Then God went up from the place where He had spoken with him.
units.rightText: And God went up from him in the place where he spake with him.

units.leftText: So Jacob set up a pillar in the place where God had spoken with him— a stone marker— and he poured out a drink offering on it and anointed it with oil.
units.rightText: And Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he spake with him, a pillar of stone: and he poured out a drink-offering thereon, and poured oil thereon.

units.leftText: Jacob called the place where God had spoken with him Bethel. Benjamin Born, Rachel Dies
units.rightText: And Jacob called the name of the place where God spake with him, Beth-el.
leftNotes: 35:15 Bethel means house of God.

units.leftText: Later, they set out from Bethel, and while they were still some distance from Ephrath, Rachel began to give birth, and her labor was difficult.
units.rightText: And they journeyed from Beth-el; and there was still some distance to come to Ephrath: and Rachel travailed, and she had hard labor.

units.leftText: During her severe labor, the midwife said to her, “Do not be afraid, for you are having another son.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when she was in hard labor, that the midwife said unto her, Fear not; for now thou shalt have another son.

units.leftText: And with her last breath— for she was dying— she named vvv him Ben-oni. But his father called him Benjamin.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as her soul was departing (for she died), that she called his name Ben-oni: but his father called him Benjamin.
leftNotes: 35:18 Ben-oni could mean son of my sorrow or son of my strength.
35:18 Benjamin means son of my right hand.

units.leftText: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).
units.rightText: And Rachel died, and was buried in the way to Ephrath (the same is Beth-lehem).

units.leftText: Jacob set up a pillar on her grave; it marks Rachel’s tomb to this day. The Sons of Jacob (1 Chronicles 2:1–2|1CH 2:1-2*)
units.rightText: And Jacob set up a pillar upon her grave: the same is the Pillar of Rachel’s grave unto this day.

units.leftText: Israel again set out and pitched his tent beyond the Tower of Eder.
units.rightText: And Israel journeyed, and spread his tent beyond the tower of Eder.

units.leftText: While Israel was living in that region, Reuben went in and slept with his father’s concubine Bilhah, and Israel heard about it. Jacob had twelve sons:
units.rightText: And it came to pass, while Israel dwelt in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father’s concubine: and Israel heard of it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve:

units.leftText: The sons of Leah were Reuben the firstborn of Jacob, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
units.rightText: the sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob’s first-born, and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun;

units.leftText: The sons of Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin.
units.rightText: the sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin;

units.leftText: The sons of Rachel’s maidservant Bilhah were Dan and Naphtali.
units.rightText: and the sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid: Dan and Naphtali;

units.leftText: And the sons of Leah’s maidservant Zilpah were Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Paddan-aram. The Death of Isaac
units.rightText: and the sons of Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid: Gad and Asher: these are the sons of Jacob, that were born to him in Paddan-aram.

units.leftText: Jacob returned to his father Isaac at Mamre, near Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had stayed.
units.rightText: And Jacob came unto Isaac his father to Mamre, to Kiriath-arba (the same is Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac sojourned.

units.leftText: And Isaac lived 180 years.
units.rightText: And the days of Isaac were a hundred and fourscore years.

units.leftText: Then he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years. And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
units.rightText: And Isaac gave up the ghost, and died, and was gathered unto his people, old and full of days: and Esau and Jacob his sons buried him.

units.leftText: This is the account of Esau (that is, Edom).
units.rightText: Now these are the generations of Esau (the same is Edom).

units.leftText: Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, Oholibamah daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite,
units.rightText: Esau took his wives of the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite,

units.leftText: and Basemath daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth.
units.rightText: and Basemath Ishmael’s daughter, sister of Nebaioth.

units.leftText: And Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau, Basemath gave birth to Reuel,
units.rightText: And Adah bare to Esau Eliphaz; and Basemath bare Reuel;

units.leftText: and Oholibamah gave birth to Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These were the sons of Esau, who were born to him in the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: and Oholibamah bare Jeush, and Jalam, and Korah: these are the sons of Esau, that were born unto him in the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: Later, Esau took his wives and sons and daughters and all the people of his household, along with his livestock, all his other animals, and all the property he had acquired in Canaan, and he moved to a land far away from his brother Jacob.
units.rightText: And Esau took his wives, and his sons, and his daughters, and all the souls of his house, and his cattle, and all his beasts, and all his possessions, which he had gathered in the land of Canaan; and went into a land away from his brother Jacob.

units.leftText: For their possessions were too great for them to dwell together; the land where they stayed could not support them because of their livestock.
units.rightText: For their substance was too great for them to dwell together; and the land of their sojournings could not bear them because of their cattle.

units.leftText: So Esau (that is, Edom) settled in the area of Mount Seir.
units.rightText: And Esau dwelt in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.

units.leftText: This is the account of Esau, the father of the Edomites, in the area of Mount Seir.
units.rightText: And these are the generations of Esau the father of the Edomites in mount Seir:

units.leftText: These are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz son of Esau’s wife Adah, and Reuel son of Esau’s wife Basemath.
units.rightText: these are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz the son of Adah the wife of Esau, Reuel the son of Basemath the wife of Esau.

units.leftText: The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.
units.rightText: And the sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.

units.leftText: Additionally, Timna, a concubine of Esau’s son Eliphaz, gave birth to Amalek. These are the grandsons of Esau’s wife Adah.
units.rightText: And Timna was concubine to Eliphaz Esau’s son; and she bare to Eliphaz Amalek: these are the sons of Adah, Esau’s wife.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. They are the grandsons of Esau’s wife Basemath.
units.rightText: And these are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, and Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah: these were the sons of Basemath, Esau’s wife.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Esau’s wife Oholibamah (daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon) whom she bore to Esau: Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
units.rightText: And these were the sons of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, Esau’s wife: and she bare to Esau Jeush, and Jalam, and Korah.

units.leftText: These are the chiefs among the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: Chiefs Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
units.rightText: These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau: the sons of Eliphaz the first-born of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,

units.leftText: Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. They are the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom, and they are the grandsons of Adah.
units.rightText: chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek: these are the chiefs that came of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Adah.
leftNotes: 36:16 Hebrew; SP (also in verse 11 and 1 Chronicles 1:36|1CH 1:36*) does not include Korah.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Esau’s son Reuel: Chiefs Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. They are the chiefs descended from Reuel in the land of Edom, and they are the grandsons of Esau’s wife Basemath.
units.rightText: And these are the sons of Reuel, Esau’s son: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah: these are the chiefs that came of Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemath, Esau’s wife.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Esau’s wife Oholibamah: Chiefs Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. They are the chiefs descended from Esau’s wife Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.
units.rightText: And these are the sons of Oholibamah, Esau’s wife: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah: these are the chiefs that came of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, Esau’s wife.

units.leftText: All these are the sons of Esau (that is, Edom), and they were their chiefs. The Descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1:38–42|1CH 1:38-42*)
units.rightText: These are the sons of Esau, and these are their chiefs: the same is Edom.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who were living in the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
units.rightText: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan and Shobal and Zibeon and Anah,

units.leftText: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. They are the chiefs of the Horites, the descendants of Seir in the land of Edom.
units.rightText: and Dishon and Ezer and Dishan: these are the chiefs that came of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.

units.leftText: The sons of Lotan were Hori and Hemam. Timna was Lotan’s sister.
units.rightText: And the children of Lotan were Hori and Heman; and Lotan’s sister was Timna.
leftNotes: 36:22 Hemam is a variant of Homam; see 1 Chronicles 1:39|1CH 1:39*.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
units.rightText: And these are the children of Shobal: Alvan and Manahath and Ebal, Shepho and Onam.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. (This is the Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness as he was pasturing the donkeys of his father Zibeon.)
units.rightText: And these are the children of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah; this is Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness, as he fed the asses of Zibeon his father.

units.leftText: These are the children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah daughter of Anah.
units.rightText: And these are the children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
units.rightText: And these are the children of Dishon: Hemdan and Eshban and Ithran and Cheran.
leftNotes: 36:26 Hebrew Dishan, a variant of Dishon

units.leftText: These are the sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
units.rightText: These are the children of Ezer: Bilhan and Zaavan and Akan.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
units.rightText: These are the children of Dishan: Uz and Aran.

units.leftText: These are the chiefs of the Horites: Chiefs Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
units.rightText: These are the chiefs that came of the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,

units.leftText: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. They are the chiefs of the Horites, according to their divisions in the land of Seir. The Kings of Edom (1 Chronicles 1:43–54|1CH 1:43-54*)
units.rightText: chief Dishon, chief Ezer, chief Dishan: these are the chiefs that came of the Horites, according to their chiefs in the land of Seir.

units.leftText: These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites:
units.rightText: And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Israel.
leftNotes: 36:31 Or before an Israelite king reigned over them:

units.leftText: Bela son of Beor reigned in Edom; the name of his city was Dinhabah.
units.rightText: And Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom; and the name of his city was Dinhabah.

units.leftText: When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned in his place.
units.rightText: And Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
units.rightText: And Jobab died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the country of Moab, reigned in his place. And the name of his city was Avith.
units.rightText: And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Avith.

units.leftText: When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah reigned in his place.
units.rightText: And Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the Euphrates reigned in his place.
units.rightText: And Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the River reigned in his stead.
leftNotes: 36:37 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: When Shaul died, Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.
units.rightText: And Shaul died, and Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead.

units.leftText: When Baal-hanan son of Achbor died, Hadad reigned in his place. His city was named Pau, and his wife’s name was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-zahab.
units.rightText: And Baal-hanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Pau; and his wife’s name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-zahab.
leftNotes: 36:39 Some MT manuscripts, SP, and Syriac (see also 1 Chronicles 1:50|1CH 1:50*); other MT manuscripts Hadar

units.leftText: These are the names of Esau’s chiefs, according to their families and regions, by their names: Chiefs Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
units.rightText: And these are the names of the chiefs that came of Esau, according to their families, after their places, by their names: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,

units.leftText: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
units.rightText: chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,

units.leftText: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
units.rightText: chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,

units.leftText: Magdiel, and Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom, according to their settlements in the land they possessed. Esau was the father of the Edomites.
units.rightText: chief Magdiel, chief Iram: these are the chiefs of Edom, according to their habitations in the land of their possession. This is Esau, the father of the Edomites.

units.leftText: Now Jacob lived in the land where his father had resided, the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father’s sojournings, in the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: This is the account of Jacob. When Joseph was seventeen years old, he was tending the flock with his brothers, the sons of his father’s wives Bilhah and Zilpah, and he brought their father a bad report about them.
units.rightText: These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brethren; and he was a lad with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah, his father’s wives: and Joseph brought the evil report of them unto their father.

units.leftText: Now Israel loved Joseph more than his other sons, because Joseph had been born to him in his old age; so he made him a robe of many colors.
units.rightText: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colors.
leftNotes: 37:3 Possibly a robe with long sleeves; also in verses 23 and 32

units.leftText: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him and could not speak a kind word to him.
units.rightText: And his brethren saw that their father loved him more than all his brethren; and they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him.

units.leftText: Then Joseph had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers, they hated him even more.
units.rightText: And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brethren: and they hated him yet the more.

units.leftText: He said to them, “Listen to this dream I had:
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Hear, I pray you, this dream which I have dreamed:

units.leftText: We were binding sheaves of grain in the field, and suddenly my sheaf rose and stood upright, while your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to mine.”
units.rightText: for, behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves came round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.

units.leftText: “Do you intend to reign over us?” his brothers asked. “Will you actually rule us?” So they hated him even more because of his dream and his statements.
units.rightText: And his brethren said to him, Shalt thou indeed reign over us? or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us? And they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.

units.leftText: Then Joseph had another dream and told it to his brothers. “Look,” he said, “I had another dream, and this time the sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”
units.rightText: And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it to his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed yet a dream; and, behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars made obeisance to me.

units.leftText: He told his father and brothers, but his father rebuked him and said, “What is this dream that you have had? Will your mother and brothers and I actually come and bow down to the ground before you?”
units.rightText: And he told it to his father, and to his brethren; and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth?

units.leftText: And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept in mind what he had said. Joseph Sold into Egypt (Acts 7:9–14|ACT 7:9-14*)
units.rightText: And his brethren envied him; but his father kept the saying in mind.

units.leftText: Some time later, Joseph’s brothers had gone to pasture their father’s flocks near Shechem.
units.rightText: And his brethren went to feed their father’s flock in Shechem.

units.leftText: Israel said to him, “Are not your brothers pasturing the flocks at Shechem? Get ready; I am sending you to them.” “I am ready,” Joseph replied.
units.rightText: And Israel said unto Joseph, Are not thy brethren feeding the flock in Shechem? come, and I will send thee unto them. And he said to him, Here am I.

units.leftText: Then Israel told him, “Go now and see how your brothers and the flocks are faring, and bring word back to me.”
units.rightText: And he said to him, Go now, see whether it is well with thy brethren, and well with the flock; and bring me word again. So he sent him out of the vale of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.

units.leftText: a man found him wandering in the field and asked, “What are you looking for?”
units.rightText: And a certain man found him, and, behold, he was wandering in the field: and the man asked him, saying, What seekest thou?

units.leftText: “I am looking for my brothers,” Joseph replied. “Can you please tell me where they are pasturing their flocks?”
units.rightText: And he said, I am seeking my brethren: tell me, I pray thee, where they are feeding the flock.

units.leftText: “They have moved on from here,” the man answered. “I heard them say, ‘Let us go to Dothan.’” So Joseph set out after his brothers and found them at Dothan.
units.rightText: And the man said, They are departed hence; for I heard them say, Let us go to Dothan. And Joseph went after his brethren, and found them in Dothan.

units.leftText: Now Joseph’s brothers saw him in the distance, and before he arrived, they plotted to kill him.
units.rightText: And they saw him afar off, and before he came near unto them, they conspired against him to slay him.

units.leftText: “Here comes that dreamer!” they said to one another.
units.rightText: And they said one to another, Behold, this dreamer cometh.

units.leftText: “Come now, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits. We can say that a vicious animal has devoured him. Then we shall see what becomes of his dreams!”
units.rightText: Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into one of the pits, and we will say, An evil beast hath devoured him: and we shall see what will become of his dreams.

units.leftText: When Reuben heard this, he tried to rescue Joseph from their hands. “Let us not take his life,” he said.
units.rightText: And Reuben heard it, and delivered him out of their hand, and said, Let us not take his life.
