units.leftText: “Do not shed his blood. Throw him into this pit in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him.” Reuben said this so that he could rescue Joseph from their hands and return him to his father.
units.rightText: And Reuben said unto them, Shed no blood; cast him into this pit that is in the wilderness, but lay no hand upon him: that he might deliver him out of their hand, to restore him to his father.

units.leftText: So when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped him of his robe — the robe of many colors he was wearing —
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Joseph was come unto his brethren, that they stripped Joseph of his coat, the coat of many colors that was on him;

units.leftText: and they took him and threw him into the pit. Now the pit was empty, with no water in it.
units.rightText: and they took him, and cast him into the pit: and the pit was empty, there was no water in it.

units.leftText: And as they sat down to eat a meal, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were carrying spices, balm, and myrrh on their way down to Egypt.
units.rightText: And they sat down to eat bread: and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and, behold, a caravan of Ishmaelites was coming from Gilead, with their camels bearing spicery and balm and myrrh, going to carry it down to Egypt.

units.leftText: Then Judah said to his brothers, “What profit will we gain if we kill our brother and cover up his blood?
units.rightText: And Judah said unto his brethren, What profit is it if we slay our brother and conceal his blood?

units.leftText: Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites and not lay a hand on him; for he is our brother, our own flesh.” And they agreed.
units.rightText: Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother, our flesh. And his brethren hearkened unto him.

units.leftText: So when the Midianite traders passed by, his brothers pulled Joseph out of the pit and sold him for twenty shekels of silver to the Ishmaelites, who took him to Egypt.
units.rightText: And there passed by Midianites, merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. And they brought Joseph into Egypt.
leftNotes: 37:28 20 shekels is approximately 8 ounces or 228 grams of silver.

units.leftText: When Reuben returned to the pit and saw that Joseph was not there, he tore his clothes,
units.rightText: And Reuben returned unto the pit; and, behold, Joseph was not in the pit; and he rent his clothes.

units.leftText: returned to his brothers, and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?” Jacob Mourns Joseph
units.rightText: And he returned unto his brethren, and said, The child is not; and I, whither shall I go?

units.leftText: Then they took Joseph’s robe, slaughtered a young goat, and dipped the robe in its blood.
units.rightText: And they took Joseph’s coat, and killed a he-goat, and dipped the coat in the blood;

units.leftText: They sent the robe of many colors to their father and said, “We found this. Examine it to see whether it is your son’s robe or not.”
units.rightText: and they sent the coat of many colors, and they brought it to their father, and said, This have we found: know now whether it is thy son’s coat or not.

units.leftText: His father recognized it and said, “It is my son’s robe! A vicious animal has devoured him. Joseph has surely been torn to pieces!”
units.rightText: And he knew it, and said, It is my son’s coat: an evil beast hath devoured him; Joseph is without doubt torn in pieces.

units.leftText: Then Jacob tore his clothes, put sackcloth around his waist, and mourned for his son many days.
units.rightText: And Jacob rent his garments, and put sackcloth upon his loins, and mourned for his son many days.

units.leftText: All his sons and daughters tried to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No, ” he said. “I will go down to Sheol mourning for my son.” So his father wept for him.
units.rightText: And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I will go down to Sheol to my son mourning. And his father wept for him.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard.
units.rightText: And the Midianites sold him into Egypt unto Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh’s, the captain of the guard.
leftNotes: 37:36 Hebrew the Medanites

units.leftText: About that time, Judah left his brothers and settled near a man named Hirah, an Adullamite.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at that time, that Judah went down from his brethren, and turned in to a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.

units.leftText: There Judah saw the daughter of a Canaanite man named Shua, and he took her as a wife and slept with her.
units.rightText: And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite whose name was Shua; and he took her, and went in unto her.

units.leftText: So she conceived and gave birth to a son, and Judah named him Er.
units.rightText: And she conceived, and bare a son; and he called his name Er.

units.leftText: Again she conceived and gave birth to a son, and she named him Onan.
units.rightText: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and she called his name Onan.

units.leftText: Then she gave birth to another son and named him Shelah; it was at Chezib that she gave birth to him.
units.rightText: And she yet again bare a son, and called his name Shelah: and he was at Chezib, when she bare him.

units.leftText: Now Judah acquired a wife for Er, his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
units.rightText: And Judah took a wife for Er his first-born, and her name was Tamar.

units.leftText: But Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD; so the LORD put him to death.
units.rightText: And Er, Judah’s first-born, was wicked in the sight of Jehovah; and Jehovah slew him.

units.leftText: Then Judah said to Onan, “Sleep with your brother’s wife. Perform your duty as her brother-in-law and raise up offspring for your brother.”
units.rightText: And Judah said unto Onan, Go in unto thy brother’s wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother unto her, and raise up seed to thy brother.

units.leftText: But Onan knew that the offspring would not belong to him; so whenever he would sleep with his brother’s wife, he would spill his seed on the ground so that he would not produce offspring for his brother.
units.rightText: And Onan knew that the seed would not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother’s wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest he should give seed to his brother.

units.leftText: What he did was wicked in the sight of the LORD, so He put Onan to death as well.
units.rightText: And the thing which he did was evil in the sight of Jehovah: and he slew him also.

units.leftText: Then Judah said to his daughter-in-law Tamar, “Live as a widow in your father’s house until my son Shelah grows up.” For he thought, “He may die too, like his brothers.” So Tamar went to live in her father’s house.
units.rightText: Then said Judah to Tamar his daughter-in-law, Remain a widow in thy father’s house, till Shelah my son be grown up; for he said, Lest he also die, like his brethren. And Tamar went and dwelt in her father’s house.

units.leftText: After a long time Judah’s wife, the daughter of Shua, died. When Judah had finished mourning, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite went up to his sheepshearers at Timnah.
units.rightText: And in process of time Shua’s daughter, the wife of Judah, died; and Judah was comforted, and went up unto his sheep-shearers to Timnah, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.

units.leftText: When Tamar was told, “Your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep,”
units.rightText: And it was told Tamar, saying, Behold, thy father-in-law goeth up to Timnah to shear his sheep.

units.leftText: she removed her widow’s garments, covered her face with a veil to disguise herself, and sat at the entrance to Enaim, which is on the way to Timnah. For she saw that although Shelah had grown up, she had not been given to him as a wife.
units.rightText: And she put off from her the garments of her widowhood, and covered herself with her veil, and wrapped herself, and sat in the gate of Enaim, which is by the way to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah was grown up, and she was not given unto him to wife.

units.leftText: When Judah saw her, he thought she was a prostitute because she had covered her face.
units.rightText: When Judah saw her, he thought her to be a harlot; for she had covered her face.

units.leftText: Not realizing that she was his daughter-in-law, he went over to her and said, “Come now, let me sleep with you.” “What will you give me for sleeping with you?” she inquired.
units.rightText: And he turned unto her by the way, and said, Come, I pray thee, let me come in unto thee: for he knew not that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, What wilt thou give me, that thou mayest come in unto me?

units.leftText: “I will send you a young goat from my flock,” Judah answered. But she replied, “Only if you leave me something as a pledge until you send it.”
units.rightText: And he said, I will send thee a kid of the goats from the flock. And she said, Wilt thou give me a pledge, till thou send it?

units.leftText: “What pledge should I give you?” he asked.
units.rightText: And he said, What pledge shall I give thee? And she said, Thy signet and thy cord, and thy staff that is in thy hand. And he gave them to her, and came in unto her, and she conceived by him.

units.leftText: Then Tamar got up and departed. And she removed her veil and put on her widow’s garments again.
units.rightText: And she arose, and went away, and put off her veil from her, and put on the garments of her widowhood.

units.leftText: Now when Judah sent his friend Hirah the Adullamite with the young goat to collect the items he had left with the woman, he could not find her.
units.rightText: And Judah sent the kid of the goats by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive the pledge from the woman’s hand: but he found her not.

units.leftText: He asked the men of that place, “Where is the shrine prostitute who was beside the road at Enaim?” “No shrine prostitute has been here,” they answered.
units.rightText: Then he asked the men of her place, saying, Where is the prostitute, that was at Enaim by the wayside? And they said, There hath been no prostitute here.

units.leftText: So Hirah returned to Judah and said, “I could not find her, and furthermore, the men of that place said, ‘No shrine prostitute has been here.’”
units.rightText: And he returned to Judah, and said, I have not found her; and also the men of the place said, There hath been no prostitute here.

units.leftText: “Let her keep the items,” Judah replied. “Otherwise we will become a laughingstock. After all, I did send her this young goat, but you could not find her.”
units.rightText: And Judah said, Let her take it to her, lest we be put to shame: behold, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her.
leftNotes: 38:23 Or we will become despised

units.leftText: About three months later, Judah was told, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has prostituted herself, and now she is pregnant.” “Bring her out!” Judah replied. “Let her be burned to death!”
units.rightText: And it came to pass about three months after, that it was told Judah, saying, Tamar thy daughter-in-law hath played the harlot; and moreover, behold, she is with child by whoredom. And Judah said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt.

units.leftText: As she was being brought out, Tamar sent a message to her father-in-law: “I am pregnant by the man to whom these items belong.” And she added, “Please examine them. Whose seal and cord and staff are these?”
units.rightText: When she was brought forth, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, By the man, whose these are, am I with child: and she said, Discern, I pray thee, whose are these, the signet, and the cords, and the staff.

units.leftText: Judah recognized the items and said, “She is more righteous than I, since I did not give her to my son Shelah.” And he did not have relations with her again. The Birth of Perez and Zerah
units.rightText: And Judah acknowledged them, and said, She is more righteous than I, forasmuch as I gave her not to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more.

units.leftText: When the time came for Tamar to give birth, there were twins in her womb.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the time of her travail, that, behold, twins were in her womb.

units.leftText: And as she was giving birth, one of them put out his hand; so the midwife took a scarlet thread and tied it around his wrist. “This one came out first,” she announced.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when she travailed, that one put out a hand: and the midwife took and bound upon his hand a scarlet thread, saying, This came out first.

units.leftText: But when he pulled his hand back and his brother came out, she said, “You have broken out first!” So he was named Perez.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as he drew back his hand, that, behold, his brother came out: and she said, Wherefore hast thou made a breach for thyself? therefore his name was called Perez.
leftNotes: 38:29 Perez means breaking out.

units.leftText: Then his brother came out with the scarlet thread around his wrist, and he was named Zerah.
units.rightText: And afterward came out his brother, that had the scarlet thread upon his hand: and his name was called Zerah.
leftNotes: 38:30 Zerah can mean scarlet or brightness.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, Joseph had been taken down to Egypt, where an Egyptian named Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had taken him there.
units.rightText: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh’s, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hand of the Ishmaelites, that had brought him down thither.

units.leftText: And the LORD was with Joseph, and he became a successful man, serving in the household of his Egyptian master.
units.rightText: And Jehovah was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.

units.leftText: When his master saw that the LORD was with him and made him prosper in all he did,
units.rightText: And his master saw that Jehovah was with him, and that Jehovah made all that he did to prosper in his hand.

units.leftText: Joseph found favor in his sight and became his personal attendant.
units.rightText: And Joseph found favor in his sight, and he ministered unto him: and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.

units.leftText: From the time that he put Joseph in charge of his household and all he owned, the LORD blessed the Egyptian’s household on account of him. The LORD’s blessing was on everything he owned, both in his house and in his field.
units.rightText: And it came to pass from the time that he made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that Jehovah blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of Jehovah was upon all that he had, in the house and in the field.

units.leftText: So Potiphar left all that he owned in Joseph’s care; he did not concern himself with anything except the food he ate.
units.rightText: And he left all that he had in Joseph’s hand; and he knew not aught that was with him, save the bread which he did eat. And Joseph was comely, and well-favored.

units.leftText: and after some time his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph and said, “Sleep with me.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass after these things, that his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.

units.leftText: But he refused. “Look,” he said to his master’s wife, “with me here, my master does not concern himself with anything in his house, and he has entrusted everything he owns to my care.
units.rightText: But he refused, and said unto his master’s wife, Behold, my master knoweth not what is with me in the house, and he hath put all that he hath into my hand:

units.leftText: No one in this house is greater than I am. He has withheld nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. So how could I do such a great evil and sin against God?”
units.rightText: he is not greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back anything from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?

units.leftText: Although Potiphar’s wife spoke to Joseph day after day, he refused to go to bed with her or even be near her.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as she spake to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not unto her, to lie by her, or to be with her.

units.leftText: One day, however, Joseph went into the house to attend to his work, and not a single household servant was inside.
units.rightText: And it came to pass about this time, that he went into the house to do his work; and there was none of the men of the house there within.

units.leftText: She grabbed Joseph by his cloak and said, “Sleep with me!” But leaving his cloak in her hand, he escaped and ran outside. Joseph Falsely Imprisoned
units.rightText: And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.

units.leftText: When she saw that he had left his cloak in her hand and had run out of the house,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and was fled forth,

units.leftText: she called her household servants. “Look,” she said, “this Hebrew has been brought to us to make sport of us. He came to me so he could sleep with me, but I screamed as loud as I could.
units.rightText: that she called unto the men of her house, and spake unto them, saying, See, he hath brought in a Hebrew unto us to mock us: he came in unto me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice:

units.leftText: When he heard me scream for help, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house.”
units.rightText: and it came to pass, when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment by me, and fled, and got him out.

units.leftText: So Potiphar’s wife kept Joseph’s cloak beside her until his master came home.
units.rightText: And she laid up his garment by her, until his master came home.

units.leftText: Then she told him the same story: “The Hebrew slave you brought us came to me to make sport of me,
units.rightText: And she spake unto him according to these words, saying, The Hebrew servant, whom thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me:

units.leftText: but when I screamed for help, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house.”
units.rightText: and it came to pass, as I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment by me, and fled out.

units.leftText: When his master heard the story his wife told him, saying, “This is what your slave did to me,” he burned with anger.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spake unto him, saying, After this manner did thy servant to me; that his wrath was kindled.

units.leftText: So Joseph’s master took him and had him thrown into the prison where the king’s prisoners were confined.
units.rightText: And Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison.

units.leftText: the LORD was with him and extended kindness to him, granting him favor in the eyes of the prison warden.
units.rightText: But Jehovah was with Joseph, and showed kindness unto him, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.

units.leftText: And the warden put all the prisoners under Joseph’s care, so that he was responsible for all that was done in the prison.
units.rightText: And the keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners that were in the prison; and whatsoever they did there, he was the doer of it.

units.leftText: The warden did not concern himself with anything under Joseph’s care, because the LORD was with Joseph and gave him success in whatever he did.
units.rightText: The keeper of the prison looked not to anything that was under his hand, because Jehovah was with him; and that which he did, Jehovah made it to prosper.

units.leftText: Some time later, the king’s cupbearer and baker offended their master, the king of Egypt.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after these things, that the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker offended their lord the king of Egypt.

units.leftText: Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker,
units.rightText: And Pharaoh was wroth against his two officers, against the chief of the butlers, and against the chief of the bakers.

units.leftText: and imprisoned them in the house of the captain of the guard, the same prison where Joseph was confined.
units.rightText: And he put them in ward in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph was bound.

units.leftText: The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he became their personal attendant.
units.rightText: And the captain of the guard charged Joseph with them, and he ministered unto them: and they continued a season in ward.

units.leftText: both of these men — the Egyptian king’s cupbearer and baker, who were being held in the prison — had a dream on the same night, and each dream had its own meaning.
units.rightText: And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were bound in the prison.

units.leftText: When Joseph came to them in the morning, he saw that they were distraught.
units.rightText: And Joseph came in unto them in the morning, and saw them, and, behold, they were sad.

units.leftText: So he asked the officials of Pharaoh who were in custody with him in his master’s house, “Why are your faces so downcast today?”
units.rightText: And he asked Pharaoh’s officers that were with him in ward in his master’s house, saying, Wherefore look ye so sad to-day?

units.leftText: “We both had dreams,” they replied, “but there is no one to interpret them.” Then Joseph said to them, “Don’t interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams.”
units.rightText: And they said unto him, We have dreamed a dream, and there is none that can interpret it. And Joseph said unto them, Do not interpretations belong to God? tell it me, I pray you.

units.leftText: So the chief cupbearer told Joseph his dream: “In my dream there was a vine before me,
units.rightText: And the chief butler told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, In my dream, behold, a vine was before me;

units.leftText: and on the vine were three branches. As it budded, its blossoms opened and its clusters ripened into grapes.
units.rightText: and in the vine were three branches: and it was as though it budded, and its blossoms shot forth; and the clusters thereof brought forth ripe grapes:

units.leftText: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes, squeezed them into his cup, and placed the cup in his hand.”
units.rightText: and Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.

units.leftText: Joseph replied, “This is the interpretation: The three branches are three days.
units.rightText: And Joseph said unto him, This is the interpretation of it: the three branches are three days;

units.leftText: Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore your position. You will put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand, just as you did when you were his cupbearer.
units.rightText: within yet three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head, and restore thee unto thine office: and thou shalt give Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, after the former manner when thou wast his butler.

units.leftText: But when it goes well for you, please remember me and show me kindness by mentioning me to Pharaoh, that he might bring me out of this prison.
units.rightText: But have me in thy remembrance when it shall be well with thee, and show kindness, I pray thee, unto me, and make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:

units.leftText: For I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and even here I have done nothing for which they should have put me in this dungeon.”
units.rightText: for indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.

units.leftText: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was favorable, he said to Joseph, “I too had a dream: There were three baskets of white bread on my head.
units.rightText: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said unto Joseph, I also was in my dream, and, behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head:

units.leftText: In the top basket were all sorts of baked goods for Pharaoh, but the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head.”
units.rightText: and in the uppermost basket there was of all manner of baked food for Pharaoh; and the birds did eat them out of the basket upon my head.

units.leftText: Joseph replied, “This is the interpretation: The three baskets are three days.
units.rightText: And Joseph answered and said, This is the interpretation thereof: the three baskets are three days;

units.leftText: Within three days Pharaoh will lift off your head and hang you on a tree. Then the birds will eat the flesh of your body.”
units.rightText: within yet three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.
leftNotes: 40:19 Or and impale you on a pole; similarly in verse 22

units.leftText: On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he held a feast for all his officials, and in their presence he lifted up the heads of the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.
units.rightText: And it came to pass the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, that he made a feast unto all his servants: and he lifted up the head of the chief butler and the head of the chief baker among his servants.

units.leftText: Pharaoh restored the chief cupbearer to his position, so that he once again placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.
units.rightText: And he restored the chief butler unto his butlership again; and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand:

units.leftText: But Pharaoh hanged the chief baker, just as Joseph had described to them in his interpretation.
units.rightText: but he hanged the chief baker: as Joseph had interpreted to them.
leftNotes: 40:22 Literally had interpreted to them

units.leftText: The chief cupbearer, however, did not remember Joseph; he forgot all about him.
units.rightText: Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.

units.leftText: After two full years had passed, Pharaoh had a dream: He was standing beside the Nile,
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and, behold, he stood by the river.

units.leftText: when seven cows, sleek and well-fed, came up from the river and began to graze among the reeds.
units.rightText: And, behold, there came up out of the river seven kine, well-favored and fat-fleshed; and they fed in the reed-grass.

units.leftText: After them, seven other cows, sickly and thin, came up from the Nile and stood beside the well-fed cows on the bank of the river.
units.rightText: And, behold, seven other kine came up after them out of the river, ill-favored and lean-fleshed, and stood by the other kine upon the brink of the river.

units.leftText: And the cows that were sickly and thin devoured the seven sleek, well-fed cows.
units.rightText: And the ill-favored and lean-fleshed kine did eat up the seven well-favored and fat kine. So Pharaoh awoke.

units.leftText: but he fell back asleep and dreamed a second time: Seven heads of grain, plump and ripe, came up on one stalk.
units.rightText: And he slept and dreamed a second time: and, behold, seven ears of grain came up upon one stalk, rank and good.

units.leftText: After them, seven other heads of grain sprouted, thin and scorched by the east wind.
units.rightText: And, behold, seven ears, thin and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.

units.leftText: And the thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven plump, ripe ones. Then Pharaoh awoke and realized it was a dream.
units.rightText: And the thin ears swallowed up the seven rank and full ears. And Pharaoh awoke, and, behold, it was a dream.

units.leftText: In the morning his spirit was troubled, so he summoned all the magicians and wise men of Egypt. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but no one could interpret them for him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in the morning that his spirit was troubled; and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt, and all the wise men thereof: and Pharaoh told them his dream; but there was none that could interpret them unto Pharaoh.

units.leftText: Then the chief cupbearer said to Pharaoh, “Today I recall my failures.
units.rightText: Then spake the chief butler unto Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day:

units.leftText: Pharaoh was once angry with his servants, and he put me and the chief baker in the custody of the captain of the guard.
units.rightText: Pharaoh was wroth with his servants, and put me in ward in the house of the captain of the guard, me and the chief baker:

units.leftText: One night both the chief baker and I had dreams, and each dream had its own meaning.
units.rightText: and we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he; we dreamed each man according to the interpretation of his dream.

units.leftText: Now a young Hebrew was there with us, a servant of the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams and he interpreted them for us individually.
units.rightText: And there was with us there a young man, a Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard; and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams; to each man according to his dream he did interpret.

units.leftText: And it happened to us just as he had interpreted: I was restored to my position, and the other man was hanged.” Joseph Interprets Pharaoh’s Dreams
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it was; me he restored unto mine office, and him he hanged.

units.leftText: So Pharaoh sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of the dungeon. After he had shaved and changed his clothes, he went in before Pharaoh.
units.rightText: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.

units.leftText: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I had a dream, and no one can interpret it. But I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I have dreamed a dream, and there is none that can interpret it: and I have heard say of thee, that when thou hearest a dream thou canst interpret it.

units.leftText: “I myself cannot do it,” Joseph replied, “but God will give Pharaoh a sound answer.”
units.rightText: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.

units.leftText: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph: “In my dream I was standing on the bank of the Nile,
units.rightText: And Pharaoh spake unto Joseph, In my dream, behold, I stood upon the brink of the river:

units.leftText: when seven cows, well-fed and sleek, came up from the river and began to graze among the reeds.
units.rightText: and, behold, there came up out of the river seven kine, fat-fleshed and well-favored: and they fed in the reed-grass:

units.leftText: After them, seven other cows— sickly, ugly, and thin— came up. I have never seen such ugly cows in all the land of Egypt!
units.rightText: and, behold, seven other kine came up after them, poor and very ill-favored and lean-fleshed, such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for badness:

units.leftText: Then the thin, ugly cows devoured the seven well-fed cows that were there first.
units.rightText: and the lean and ill-favored kine did eat up the first seven fat kine:

units.leftText: When they had devoured them, however, no one could tell that they had done so; their appearance was as ugly as it had been before. Then I awoke.
units.rightText: and when they had eaten them up, it could not be known that they had eaten them; but they were still ill-favored, as at the beginning. So I awoke.

units.leftText: In my dream I also saw seven heads of grain, plump and ripe, growing on a single stalk.
units.rightText: And I saw in my dream, and, behold, seven ears came up upon one stalk, full and good:

units.leftText: After them, seven other heads of grain sprouted— withered, thin, and scorched by the east wind.
units.rightText: and, behold, seven ears, withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them:

units.leftText: And the thin heads of grain swallowed the seven plump ones. I told this dream to the magicians, but no one could explain it to me.”
units.rightText: and the thin ears swallowed up the seven good ears: and I told it unto the magicians; but there was none that could declare it to me.

units.leftText: At this, Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dreams of Pharaoh are one and the same. God has revealed to Pharaoh what He is about to do.
units.rightText: And Joseph said unto Pharaoh, The dream of Pharaoh is one: what God is about to do he hath declared unto Pharaoh.

units.leftText: The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven ripe heads of grain are seven years. The dreams have the same meaning.
units.rightText: The seven good kine are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one.

units.leftText: Moreover, the seven thin, ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and so are the seven worthless heads of grain scorched by the east wind — they are seven years of famine.
units.rightText: And the seven lean and ill-favored kine that came up after them are seven years, and also the seven empty ears blasted with the east wind; they shall be seven years of famine.

units.leftText: It is just as I said to Pharaoh: God has shown Pharaoh what He is about to do.
units.rightText: That is the thing which I spake unto Pharaoh: what God is about to do he hath showed unto Pharaoh.

units.leftText: Behold, seven years of great abundance are coming throughout the land of Egypt,
units.rightText: Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt:

units.leftText: but seven years of famine will follow them. Then all the abundance in the land of Egypt will be forgotten, and the famine will devastate the land.
units.rightText: and there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land;

units.leftText: The abundance in the land will not be remembered, since the famine that follows it will be so severe.
units.rightText: and the plenty shall not be known in the land by reason of that famine which followeth; for it shall be very grievous.

units.leftText: Moreover, because the dream was given to Pharaoh in two versions, the matter has been decreed by God, and He will carry it out shortly.
units.rightText: And for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh, it is because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.

units.leftText: Now, therefore, Pharaoh should look for a discerning and wise man and set him over the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Let Pharaoh take action and appoint commissioners over the land to take a fifth of the harvest of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.
units.rightText: Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint overseers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt in the seven plenteous years.
leftNotes: 41:34 See LXX; MT a fifth from the land

units.leftText: Under the authority of Pharaoh, let them collect all the excess food from these good years, that they may come and lay up the grain to be preserved as food in the cities.
units.rightText: And let them gather all the food of these good years that come, and lay up grain under the hand of Pharaoh for food in the cities, and let them keep it.

units.leftText: This food will be a reserve for the land during the seven years of famine to come upon the land of Egypt. Then the country will not perish in the famine.” Joseph Given Charge of Egypt
units.rightText: And the food shall be for a store to the land against the seven years of famine, which shall be in the land of Egypt; that the land perish not through the famine.

units.leftText: This proposal pleased Pharaoh and all his officials.
units.rightText: And the thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.

units.leftText: So Pharaoh asked them, “Can we find anyone like this man, in whom the Spirit of God abides?”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom the spirit of God is?
leftNotes: 41:38 Or the spirit of the gods

units.leftText: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one as discerning and wise as you.
units.rightText: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath showed thee all this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou:

units.leftText: You shall be in charge of my house, and all my people are to obey your commands. Only with regard to the throne will I be greater than you.”
units.rightText: thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou.

units.leftText: Pharaoh also told Joseph, “I hereby place you over all the land of Egypt.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Then Pharaoh removed the signet ring from his finger, put it on Joseph’s finger, clothed him in garments of fine linen, and placed a gold chain around his neck.
units.rightText: And Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;

units.leftText: He had Joseph ride in his second chariot, with men calling out before him, “Bow the knee!” So he placed him over all the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: and he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee: and he set him over all the land of Egypt.
leftNotes: 41:43 That is, “Abrek,” probably an Egyptian word that sounds similar to the Hebrew for kneel

units.leftText: And Pharaoh declared to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh, but without your permission, no one in all the land of Egypt shall lift his hand or foot.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I am Pharaoh, and without thee shall no man lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-paneah, and he gave him Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, to be his wife. And Joseph took charge of all the land of Egypt. The Seven Years of Plenty
units.rightText: And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphenath-paneah; and he gave him to wife Asenath, the daughter of Poti-phera priest of On. And Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.
leftNotes: 41:45 Zaphenath-paneah probably means Revealer of Mysteries or God speaks and lives.
41:45 That is, Heliopolis, as in LXX; also in verse 50

units.leftText: Now Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph left Pharaoh’s presence and traveled throughout the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: During the seven years of abundance, the land brought forth bountifully.
units.rightText: And in the seven plenteous years the earth brought forth by handfuls.

units.leftText: During those seven years, Joseph collected all the excess food in the land of Egypt and stored it in the cities. In every city he laid up the food from the fields around it.
units.rightText: And he gathered up all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities: the food of the field, which was round about every city, laid he up in the same.

units.leftText: So Joseph stored up grain in such abundance, like the sand of the sea, that he stopped keeping track of it; for it was beyond measure.
units.rightText: And Joseph laid up grain as the sand of the sea, very much, until he left off numbering; for it was without number.

units.leftText: Before the years of famine arrived, two sons were born to Joseph by Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.
units.rightText: And unto Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Poti-phera priest of On, bare unto him.

units.leftText: Joseph named the firstborn Manasseh, saying, “God has made me forget all my hardship and all my father’s household.”
units.rightText: And Joseph called the name of the first-born Manasseh: For, said he, God hath made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.
leftNotes: 41:51 Manasseh sounds like the Hebrew for making to forget.

units.leftText: And the second son he named Ephraim, saying, “God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.” The Famine Begins
units.rightText: And the name of the second called he Ephraim: For God hath made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.
leftNotes: 41:52 Ephraim sounds like the Hebrew for making fruitful or twice fruitful.

units.leftText: When the seven years of abundance in the land of Egypt came to an end,
units.rightText: And the seven years of plenty, that was in the land of Egypt, came to an end.

units.leftText: the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. And although there was famine in every country, there was food throughout the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And the seven years of famine began to come, according as Joseph had said: and there was famine in all lands; but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.

units.leftText: When extreme hunger came to all the land of Egypt and the people cried out to Pharaoh for food, he told all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph and do whatever he tells you.”
units.rightText: And when all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread: and Pharaoh said unto all the Egyptians, Go unto Joseph; what he saith to you, do.

units.leftText: When the famine had spread over all the land, Joseph opened up all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians; for the famine was severe in the land of Egypt.
units.rightText: And the famine was over all the face of the earth: and Joseph opened all the store-houses, and sold unto the Egyptians; and the famine was sore in the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: And every nation came to Joseph in Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was severe over all the earth.
units.rightText: And all countries came into Egypt to Joseph to buy grain, because the famine was sore in all the earth.

units.leftText: When Jacob learned that there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you staring at one another?”
units.rightText: Now Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said unto his sons, Why do ye look one upon another?

units.leftText: “Look,” he added, “I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy some for us, so that we may live and not die.”
units.rightText: And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt: get you down thither, and buy for us from thence; that we may live, and not die.

units.leftText: So ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
units.rightText: And Joseph’s ten brethren went down to buy grain from Egypt.

units.leftText: But Jacob did not send Joseph’s brother Benjamin with his brothers, for he said, “I am afraid that harm might befall him.”
units.rightText: But Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, Jacob sent not with his brethren; for he said, Lest peradventure harm befall him.

units.leftText: So the sons of Israel were among those who came to buy grain, since the famine had also spread to the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: And the sons of Israel came to buy among those that came: for the famine was in the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: Now Joseph was the ruler of the land; he was the one who sold grain to all its people. So when his brothers arrived, they bowed down before him with their faces to the ground.
units.rightText: And Joseph was the governor over the land; he it was that sold to all the people of the land. And Joseph’s brethren came, and bowed down themselves to him with their faces to the earth.

units.leftText: And when Joseph saw his brothers, he recognized them, but he treated them as strangers and spoke harshly to them. “Where have you come from?” he asked. “From the land of Canaan,” they replied. “We are here to buy food.”
units.rightText: And Joseph saw his brethren, and he knew them, but made himself strange unto them, and spake roughly with them; and he said unto them, Whence come ye? And they said, From the land of Canaan to buy food.

units.leftText: Although Joseph recognized his brothers, they did not recognize him.
units.rightText: And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.

units.leftText: Joseph remembered his dreams about them and said, “You are spies! You have come to see if our land is vulnerable.”
units.rightText: And Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed of them, and said unto them, Ye are spies; to see the nakedness of the land ye are come.

units.leftText: “Not so, my lord,” they replied. “Your servants have come to buy food.
units.rightText: And they said unto him, Nay, my lord, but to buy food are thy servants come.

units.leftText: We are all sons of one man. Your servants are honest men, not spies.”
units.rightText: We are all one man’s sons; we are true men, thy servants are no spies.

units.leftText: “No,” he told them. “You have come to see if our land is vulnerable.”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Nay, but to see the nakedness of the land ye are come.

units.leftText: But they answered, “Your servants are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan. The youngest is now with our father, and one is no more.”
units.rightText: And they said, We thy servants are twelve brethren, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and, behold, the youngest is this day with our father, and one is not.

units.leftText: Then Joseph declared, “Just as I said, you are spies!
units.rightText: And Joseph said unto them, That is it that I spake unto you, saying, Ye are spies:

units.leftText: And this is how you will be tested: As surely as Pharaoh lives, you shall not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here.
units.rightText: hereby ye shall be proved: by the life of Pharaoh ye shall not go forth hence, except your youngest brother come hither.

units.leftText: Send one of your number to get your brother; the rest of you will be confined so that the truth of your words may be tested. If they are untrue, then as surely as Pharaoh lives, you are spies!”
units.rightText: Send one of you, and let him fetch your brother, and ye shall be bound, that your words may be proved, whether there be truth in you: or else by the life of Pharaoh surely ye are spies.

units.leftText: So Joseph imprisoned them for three days,
units.rightText: And he put them all together into ward three days.

units.leftText: and on the third day he said to them, “I fear God. So do this and you will live:
units.rightText: And Joseph said unto them the third day, This do, and live; for I fear God:

units.leftText: If you are honest, leave one of your brothers in custody while the rest of you go and take back grain to relieve the hunger of your households.
units.rightText: if ye be true men, let one of your brethren be bound in your prison-house; but go ye, carry grain for the famine of your houses:

units.leftText: Then bring your youngest brother to me so that your words can be verified, that you may not die.” And to this they consented.
units.rightText: and bring your youngest brother unto me; so shall your words be verified, and ye shall not die. And they did so.

units.leftText: Then they said to one another, “Surely we are being punished because of our brother. We saw his anguish when he pleaded with us, but we would not listen. That is why this distress has come upon us.”
units.rightText: And they said one to another, We are verily guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul, when he besought us, and we would not hear; therefore is this distress come upon us.

units.leftText: And Reuben responded, “Didn’t I tell you not to sin against the boy? But you would not listen. Now we must account for his blood!”
units.rightText: And Reuben answered them, saying, Spake I not unto you, saying, Do not sin against the child; and ye would not hear? therefore also, behold, his blood is required.

units.leftText: They did not realize that Joseph understood them, since there was an interpreter between them.
units.rightText: And they knew not that Joseph understood them; for there was an interpreter between them.

units.leftText: And he turned away from them and wept. When he turned back and spoke to them, he took Simeon from them and had him bound before their eyes. Joseph’s Brothers Return to Canaan
units.rightText: And he turned himself about from them, and wept; and he returned to them, and spake to them, and took Simeon from among them, and bound him before their eyes.

units.leftText: Then Joseph gave orders to fill their bags with grain, to return each man’s silver to his sack, and to give them provisions for their journey. This order was carried out,
units.rightText: Then Joseph commanded to fill their vessels with grain, and to restore every man’s money into his sack, and to give them provision for the way: and thus was it done unto them.
leftNotes: 42:25 Or money; here and throughout chapters 42–44

units.leftText: and they loaded the grain on their donkeys and departed.
units.rightText: And they laded their asses with their grain, and departed thence.

units.leftText: At the place where they lodged for the night, one of them opened his sack to get feed for his donkey, and he saw his silver in the mouth of the sack.
units.rightText: And as one of them opened his sack to give his ass provender in the lodging-place, he espied his money; and, behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.

units.leftText: “My silver has been returned!” he said to his brothers. “It is here in my sack.” Their hearts sank, and trembling, they turned to one another and said, “What is this that God has done to us?”
units.rightText: And he said unto his brethren, My money is restored; and, lo, it is even in my sack: and their heart failed them, and they turned trembling one to another, saying, What is this that God hath done unto us?

units.leftText: When they reached their father Jacob in the land of Canaan, they described to him all that had happened to them:
units.rightText: And they came unto Jacob their father unto the land of Canaan, and told him all that had befallen them, saying,

units.leftText: “The man who is lord of the land spoke harshly to us and accused us of spying on the country.
units.rightText: The man, the lord of the land, spake roughly with us, and took us for spies of the country.

units.leftText: But we told him, ‘We are honest men, not spies.
units.rightText: And we said unto him, We are true men; we are no spies:

units.leftText: We are twelve brothers, sons of one father. One is no more, and the youngest is now with our father in the land of Canaan.’
units.rightText: we are twelve brethren, sons of our father; one is not, and the youngest is this day with our father in the land of Canaan.

units.leftText: Then the man who is lord of the land said to us, ‘This is how I will know whether you are honest: Leave one brother with me, take food to relieve the hunger of your households, and go.
units.rightText: And the man, the lord of the land, said unto us, Hereby shall I know that ye are true men: leave one of your brethren with me, and take grain for the famine of your houses, and go your way;

units.leftText: But bring your youngest brother back to me so I will know that you are not spies but honest men. Then I will give your brother back to you, and you can trade in the land.’”
units.rightText: and bring your youngest brother unto me: then shall I know that ye are no spies, but that ye are true men: so will I deliver you your brother, and ye shall traffic in the land.

units.leftText: As they began emptying their sacks, there in each man’s sack was his bag of silver! And when they and their father saw the bags of silver, they were dismayed.
units.rightText: And it came to pass as they emptied their sacks, that, behold, every man’s bundle of money was in his sack: and when they and their father saw their bundles of money, they were afraid.

units.leftText: Their father Jacob said to them, “You have deprived me of my sons. Joseph is gone and Simeon is no more. Now you want to take Benjamin. Everything is going against me!”
units.rightText: And Jacob their father said unto them, Me have ye bereaved of my children: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye will take Benjamin away: all these things are against me.

units.leftText: Then Reuben said to his father, “You may kill my two sons if I fail to bring him back to you. Put him in my care, and I will return him.”
units.rightText: And Reuben spake unto his father, saying, Slay my two sons, if I bring him not to thee: deliver him into my hand, and I will bring him to thee again.

units.leftText: But Jacob replied, “My son will not go down there with you, for his brother is dead, and he alone is left. If any harm comes to him on your journey, you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow.”
units.rightText: And he said, My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he only is left: if harm befall him by the way in which ye go, then will ye bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.

units.leftText: Now the famine was still severe in the land.
units.rightText: And the famine was sore in the land.

units.leftText: So when Jacob’s sons had eaten all the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, “Go back and buy us a little more food.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when they had eaten up the grain which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said unto them, Go again, buy us a little food.

units.leftText: But Judah replied, “The man solemnly warned us, ‘You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.’
units.rightText: And Judah spake unto him, saying, The man did solemnly protest unto us, saying, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.

units.leftText: If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.
units.rightText: If thou wilt send our brother with us, we will go down and buy thee food:

units.leftText: But if you will not send him, we will not go; for the man told us, ‘You will not see my face again unless your brother is with you.’”
units.rightText: but if thou wilt not send him, we will not go down; for the man said unto us, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.

units.leftText: “Why did you bring this trouble upon me?” Israel asked. “Why did you tell the man you had another brother?”
units.rightText: And Israel said, Wherefore dealt ye so ill with me, as to tell the man whether ye had yet a brother?

units.leftText: They replied, “The man questioned us in detail about ourselves and our family: ‘Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?’ And we answered him accordingly. How could we possibly know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother here’?”
units.rightText: And they said, The man asked straitly concerning ourselves, and concerning our kindred, saying, Is your father yet alive? have ye another brother? and we told him according to the tenor of these words: could we in any wise know that he would say, Bring your brother down?

units.leftText: And Judah said to his father Israel, “Send the boy with me, and we will go at once, so that we may live and not die— neither we, nor you, nor our children.
units.rightText: And Judah said unto Israel his father, Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go; that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, and also our little ones.

units.leftText: I will guarantee his safety. You may hold me personally responsible. If I do not bring him back and set him before you, then may I bear the guilt before you all my life.
units.rightText: I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him: if I bring him not unto thee, and set him before thee, then let me bear the blame for ever:

units.leftText: If we had not delayed, we could have come and gone twice by now.”
units.rightText: for except we had lingered, surely we had now returned a second time.

units.leftText: Then their father Israel said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: Put some of the best products of the land in your packs and carry them down as a gift for the man — a little balm and a little honey, spices and myrrh, pistachios and almonds.
units.rightText: And their father Israel said unto them, If it be so now, do this: take of the choice fruits of the land in your vessels, and carry down the man a present, a little balm, and a little honey, spicery and myrrh, nuts, and almonds;

units.leftText: Take double the silver with you so that you may return the silver that was put back into the mouths of your sacks. Perhaps it was a mistake.
units.rightText: and take double money in your hand; and the money that was returned in the mouth of your sacks carry again in your hand; peradventure it was an oversight:

units.leftText: Take your brother as well, and return to the man at once.
units.rightText: take also your brother, and arise, go again unto the man:

units.leftText: May God Almighty grant you mercy before the man, that he may release your other brother along with Benjamin. As for me, if I am bereaved, I am bereaved.”
units.rightText: and God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may release unto you your other brother and Benjamin. And if I be bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.
leftNotes: 43:14 Hebrew El-Shaddai

units.leftText: So the men took these gifts, along with double the amount of silver, and Benjamin as well. Then they hurried down to Egypt and stood before Joseph. Joseph’s Hospitality to His Brothers
units.rightText: And the men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and rose up, and went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.

units.leftText: When Joseph saw Benjamin with his brothers, he said to the steward of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and prepare it, for they shall dine with me at noon.”
units.rightText: And when Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, Bring the men into the house, and slay, and make ready; for the men shall dine with me at noon.

units.leftText: The man did as Joseph had commanded and took the brothers to Joseph’s house.
units.rightText: And the man did as Joseph bade; and the man brought the men to Joseph’s house.

units.leftText: But the brothers were frightened that they had been taken to Joseph’s house. “We have been brought here because of the silver that was returned in our bags the first time,” they said. “They intend to overpower us and take us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”
units.rightText: And the men were afraid, because they were brought to Joseph’s house; and they said, Because of the money that was returned in our sacks at the first time are we brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, and fall upon us, and take us for bondmen, and our asses.

units.leftText: So they approached Joseph’s steward and spoke to him at the entrance to the house.
units.rightText: And they came near to the steward of Joseph’s house, and they spake unto him at the door of the house,

units.leftText: “Please, sir,” they said, “we really did come down here the first time to buy food.
units.rightText: and said, Oh, my lord, we came indeed down at the first time to buy food:

units.leftText: But when we came to the place we lodged for the night, we opened our sacks and, behold, each of us found his silver in the mouth of his sack! It was the full amount of our silver, and we have brought it back with us.
units.rightText: and it came to pass, when we came to the lodging-place, that we opened our sacks, and, behold, every man’s money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight: and we have brought it again in our hand.

units.leftText: We have brought additional silver with us to buy food. We do not know who put our silver in our sacks.”
units.rightText: And other money have we brought down in our hand to buy food: we know not who put our money in our sacks.

units.leftText: “It is fine,” said the steward. “Do not be afraid. Your God, the God of your father, gave you the treasure that was in your sacks. I received your silver.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
units.rightText: And he said, Peace be to you, fear not: your God, and the God of your father, hath given you treasure in your sacks: I had your money. And he brought Simeon out unto them.

units.leftText: And the steward took the men into Joseph’s house, gave them water to wash their feet, and provided food for their donkeys.
units.rightText: And the man brought the men into Joseph’s house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet; and he gave their asses provender.

units.leftText: Since the brothers had been told that they were going to eat a meal there, they prepared their gift for Joseph’s arrival at noon.
units.rightText: And they made ready the present against Joseph’s coming at noon: for they heard that they should eat bread there.

units.leftText: When Joseph came home, they presented him with the gifts they had brought, and they bowed to the ground before him.
units.rightText: And when Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed down themselves to him to the earth.

units.leftText: He asked if they were well, and then he asked, “How is your elderly father you told me about? Is he still alive?”
units.rightText: And he asked them of their welfare, and said, Is your father well, the old man of whom ye spake? Is he yet alive?

units.leftText: “Your servant our father is well,” they answered. “He is still alive.” And they bowed down to honor him.
units.rightText: And they said, Thy servant our father is well, he is yet alive. And they bowed the head, and made obeisance.

units.leftText: When Joseph looked up and saw his brother Benjamin, his own mother’s son, he asked, “Is this your youngest brother, the one you told me about?” Then he declared, “May God be gracious to you, my son.”
units.rightText: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw Benjamin his brother, his mother’s son, and said, Is this your youngest brother, of whom ye spake unto me? And he said, God be gracious unto thee, my son.

units.leftText: Joseph hurried out because he was moved to tears for his brother, and he went to a private room to weep.
units.rightText: And Joseph made haste; for his heart yearned over his brother: and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there.

units.leftText: Then he washed his face and came back out. Regaining his composure, he said, “Serve the meal.”
units.rightText: And he washed his face, and came out; and he refrained himself, and said, Set on bread.

units.leftText: They separately served Joseph, his brothers, and the Egyptians. They ate separately because the Egyptians would not eat with the Hebrews, since that was detestable to them.
units.rightText: And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, that did eat with him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.

units.leftText: They were seated before Joseph in order by age, from the firstborn to the youngest, and the men looked at one another in astonishment.
units.rightText: And they sat before him, the first-born according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth: and the men marvelled one with another.

units.leftText: When the portions were served to them from Joseph’s table, Benjamin’s portion was five times larger than any of the others. So they feasted and drank freely with Joseph.
units.rightText: And he took and sent messes unto them from before him: but Benjamin’s mess was five times so much as any of theirs. And they drank, and were merry with him.

units.leftText: Then Joseph instructed his steward: “Fill the men’s sacks with as much food as they can carry, and put each one’s silver in the mouth of his sack.
units.rightText: And he commanded the steward of his house, saying, Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put every man’s money in his sack’s mouth.

units.leftText: Put my cup, the silver one, in the mouth of the youngest one’s sack, along with the silver for his grain.” So the steward did as Joseph had instructed.
units.rightText: And put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, and his grain money. And he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.

units.leftText: At daybreak, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
units.rightText: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their asses.

units.leftText: They had not gone far from the city when Joseph told his steward, “Pursue the men at once, and when you overtake them, ask, ‘Why have you repaid good with evil?
units.rightText: And when they were gone out of the city, and were not yet far off, Joseph said unto his steward, Up, follow after the men; and when thou dost overtake them, say unto them, Wherefore have ye rewarded evil for good?
leftNotes: 44:4 LXX includes Why have you stolen my silver cup?

units.leftText: Is this not the cup my master drinks from and uses for divination? What you have done is wicked!’”
units.rightText: Is not this that in which my lord drinketh, and whereby he indeed divineth? ye have done evil in so doing.
leftNotes: 44:5 Hebrew Is it not this which

units.leftText: When the steward overtook them, he relayed these words to them.
units.rightText: And he overtook them, and he spake unto them these words.

units.leftText: “Why does my lord say these things?” they asked. “Your servants could not possibly do such a thing.
units.rightText: And they said unto him, Wherefore speaketh my lord such words as these? Far be it from thy servants that they should do such a thing.

units.leftText: We even brought back to you from the land of Canaan the silver we found in the mouths of our sacks. Why would we steal silver or gold from your master’s house?
units.rightText: Behold, the money, which we found in our sacks’ mouths, we brought again unto thee out of the land of Canaan: how then should we steal out of thy lord’s house silver or gold?

units.leftText: If any of your servants is found to have it, he must die, and the rest will become slaves of my lord.”
units.rightText: With whomsoever of thy servants it be found, let him die, and we also will be my lord’s bondmen.

units.leftText: “As you say,” replied the steward. “But only the one who is found with the cup will be my slave, and the rest of you shall be free of blame.”
units.rightText: And he said, Now also let it be according unto your words: he with whom it is found shall be my bondman; and ye shall be blameless.

units.leftText: So each one quickly lowered his sack to the ground and opened it.
units.rightText: Then they hasted, and took down every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack.

units.leftText: The steward searched, beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest — and the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.
units.rightText: And he searched, and began at the eldest, and left off at the youngest: and the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.

units.leftText: Then they all tore their clothes, loaded their donkeys, and returned to the city.
units.rightText: Then they rent their clothes, and laded every man his ass, and returned to the city.

units.leftText: When Judah and his brothers arrived at Joseph’s house, he was still there, and they fell to the ground before him.
units.rightText: And Judah and his brethren came to Joseph’s house; and he was yet there: and they fell before him on the ground.

units.leftText: “What is this deed you have done?” Joseph declared. “Do you not know that a man like me can surely divine the truth?”
units.rightText: And Joseph said unto them, What deed is this that ye have done? know ye not that such a man as I can indeed divine?

units.leftText: “What can we say to my lord?” Judah replied. “How can we plead? How can we justify ourselves? God has exposed the iniquity of your servants. We are now my lord’s slaves— both we and the one who was found with the cup.”
units.rightText: And Judah said, What shall we say unto my lord? what shall we speak? or how shall we clear ourselves? God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants: behold, we are my lord’s bondmen, both we, and he also in whose hand the cup is found.

units.leftText: But Joseph replied, “Far be it from me to do this. The man who was found with the cup will be my slave. The rest of you may return to your father in peace.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
units.rightText: And he said, Far be it from me that I should do so: the man in whose hand the cup is found, he shall be my bondman; but as for you, get you up in peace unto your father.

units.leftText: Then Judah approached Joseph and said, “Sir, please let your servant speak personally to my lord. Do not be angry with your servant, for you are equal to Pharaoh himself.
units.rightText: Then Judah came near unto him, and said, Oh, my lord, let thy servant, I pray thee, speak a word in my lord’s ears, and let not thine anger burn against thy servant; for thou art even as Pharaoh.

units.leftText: My lord asked his servants, ‘Do you have a father or a brother?’
units.rightText: My lord asked his servants, saying, Have ye a father, or a brother?

units.leftText: And we answered, ‘We have an elderly father and a younger brother, the child of his old age. The boy’s brother is dead. He is the only one of his mother’s sons left, and his father loves him.’
units.rightText: And we said unto my lord, We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother; and his father loveth him.

units.leftText: Then you told your servants, ‘Bring him down to me so that I can see him for myself.’
units.rightText: And thou saidst unto thy servants, Bring him down unto me, that I may set mine eyes upon him.

units.leftText: So we said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father. If he were to leave, his father would die.’
units.rightText: And we said unto my lord, The lad cannot leave his father: for if he should leave his father, his father would die.

units.leftText: But you said to your servants, ‘Unless your younger brother comes down with you, you will not see my face again.’
units.rightText: And thou saidst unto thy servants, Except your youngest brother come down with you, ye shall see my face no more.

units.leftText: Now when we returned to your servant my father, we relayed your words to him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass when we came up unto thy servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.

units.leftText: Then our father said, ‘Go back and buy us some food.’
units.rightText: And our father said, Go again, buy us a little food.

units.leftText: But we answered, ‘We cannot go down there unless our younger brother goes with us. So if our younger brother is not with us, we cannot see the man.’
units.rightText: And we said, We cannot go down: if our youngest brother be with us, then will we go down; for we may not see the man’s face, except our youngest brother be with us.

units.leftText: And your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.
units.rightText: And thy servant my father said unto us, Ye know that my wife bare me two sons:

units.leftText: When one of them was gone, I said: “Surely he has been torn to pieces.” And I have not seen him since.
units.rightText: and the one went out from me, and I said, Surely he is torn in pieces; and I have not seen him since:

units.leftText: Now if you also take this one from me and harm comes to him, you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow.’
units.rightText: and if ye take this one also from me, and harm befall him, ye will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.

units.leftText: So if the boy is not with us when I return to your servant, and if my father, whose life is wrapped up in the boy’s life,
units.rightText: Now therefore when I come to thy servant my father, and the lad is not with us; seeing that his life is bound up in the lad’s life;

units.leftText: sees that the boy is not with us, he will die. Then your servants will have brought the gray hair of your servant our father down to Sheol in sorrow.
units.rightText: it will come to pass, when he seeth that the lad is not with us, that he will die: and thy servants will bring down the gray hairs of thy servant our father with sorrow to Sheol.

units.leftText: Indeed, your servant guaranteed the boy’s safety to my father, saying, ‘If I do not return him to you, I will bear the guilt before you, my father, all my life.’
units.rightText: For thy servant became surety for the lad unto my father, saying, If I bring him not unto thee, then shall I bear the blame to my father for ever.

units.leftText: Now please let your servant stay here as my lord’s slave in place of the boy. Let him return with his brothers.
units.rightText: Now therefore, let thy servant, I pray thee, abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren.

units.leftText: For how can I go back to my father without the boy? I could not bear to see the misery that would overwhelm him.”
units.rightText: For how shall I go up to my father, if the lad be not with me? lest I see the evil that shall come on my father.

units.leftText: Then Joseph could no longer control himself before all his attendants, and he cried out, “Send everyone away from me!”
units.rightText: Then Joseph could not refrain himself before all them that stood by him; and he cried, Cause every man to go out from me. And there stood no man with him, while Joseph made himself known unto his brethren.

units.leftText: But he wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard him, and Pharaoh’s household soon heard of it.
units.rightText: And he wept aloud: and the Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.

units.leftText: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?” But they were unable to answer him, because they were terrified in his presence.
units.rightText: And Joseph said unto his brethren, I am Joseph; doth my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him; for they were troubled at his presence.

units.leftText: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “Please come near me.” And they did so.
units.rightText: And Joseph said unto his brethren, Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said, I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt.

units.leftText: And now, do not be distressed or angry with yourselves that you sold me into this place, because it was to save lives that God sent me before you.
units.rightText: And now be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life.

units.leftText: For the famine has covered the land these two years, and there will be five more years without plowing or harvesting.
units.rightText: For these two years hath the famine been in the land: and there are yet five years, in which there shall be neither plowing nor harvest.

units.leftText: God sent me before you to preserve you as a remnant on the earth and to save your lives by a great deliverance.
units.rightText: And God sent me before you to preserve you a remnant in the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.
leftNotes: 45:7 Or and to keep you alive as a great band of survivors

units.leftText: Therefore it was not you who sent me here, but God, who has made me a father to Pharaoh — lord of all his household and ruler over all the land of Egypt. Joseph Sends for His Father
units.rightText: So now it was not you that sent me hither, but God: and he hath made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: Now return quickly to my father and tell him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me without delay.
units.rightText: Haste ye, and go up to my father, and say unto him, Thus saith thy son Joseph, God hath made me lord of all Egypt: come down unto me, tarry not;

units.leftText: You shall settle in the land of Goshen and be near me— you and your children and grandchildren, your flocks and herds, and everything you own.
units.rightText: and thou shalt dwell in the land of Goshen, and thou shalt be near unto me, thou, and thy children, and thy children’s children, and thy flocks, and thy herds, and all that thou hast:

units.leftText: And there I will provide for you, because there will be five more years of famine. Otherwise, you and your household and everything you own will come to destitution.’
units.rightText: and there will I nourish thee; for there are yet five years of famine; lest thou come to poverty, thou, and thy household, and all that thou hast.

units.leftText: Behold! You and my brother Benjamin can see that I, Joseph, am the one speaking with you.
units.rightText: And, behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaketh unto you.

units.leftText: Tell my father about all my splendor in Egypt and everything you have seen. And bring my father down here quickly.”
units.rightText: And ye shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that ye have seen: and ye shall haste and bring down my father hither.

units.leftText: Then Joseph threw his arms around his brother Benjamin and wept, and Benjamin wept as they embraced.
units.rightText: And he fell upon his brother Benjamin’s neck, and wept; and Benjamin wept upon his neck.

units.leftText: Joseph kissed each of his brothers as he wept over them. And afterward his brothers talked with him. Pharaoh Invites Jacob to Egypt
units.rightText: And he kissed all his brethren, and wept upon them: and after that his brethren talked with him.

units.leftText: When the news reached Pharaoh’s house that Joseph’s brothers had come, Pharaoh and his servants were pleased.
