units.rightText: And the report thereof was heard in Pharaoh’s house, saying, Joseph’s brethren are come: and it pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.

units.leftText: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Do as follows: Load your animals and return to the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Say unto thy brethren, This do ye: lade your beasts, and go, get you unto the land of Canaan;

units.leftText: Then bring your father and your families and return to me. I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat from the fat of the land.’
units.rightText: and take your father and your households, and come unto me: and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and ye shall eat the fat of the land.

units.leftText: You are also directed to tell them: ‘Take wagons from the land of Egypt for your young children and your wives, and bring your father and come back.
units.rightText: Now thou art commanded, this do ye: take you wagons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.

units.leftText: But pay no regard to your belongings, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.’”
units.rightText: Also regard not your stuff; for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.

units.leftText: So the sons of Israel did as they were told. Joseph gave them wagons as Pharaoh had instructed, and he also gave them provisions for their journey.
units.rightText: And the sons of Israel did so: and Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.

units.leftText: He gave new garments to each of them, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred shekels of silver and five sets of clothes.
units.rightText: To all of them he gave each man changes of raiment; but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver, and five changes of raiment.
leftNotes: 45:22 300 shekels is approximately 7.5 pounds or 3.4 kilograms of silver.

units.leftText: And he sent to his father the following: ten donkeys loaded with the best of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provisions for his father’s journey.
units.rightText: And to his father he sent after this manner: ten asses laden with the good things of Egypt, and ten she-asses laden with grain and bread and provision for his father by the way.

units.leftText: Then Joseph sent his brothers on their way, and as they were leaving, he said to them, “Do not quarrel on the way!” The Revival of Jacob
units.rightText: So he sent his brethren away, and they departed: and he said unto them, See that ye fall not out by the way.

units.leftText: So the brothers went up out of Egypt and came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan.
units.rightText: And they went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan unto Jacob their father.

units.leftText: “Joseph is still alive,” they said, “and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt!”
units.rightText: And they told him, saying, Joseph is yet alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt. And his heart fainted, for he believed them not.

units.leftText: However, when they relayed all that Joseph had told them, and when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him back, the spirit of their father Jacob was revived.
units.rightText: And they told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said unto them: and when he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob their father revived:

units.leftText: “Enough!” declared Israel. “My son Joseph is still alive! I will go to see him before I die.”
units.rightText: and Israel said, It is enough; Joseph my son is yet alive: I will go and see him before I die.

units.leftText: So Israel set out with all that he had, and when he came to Beersheba, he offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.
units.rightText: And Israel took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beer-sheba, and offered sacrifices unto the God of his father Isaac.

units.leftText: And that night God spoke to Israel in a vision: “Jacob, Jacob!” He said. “Here I am,” replied Jacob.
units.rightText: And God spake unto Israel in the visions of the night, and said, Jacob, Jacob. And he said, Here am I.

units.leftText: “I am God,” He said, “the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.
units.rightText: And he said, I am God, the God of thy father: fear not to go down into Egypt; for I will there make of thee a great nation:

units.leftText: I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will surely bring you back. And Joseph’s own hands will close your eyes.”
units.rightText: I will go down with thee into Egypt; and I will also surely bring thee up again: and Joseph shall put his hand upon thine eyes.

units.leftText: Then Jacob departed from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel took their father Jacob in the wagons Pharaoh had sent to carry him, along with their children and wives.
units.rightText: And Jacob rose up from Beer-sheba: and the sons of Israel carried Jacob their father, and their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.

units.leftText: They also took the livestock and possessions they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and Jacob and all his offspring went to Egypt. Those Who Went to Egypt (Exodus 1:1–7|EXO 1:1-7*)
units.rightText: And they took their cattle, and their goods, which they had gotten in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt, Jacob, and all his seed with him:

units.leftText: Jacob took with him to Egypt his sons and grandsons, and his daughters and granddaughters — all his offspring. The Children of Leah
units.rightText: his sons, and his sons’ sons with him, his daughters, and his sons’ daughters, and all his seed brought he with him into Egypt.

units.leftText: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel (Jacob and his descendants) who went to Egypt: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.
units.rightText: And these are the names of the children of Israel, who came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob’s first-born.

units.leftText: The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
units.rightText: And the sons of Reuben: Hanoch, and Pallu, and Hezron, and Carmi.

units.leftText: The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman.
units.rightText: And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman.
leftNotes: 46:10 Jemuel is another name for Nemuel; see Numbers 26:12|NUM 26:12*.
46:10 Zohar is a variant of Zerah; see Numbers 26:13|NUM 26:13* and 1 Chronicles 4:24.

units.leftText: The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
units.rightText: And the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

units.leftText: The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.
units.rightText: And the sons of Judah: Er, and Onan, and Shelah, and Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And the sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.

units.leftText: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Job, and Shimron.
units.rightText: And the sons of Issachar: Tola, and Puvah, and Iob, and Shimron.
leftNotes: 46:13 Hebrew; SP and Syriac Puah; see 1 Chronicles 7:1|1CH 7:1*.
46:13 Hebrew; SP and some LXX manuscripts Jashub; see Numbers 26:24|NUM 26:24* and 1 Chronicles 7:1.

units.leftText: The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
units.rightText: And the sons of Zebulun: Sered, and Elon, and Jahleel.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Leah born to Jacob in Paddan-aram, in addition to his daughter Dinah. The total number of sons and daughters was thirty-three. The Children of Zilpah
units.rightText: These are the sons of Leah, whom she bare unto Jacob in Paddan-aram, with his daughter Dinah: all the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty and three.
leftNotes: 46:15 That is, northwest Mesopotamia

units.leftText: The sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
units.rightText: And the sons of Gad: Ziphion, and Haggi, Shuni, and Ezbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli.
leftNotes: 46:16 SP and LXX Zephon; see also Numbers 26:15|NUM 26:15*.
46:16 Arodi is a variant of Arod; see Numbers 26:17|NUM 26:17*.

units.leftText: The children of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and their sister Serah. The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
units.rightText: And the sons of Asher: Imnah, and Ishvah, and Ishvi, and Beriah, and Serah their sister; and the sons of Beriah: Heber, and Malchiel.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Jacob born to Zilpah — whom Laban gave to his daughter Leah — sixteen in all. The Children of Rachel
units.rightText: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter; and these she bare unto Jacob, even sixteen souls.

units.leftText: The sons of Jacob’s wife Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
units.rightText: The sons of Rachel Jacob’s wife: Joseph and Benjamin.

units.leftText: Manasseh and Ephraim were born to Joseph in the land of Egypt by Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.
units.rightText: And unto Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Poti-phera priest of On, bare unto him.
leftNotes: 46:20 That is, Heliopolis, as in LXX

units.leftText: The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
units.rightText: And the sons of Benjamin: Bela, and Becher, and Ashbel, Gera, and Naaman, Ehi, and Rosh, Muppim, and Huppim, and Ard.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Rachel born to Jacob — fourteen in all. The Children of Bilhah
units.rightText: These are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob: all the souls were fourteen.

units.leftText: The son of Dan: Hushim.
units.rightText: And the sons of Dan: Hushim.

units.leftText: The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
units.rightText: And the sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shillem.

units.leftText: These are the sons of Jacob born to Bilhah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Rachel — seven in all.
units.rightText: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave unto Rachel his daughter, and these she bare unto Jacob: all the souls were seven.

units.leftText: All those belonging to Jacob who came to Egypt— his direct descendants, besides the wives of Jacob’s sons— numbered sixty-six persons.
units.rightText: All the souls that came with Jacob into Egypt, that came out of his loins, besides Jacob’s sons’ wives, all the souls were threescore and six;

units.leftText: And with the two sons who had been born to Joseph in Egypt, the members of Jacob’s family who went to Egypt were seventy in all. Jacob Arrives in Egypt
units.rightText: and the sons of Joseph, who were born to him in Egypt, were two souls: all the souls of the house of Jacob, that came into Egypt, were threescore and ten.
leftNotes: 46:27 Hebrew; LXX the nine sons, probably including Joseph’s grandsons through Ephraim and Manasseh; see 1 Chronicles 7:14–29|1CH 7:14-29*.
46:27 Hebrew (see also Exodus 1:5|EXO 1:5*); LXX (see also Acts 7:14) seventy-five

units.leftText: Now Jacob had sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph to get directions to Goshen. When Jacob’s family arrived in the land of Goshen,
units.rightText: And he sent Judah before him unto Joseph, to show the way before him unto Goshen; and they came into the land of Goshen.

units.leftText: Joseph prepared his chariot and went there to meet his father Israel. Joseph presented himself to him, embraced him, and wept profusely.
units.rightText: And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Israel his father, to Goshen; and he presented himself unto him, and fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.

units.leftText: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Finally I can die, now that I have seen your face and know that you are still alive!”
units.rightText: And Israel said unto Joseph, Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, that thou art yet alive.

units.leftText: Joseph said to his brothers and to his father’s household, “I will go up and inform Pharaoh: ‘My brothers and my father’s household from the land of Canaan have come to me.
units.rightText: And Joseph said unto his brethren, and unto his father’s house, I will go up, and tell Pharaoh, and will say unto him, My brethren, and my father’s house, who were in the land of Canaan, are come unto me;

units.leftText: The men are shepherds; they raise livestock, and they have brought their flocks and herds and all that they own.’
units.rightText: and the men are shepherds, for they have been keepers of cattle; and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.

units.leftText: When Pharaoh summons you and asks, ‘What is your occupation?’
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass, when Pharaoh shall call you, and shall say, What is your occupation?

units.leftText: you are to say, ‘Your servants have raised livestock ever since our youth — both we and our fathers.’ Then you will be allowed to settle in the land of Goshen, since all shepherds are detestable to the Egyptians.”
units.rightText: that ye shall say, Thy servants have been keepers of cattle from our youth even until now, both we, and our fathers: that ye may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians.

units.leftText: So Joseph went and told Pharaoh: “My father and my brothers, with their flocks and herds and all they own, have come from the land of Canaan and are now in Goshen.”
units.rightText: Then Joseph went in and told Pharaoh, and said, My father and my brethren, and their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have, are come out of the land of Canaan; and, behold, they are in the land of Goshen.

units.leftText: And he chose five of his brothers and presented them before Pharaoh.
units.rightText: And from among his brethren he took five men, and presented them unto Pharaoh.

units.leftText: “What is your occupation?” Pharaoh asked Joseph’s brothers. “Your servants are shepherds,” they replied, “both we and our fathers.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh said unto his brethren, What is your occupation? And they said unto Pharaoh, Thy servants are shepherds, both we, and our fathers.

units.leftText: Then they said to Pharaoh, “We have come to live in the land for a time, because there is no pasture for the flocks of your servants, since the famine in the land of Canaan has been severe. So now, please allow your servants to settle in the land of Goshen.”
units.rightText: And they said unto Pharaoh, To sojourn in the land are we come; for there is no pasture for thy servants’ flocks; for the famine is sore in the land of Canaan: now therefore, we pray thee, let thy servants dwell in the land of Goshen.

units.leftText: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Now that your father and brothers have come to you,
units.rightText: And Pharaoh spake unto Joseph, saying, Thy father and thy brethren are come unto thee:

units.leftText: the land of Egypt is before you; settle your father and brothers in the best part of the land. They may dwell in the land of Goshen. And if you know of any talented men among them, put them in charge of my own livestock.”
units.rightText: the land of Egypt is before thee; in the best of the land make thy father and thy brethren to dwell; in the land of Goshen let them dwell: and if thou knowest any able men among them, then make them rulers over my cattle.

units.leftText: Then Joseph brought in his father Jacob and presented him before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
units.rightText: And Joseph brought in Jacob his father, and set him before Pharaoh: and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.

units.leftText: “How many years have you lived?” Pharaoh asked.
units.rightText: And Pharaoh said unto Jacob, How many are the days of the years of thy life?

units.leftText: “My travels have lasted 130 years,” Jacob replied. “My years have been few and hard, and they have not matched the years of the travels of my fathers.”
units.rightText: And Jacob said unto Pharaoh, The days of the years of my pilgrimage are a hundred and thirty years: few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not attained unto the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.
leftNotes: 47:9 Hebrew sojourns; twice in this verse

units.leftText: Then Jacob blessed Pharaoh and departed from his presence.
units.rightText: And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from the presence of Pharaoh.

units.leftText: So Joseph settled his father and brothers in the land of Egypt and gave them property in the best part of the land, the district of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
units.rightText: And Joseph placed his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.

units.leftText: Joseph also provided his father and brothers and all his father’s household with food for their families. The Famine Continues
units.rightText: And Joseph nourished his father, and his brethren, and all his father’s household, with bread, according to their families.

units.leftText: There was no food, however, in all that region, because the famine was so severe; the lands of Egypt and Canaan had been exhausted by the famine.
units.rightText: And there was no bread in all the land; for the famine was very sore, so that the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan fainted by reason of the famine.

units.leftText: Joseph collected all the money to be found in the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan in exchange for the grain they were buying, and he brought it into Pharaoh’s palace.
units.rightText: And Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the grain which they bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh’s house.

units.leftText: When the money from the lands of Egypt and Canaan was gone, all the Egyptians came to Joseph and said, “Give us food. Why should we die before your eyes? For our funds have run out!”
units.rightText: And when the money was all spent in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came unto Joseph, and said, Give us bread: for why should we die in thy presence? for our money faileth.

units.leftText: “Then bring me your livestock,” said Joseph. “Since the money is gone, I will sell you food in exchange for your livestock.”
units.rightText: And Joseph said, Give your cattle; and I will give you for your cattle, if money fail.

units.leftText: So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and he gave them food in exchange for their horses, their flocks and herds, and their donkeys. Throughout that year he provided them with food in exchange for all their livestock.
units.rightText: And they brought their cattle unto Joseph; and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses, and for the flocks, and for the herds, and for the asses: and he fed them with bread in exchange for all their cattle for that year.

units.leftText: When that year was over, they came to him the second year and said, “We cannot hide from our lord that our money is gone and all our livestock belongs to you. There is nothing left for our lord except our bodies and our land.
units.rightText: And when that year was ended, they came unto him the second year, and said unto him, We will not hide from my lord, how that our money is all spent; and the herds of cattle are my lord’s; there is nought left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands:

units.leftText: Why should we perish before your eyes— we and our land as well? Purchase us and our land in exchange for food. Then we, along with our land, will be slaves to Pharaoh. Give us seed that we may live and not die, and that the land may not become desolate.”
units.rightText: wherefore should we die before thine eyes, both we and our land? buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants unto Pharaoh: and give us seed, that we may live, and not die, and that the land be not desolate.

units.leftText: So Joseph acquired for Pharaoh all the land in Egypt; the Egyptians, one and all, sold their fields because the famine was so severe upon them. The land became Pharaoh’s,
units.rightText: So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh; for the Egyptians sold every man his field, because the famine was sore upon them: and the land became Pharaoh’s.

units.leftText: and Joseph reduced the people to servitude from one end of Egypt to the other.
units.rightText: And as for the people, he removed them to the cities from one end of the border of Egypt even to the other end thereof.
leftNotes: 47:21 SP, LXX, Vulgate; Hebrew removed the people to the cities

units.leftText: However, he did not acquire the priests’ portion of the land, for it had been given to them by Pharaoh. They ate the rations that Pharaoh supplied; so they did not sell their land.
units.rightText: Only the land of the priests bought he not: for the priests had a portion from Pharaoh, and did eat their portion which Pharaoh gave them; wherefore they sold not their land.

units.leftText: Then Joseph said to the people, “Now that I have acquired you and your land for Pharaoh this day, here is seed for you to sow in the land.
units.rightText: Then Joseph said unto the people, Behold, I have bought you this day and your land for Pharaoh: lo, here is seed for you, and ye shall sow the land.

units.leftText: At harvest time, you are to give a fifth of it to Pharaoh, and four-fifths will be yours as seed for the field and food for yourselves and your households and children.”
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass at the ingatherings, that ye shall give a fifth unto Pharaoh, and four parts shall be your own, for seed of the field, and for your food, and for them of your households, and for food for your little ones.

units.leftText: “You have saved our lives,” they said. “We have found favor in our lord’s eyes, and we will be Pharaoh’s servants.”
units.rightText: And they said, Thou hast saved our lives: let us find favor in the sight of my lord, and we will be Pharaoh’s servants.

units.leftText: So Joseph established a law that a fifth of the produce belongs to Pharaoh, and it is in effect in the land of Egypt to this day. Only the priests’ land does not belong to Pharaoh. The Israelites Prosper in Goshen
units.rightText: And Joseph made it a statute concerning the land of Egypt unto this day, that Pharaoh should have the fifth; only the land of the priests alone became not Pharaoh’s.

units.leftText: Now the Israelites settled in the land of Egypt, in the region of Goshen. They acquired property there and became fruitful and increased greatly in number.
units.rightText: And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; and they gat them possessions therein, and were fruitful, and multiplied exceedingly.

units.leftText: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and the length of his life was 147 years.
units.rightText: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years: so the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred forty and seven years.

units.leftText: When the time drew near for Israel to die, he called his son Joseph and said to him, “If I have found favor in your eyes, put your hand under my thigh and promise to show me kindness and faithfulness. Do not bury me in Egypt,
units.rightText: And the time drew near that Israel must die: and he called his son Joseph, and said unto him, If now I have found favor in thy sight, put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly with me: bury me not, I pray thee, in Egypt;

units.leftText: but when I lie down with my fathers, carry me out of Egypt and bury me with them.” Joseph answered, “I will do as you have requested.”
units.rightText: but when I sleep with my fathers, thou shalt carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their burying-place. And he said, I will do as thou hast said.

units.leftText: “Swear to me,” Jacob said. So Joseph swore to him, and Israel bowed in worship at the head of his bed.
units.rightText: And he said, Swear unto me: and he sware unto him. And Israel bowed himself upon the bed’s head.
leftNotes: 47:31 Hebrew; LXX Israel worshiped as he leaned on the top of his staff; see Hebrews 11:21|HEB 11:21*.

units.leftText: Some time later Joseph was told, “Your father is ill.” So he set out with his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
units.rightText: And it came to pass after these things, that one said to Joseph, Behold, thy father is sick: and he took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.

units.leftText: When Jacob was told, “Your son Joseph has come to you,” Israel rallied his strength and sat up in bed.
units.rightText: And one told Jacob, and said, Behold, thy son Joseph cometh unto thee: and Israel strengthened himself, and sat upon the bed.

units.leftText: Jacob said to Joseph, “God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and there He blessed me
units.rightText: And Jacob said unto Joseph, God Almighty appeared unto me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,
leftNotes: 48:3 Hebrew El-Shaddai

units.leftText: and told me, ‘Behold, I will make you fruitful and multiply you; I will make you a multitude of peoples, and will give this land to your descendants after you as an everlasting possession.’
units.rightText: and said unto me, Behold, I will make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, and I will make of thee a company of peoples, and will give this land to thy seed after thee for an everlasting possession.

units.leftText: And now your two sons born to you in Egypt before I came to you here shall be reckoned as mine; Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
units.rightText: And now thy two sons, who were born unto thee in the land of Egypt before I came unto thee into Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh, even as Reuben and Simeon, shall be mine.

units.leftText: Any children born to you after them shall be yours, and they shall be called by the names of their brothers in the territory they inherit.
units.rightText: And thy issue, that thou begettest after them, shall be thine; they shall be called after the name of their brethren in their inheritance.

units.leftText: Now as for me, when I was returning from Paddan, to my sorrow Rachel died along the way in the land of Canaan, some distance from Ephrath. So I buried her there beside the road to Ephrath” (that is, Bethlehem).
units.rightText: And as for me, when I came from Paddan, Rachel died by me in the land of Canaan in the way, when there was still some distance to come unto Ephrath: and I buried her there in the way to Ephrath (the same is Beth-lehem).
leftNotes: 48:7 That is, northwest Mesopotamia

units.leftText: When Israel saw the sons of Joseph, he asked, “Who are these?”
units.rightText: And Israel beheld Joseph’s sons, and said, Who are these?

units.leftText: Joseph said to his father, “They are the sons God has given me in this place.” So Jacob said, “Please bring them to me, that I may bless them.”
units.rightText: And Joseph said unto his father, They are my sons, whom God hath given me here. And he said, Bring them, I pray thee, unto me, and I will bless them.

units.leftText: Now Israel’s eyesight was poor because of old age; he could hardly see. Joseph brought his sons to him, and his father kissed them and embraced them.
units.rightText: Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he could not see. And he brought them near unto him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.

units.leftText: “I never expected to see your face again,” Israel said to Joseph, “but now God has let me see your children as well.”
units.rightText: And Israel said unto Joseph, I had not thought to see thy face: and, lo, God hath let me see thy seed also.

units.leftText: Then Joseph removed his sons from his father’s knees and bowed facedown.
units.rightText: And Joseph brought them out from between his knees; and he bowed himself with his face to the earth.

units.leftText: And Joseph took both of them— with Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel’s right hand— and brought them close to him.
units.rightText: And Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel’s right hand, and brought them near unto him.

units.leftText: But Israel stretched out his right hand and put it on the head of Ephraim, the younger; and crossing his hands, he put his left on Manasseh’s head, although Manasseh was the firstborn.
units.rightText: And Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it upon Ephraim’s head, who was the younger, and his left hand upon Manasseh’s head, guiding his hands wittingly; for Manasseh was the first-born.

units.leftText: Then he blessed Joseph and said: “May the God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has been my shepherd all my life to this day,
units.rightText: And he blessed Joseph, and said, The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God who hath fed me all my life long unto this day,

units.leftText: the angel who has redeemed me from all harm— may He bless these boys. And may they be called by my name and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and may they grow into a multitude upon the earth.”
units.rightText: the angel who hath redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth.
leftNotes: 48:16 Or Angel

units.leftText: When Joseph saw that his father had placed his right hand on Ephraim’s head, he was displeased and took his father’s hand to move it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s.
units.rightText: And when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it displeased him: and he held up his father’s hand, to remove it from Ephraim’s head unto Manasseh’s head.

units.leftText: “Not so, my father!” Joseph said. “This one is the firstborn; put your right hand on his head.”
units.rightText: And Joseph said unto his father, Not so, my father; for this is the first-born; put thy right hand upon his head.

units.leftText: But his father refused. “I know, my son, I know!” he said. “He too shall become a people, and he too shall be great; nevertheless, his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his offspring shall become a multitude of nations.”
units.rightText: And his father refused, and said, I know it, my son, I know it; he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great: howbeit his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations.

units.leftText: So that day Jacob blessed them and said: “By you shall Israel pronounce this blessing: ‘May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.’” So he put Ephraim before Manasseh.
units.rightText: And he blessed them that day, saying, In thee will Israel bless, saying, God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh: and he set Ephraim before Manasseh.

units.leftText: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Look, I am about to die, but God will be with you and bring you back to the land of your fathers.
units.rightText: And Israel said unto Joseph, Behold, I die: but God will be with you, and bring you again unto the land of your fathers.

units.leftText: And to you, as one who is above your brothers, I give the ridge of land that I took from the Amorites with my sword and bow.”
units.rightText: Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.
leftNotes: 48:22 Or one portion of the land; Hebrew shekem, which sounds like the town and district called Shechem

units.leftText: Then Jacob called for his sons and said, “Gather around so that I can tell you what will happen to you in the days to come:
units.rightText: And Jacob called unto his sons, and said: Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the latter days.

units.leftText: Come together and listen, O sons of Jacob; listen to your father Israel.
units.rightText: Assemble yourselves, and hear, ye sons of Jacob; And hearken unto Israel your father.

units.leftText: Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, excelling in honor, excelling in power.
units.rightText: Reuben, thou art my first-born, my might, and the beginning of my strength; The pre-eminence of dignity, and the pre-eminence of power.

units.leftText: Uncontrolled as the waters, you will no longer excel, because you went up to your father’s bed, onto my couch, and defiled it.
units.rightText: Boiling over as water, thou shalt not have the pre-eminence; Because thou wentest up to thy father’s bed; Then defiledst thou it: he went up to my couch.

units.leftText: Simeon and Levi are brothers; their swords are weapons of violence.
units.rightText: Simeon and Levi are brethren; Weapons of violence are their swords.
leftNotes: 49:5 Or dwelling places

units.leftText: May I never enter their council; may I never join their assembly. For they kill men in their anger, and hamstring oxen on a whim.
units.rightText: O my soul, come not thou into their council; Unto their assembly, my glory, be not thou united; For in their anger they slew a man, And in their self-will they hocked an ox.

units.leftText: Cursed be their anger, for it is strong, and their wrath, for it is cruel! I will disperse them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.
units.rightText: Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; And their wrath, for it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, And scatter them in Israel.

units.leftText: Judah, your brothers shall praise you. Your hand shall be on the necks of your enemies; your father’s sons shall bow down to you.
units.rightText: Judah, thee shall thy brethren praise: Thy hand shall be on the neck of thine enemies; Thy father’s sons shall bow down before thee.
leftNotes: 49:8 Judah sounds like the Hebrew for praise.

units.leftText: Judah is a young lion— my son, you return from the prey. Like a lion he crouches and lies down; like a lioness, who dares to rouse him?
units.rightText: Judah is a lion’s whelp; From the prey, my son, thou art gone up: He stooped down, he couched as a lion, And as a lioness; who shall rouse him up?

units.leftText: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and the allegiance of the nations is his.
units.rightText: The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, Nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet, Until Shiloh come; And unto him shall the obedience of the peoples be.
leftNotes: 49:10 Or from his descendants
49:10 Or until the one to whom tribute belongs

units.leftText: He ties his donkey to the vine, his colt to the choicest branch. He washes his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.
units.rightText: Binding his foal unto the vine, And his ass’s colt unto the choice vine; He hath washed his garments in wine, And his vesture in the blood of grapes:

units.leftText: His eyes are darker than wine, and his teeth are whiter than milk.
units.rightText: His eyes shall be red with wine, And his teeth white with milk.

units.leftText: Zebulun shall dwell by the seashore and become a harbor for ships; his border shall extend to Sidon.
units.rightText: Zebulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea; And he shall be for a haven of ships; And his border shall be upon Sidon.

units.leftText: Issachar is a strong donkey, lying down between the sheepfolds.
units.rightText: Issachar is a strong ass, Couching down between the sheepfolds:
leftNotes: 49:14 Or saddlebags or hearths

units.leftText: He saw that his resting place was good and that his land was pleasant, so he bent his shoulder to the burden and submitted to labor as a servant.
units.rightText: And he saw a resting-place that it was good, And the land that it was pleasant; And he bowed his shoulder to bear, And became a servant under taskwork.

units.leftText: Dan shall provide justice for his people as one of the tribes of Israel.
units.rightText: Dan shall judge his people, As one of the tribes of Israel.
leftNotes: 49:16 Or Dan shall judge his people; Dan means He has judged or He has vindicated.

units.leftText: He will be a snake by the road, a viper in the path that bites the horse’s heels so that its rider tumbles backward.
units.rightText: Dan shall be a serpent in the way, An adder in the path, That biteth the horse’s heels, So that his rider falleth backward.

units.leftText: I await Your salvation, O LORD.
units.rightText: I have waited for thy salvation, O Jehovah.

units.leftText: Gad will be attacked by raiders, but he will attack their heels.
units.rightText: Gad, a troop shall press upon him; But he shall press upon their heel.
leftNotes: 49:19 Gad sounds like the Hebrew for raid and also for band of raiders.

units.leftText: Asher’s food will be rich; he shall provide royal delicacies.
units.rightText: Out of Asher his bread shall be fat, And he shall yield royal dainties.

units.leftText: Naphtali is a doe set free that bears beautiful fawns.
units.rightText: Naphtali is a hind let loose: He giveth goodly words.
leftNotes: 49:21 Or gives beautiful words or bears fawns of the fold

units.leftText: Joseph is a fruitful vine— a fruitful vine by a spring, whose branches scale the wall.
units.rightText: Joseph is a fruitful bough, A fruitful bough by a fountain; His branches run over the wall.
leftNotes: 49:22 Or Joseph is a wild donkey, a wild donkey by a spring, with his wild colts beside the wall

units.leftText: The archers attacked him with bitterness; they aimed at him in hostility.
units.rightText: The archers have sorely grieved him, And shot at him, and persecuted him:

units.leftText: Yet he steadied his bow, and his strong arms were tempered by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, in the name of the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel,
units.rightText: But his bow abode in strength, And the arms of his hands were made strong, By the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob (From thence is the shepherd, the stone of Israel),

units.leftText: by the God of your father who helps you, and by the Almighty who blesses you, with blessings of the heavens above, with blessings of the depths below, with blessings of the breasts and womb.
units.rightText: Even by the God of thy father, who shall help thee, And by the Almighty, who shall bless thee, With blessings of heaven above, Blessings of the deep that coucheth beneath, Blessings of the breasts, and of the womb.
leftNotes: 49:25 Hebrew Shaddai

units.leftText: The blessings of your father have surpassed the blessings of the ancient mountains and the bounty of the everlasting hills. May they rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the prince of his brothers.
units.rightText: The blessings of thy father Have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors Unto the utmost bound of the everlasting hills: They shall be on the head of Joseph, And on the crown of the head of him that was separate from his brethren.
leftNotes: 49:26 Or of my ancestors

units.leftText: Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours the prey, in the evening he divides the plunder.”
units.rightText: Benjamin is a wolf that raveneth: In the morning he shall devour the prey, And at even he shall divide the spoil.

units.leftText: These are the tribes of Israel, twelve in all, and this was what their father said to them. He blessed them, and he blessed each one with a suitable blessing. The Death of Jacob
units.rightText: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel: and this is it that their father spake unto them and blessed them; every one according to his blessing he blessed them.

units.leftText: Then Jacob instructed them, “I am about to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite.
units.rightText: And he charged them, and said unto them, I am to be gathered unto my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,

units.leftText: The cave is in the field of Machpelah near Mamre, in the land of Canaan. This is the field Abraham purchased from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site.
units.rightText: in the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is before Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field from Ephron the Hittite for a possession of a burying-place.

units.leftText: There Abraham and his wife Sarah are buried, there Isaac and his wife Rebekah are buried, and there I buried Leah.
units.rightText: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah—

units.leftText: The field and the cave that is in it were purchased from the Hittites.”
units.rightText: the field and the cave that is therein, which was purchased from the children of Heth.

units.leftText: When Jacob had finished instructing his sons, he pulled his feet into the bed and breathed his last, and he was gathered to his people.
units.rightText: And when Jacob made an end of charging his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the ghost, and was gathered unto his people.

units.leftText: Then Joseph fell upon his father’s face, wept over him, and kissed him.
units.rightText: And Joseph fell upon his father’s face, and wept upon him, and kissed him.

units.leftText: And Joseph directed the physicians in his service to embalm his father Israel. So they embalmed him,
units.rightText: And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father: and the physicians embalmed Israel.

units.leftText: taking the forty days required to complete the embalming. And the Egyptians mourned for him seventy days.
units.rightText: And forty days were fulfilled for him; for so are fulfilled the days of embalming: and the Egyptians wept for him threescore and ten days.

units.leftText: When the days of mourning had passed, Joseph said to Pharaoh’s court, “If I have found favor in your eyes, please tell Pharaoh that
units.rightText: And when the days of weeping for him were past, Joseph spake unto the house of Pharaoh, saying, If now I have found favor in your eyes, speak, I pray you, in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,

units.leftText: my father made me swear an oath when he said, ‘I am about to die. You must bury me in the tomb that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan.’ Now let me go and bury my father, and then return.”
units.rightText: My father made me swear, saying, Lo, I die: in my grave which I have digged for me in the land of Canaan, there shalt thou bury me. Now therefore let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father, and I will come again.

units.leftText: Pharaoh replied, “Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear to do.”
units.rightText: And Pharaoh said, Go up, and bury thy father, according as he made thee swear.

units.leftText: Then Joseph went to bury his father, and all the servants of Pharaoh accompanied him — the elders of Pharaoh’s household and all the elders of the land of Egypt —
units.rightText: And Joseph went up to bury his father; and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,

units.leftText: along with all of Joseph’s household, and his brothers, and his father’s household. Only their children and flocks and herds were left in Goshen.
units.rightText: and all the house of Joseph, and his brethren, and his father’s house: only their little ones, and their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen.

units.leftText: Chariots and horsemen alike went up with him, and it was an exceedingly large procession.
units.rightText: And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen: and it was a very great company.

units.leftText: When they reached the threshing floor of Atad, which is across the Jordan, they lamented and wailed loudly, and Joseph mourned for his father seven days.
units.rightText: And they came to the threshing-floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and there they lamented with a very great and sore lamentation: and he made a mourning for his father seven days.

units.leftText: When the Canaanites of the land saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, “This is a solemn ceremony of mourning by the Egyptians.” Thus the place across the Jordan is called Abel-mizraim.
units.rightText: And when the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, This is a grievous mourning to the Egyptians: wherefore the name of it was called Abel-mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan.
leftNotes: 50:11 Abel-mizraim means mourning of the Egyptians.

units.leftText: So Jacob’s sons did as he had charged them.
units.rightText: And his sons did unto him according as he commanded them:

units.leftText: They carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave at Machpelah in the field near Mamre, which Abraham had purchased from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site.
units.rightText: for his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field, for a possession of a burying-place, of Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.

units.leftText: After Joseph had buried his father, he returned to Egypt with his brothers and all who had gone with him to bury his father. Joseph Comforts His Brothers
units.rightText: And Joseph returned into Egypt, he, and his brethren, and all that went up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.

units.leftText: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, “What if Joseph bears a grudge? Then he will surely repay us for all the evil that we did to him.”
units.rightText: And when Joseph’s brethren saw that their father was dead, they said, It may be that Joseph will hate us, and will fully requite us all the evil which we did unto him.

units.leftText: So they sent word to Joseph, saying, “Before he died, your father commanded,
units.rightText: And they sent a message unto Joseph, saying, Thy father did command before he died, saying,

units.leftText: ‘This is what you are to say to Joseph: I beg you, please forgive the transgression and sin of your brothers, for they did you wrong.’ So now, Joseph, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father.”
units.rightText: So shall ye say unto Joseph, Forgive, I pray thee now, the transgression of thy brethren, and their sin, for that they did unto thee evil. And now, we pray thee, forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of thy father. And Joseph wept when they spake unto him.

units.leftText: His brothers also came to him, bowed down before him, and said, “We are your slaves!”
units.rightText: And his brethren also went and fell down before his face; and they said, Behold, we are thy servants.

units.leftText: But Joseph replied, “Do not be afraid. Am I in the place of God?
units.rightText: And Joseph said unto them, Fear not: for am I in the place of God?

units.leftText: As for you, what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good, in order to accomplish a day like this— to preserve the lives of many people.
units.rightText: And as for you, ye meant evil against me; but God meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

units.leftText: Therefore do not be afraid. I will provide for you and your little ones.” So Joseph reassured his brothers and spoke kindly to them. The Death of Joseph
units.rightText: Now therefore fear ye not: I will nourish you, and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spake kindly unto them.

units.leftText: Now Joseph and his father’s household remained in Egypt, and Joseph lived to the age of 110.
units.rightText: And Joseph dwelt in Egypt, he, and his father’s house: and Joseph lived a hundred and ten years.

units.leftText: He saw Ephraim’s sons to the third generation, and indeed the sons of Machir son of Manasseh were brought up on Joseph’s knees.
units.rightText: And Joseph saw Ephraim’s children of the third generation: the children also of Machir the son of Manasseh were born upon Joseph’s knees.
leftNotes: 50:23 Or born or placed at birth

units.leftText: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “I am about to die, but God will surely visit you and bring you up from this land to the land He promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
units.rightText: And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die; but God will surely visit you, and bring you up out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

units.leftText: And Joseph made the sons of Israel take an oath and said, “God will surely attend to you, and then you must carry my bones up from this place.”
units.rightText: And Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.

units.leftText: So Joseph died at the age of 110. And they embalmed his body and placed it in a coffin in Egypt.
units.rightText: So Joseph died, being a hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.
